subCommands.description: This determines whether or not the rocket will generate a smoke trail appearance. By default, liquid-propellant rockets do not produce a smoke trail, but solid-propellant rockets do produce a smoke trail.

subCommands.name: jet_engine_type
subCommands.description: Definitions for each type of jet engine are performed within the jet_engine_type block. Since the definition is for a ‘type’ of engine and not an ‘instance’ of an engine, no installation position/attitude data is included. Typically, the fuel_feed is specified at the instance-level rather than at the type-level.

subCommands.name: tsfc_idle_pph
subCommands.description: This specifies the thrust specific fuel consumption at idle in lbs-thrust/lbs-fuel/hr.

subCommands.name: tsfc_mil_pph
subCommands.description: This specifies the thrust specific fuel consumption at military power (full power without afterburner) in lbs-thrust/lbs-fuel/hr.

subCommands.name: tsfc_ab_pph
subCommands.description: This specifies the thrust specific fuel consumption using full afterburner in lbs-thrust/lbs-fuel/hr.

subCommands.name: rated_thrust_idle
subCommands.description: This specifies the thrust at idle. Since thrust varies with various conditions, this is a reference value.

subCommands.name: rated_thrust_mil
subCommands.description: This specifies the thrust at military power (full power without afterburner). Since thrust varies with various conditions, this is a reference value.

subCommands.name: rated_thrust_ab
subCommands.description: This specifies the thrust using full afterburner. Since thrust varies with various conditions, this is a reference value.

subCommands.name: thrust_table_idle
subCommands.description: This is a simple table of idle thrust versus altitude. Note that is does not consider Mach-effects. The thrust_idle_mach_alt_table or thrust_idle_alt_mach_table are preferable, but if no Mach data is available, this table can be used.

subCommands.name: thrust_idle_mach_alt_table
subCommands.description: This is an improved table over thrust_table_idle, since it includes Mach-effects. However, most users will prefer the format of the thrust_idle_alt_mach_table instead.

subCommands.name: thrust_idle_alt_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is typically the best thrust table format – it includes Mach-effects and organizes its data in a preferred manner. The thrust_idle_mach_alt_table is an alternative format.

subCommands.name: thrust_table_mil
subCommands.description: This is a simple table of military (MIL) thrust versus altitude. Note that is does not consider Mach-effects. The thrust_mil_mach_alt_table or thrust_mil_alt_mach_table are preferable, but if no Mach data is available, this table can be used.

subCommands.name: thrust_mil_mach_alt_table
subCommands.description: This is an improved table over thrust_table_mil, since it includes Mach-effects. However, most users will prefer the format of the thrust_mil_alt_mach_table instead.

subCommands.name: thrust_mil_alt_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is typically the best thrust table format – it includes Mach-effects and organizes its data in a preferred manner. The thrust_mil_mach_alt_table is an alternative format.

subCommands.name: thrust_table_ab
subCommands.description: This is a simple table of afterburner (AB) thrust versus altitude. Note that is does not consider Mach-effects. The thrust_ab_mach_alt_table or thrust_ab_alt_mach_table are preferable, but if no Mach data is available, this table can be used.

subCommands.name: thrust_ab_mach_alt_table
subCommands.description: This is an improved table over thrust_table_ab, since it includes Mach-effects. However, most users will prefer the format of the thrust_ab_alt_mach_table instead.

subCommands.name: thrust_ab_alt_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is typically the best thrust table format – it includes Mach-effects and organizes its data in a preferred manner. The thrust_ab_mach_alt_table is an alternative format.

subCommands.name: spin_up_mil_per_sec
subCommands.description: This defines how quickly the engine will “spool-up” as the power level is advanced. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-up from idle to MIL power in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-up from idle to MIL power.

subCommands.name: spin_up_table_mil_per_sec
subCommands.description: This defines how quickly the engine will “spool-up” as the power level is advanced. Rather than a single value, this command uses a table that is a function of the throttle level (normalized), allowing a more realistic spin-up as a function of current power condition. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-up from idle to MIL power in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-up from idle to MIL power.

subCommands.name: spin_up_ab_per_sec
subCommands.description: This defines how quickly the engine will “spool-up” as the power level is advanced. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-up from MIL to Full AB power in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-up from MIL to Full AB power.

subCommands.name: spin_up_table_ab_per_sec
subCommands.description: This defines how quickly the engine will “spool-up” as the power level is advanced. Rather than a single value, this command uses a table that is a function of the throttle level (normalized), allowing a more realistic spin-up as a function of current power condition. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-up from MIL to Full AB power in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-up from MIL to Full AB power.

subCommands.name: spin_down_mil_per_sec
subCommands.description: This defines how quickly the engine will “spool-down” as the power level is reduced. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-down from MIL power to idle in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-down from MIL power to idle.

subCommands.name: spin_down_table_mil_per_sec
subCommands.description: This defines how quickly the engine will “spool-down” as the power level is reduced. Rather than a single value, this command uses a table that is a function of the throttle level (normalized), allowing a more realistic spin-down as a function of current power condition. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-down from MIL power to idle in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-down from MIL power to idle.

subCommands.name: spin_down_ab_per_sec
subCommands.description: This defines how quickly the engine will “spool-down” as the power level is reduced. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-down from Full AB power to MIL power in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-down from Full AB power to MIL power.

subCommands.name: spin_down_table_ab_per_sec
subCommands.description: This defines how quickly the engine will “spool-down” as the power level is reduced. Rather than a single value, this command uses a table that is a function of the throttle level (normalized), allowing a more realistic spin-down as a function of current power condition. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-down from Full AB power to MIL power in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-down from Full AB power to MIL power.

subCommands.name: throttle_setting_mil
subCommands.description: This specifies the control_value defined in flight_controls that will be used to control the MIL (military) power throttle setting. This can be done at the engine-level or in the propulsion_data of the p6dof_object_type.

subCommands.name: throttle_setting_ab
subCommands.description: This specifies the control_value defined in flight_controls that will be used to control the AB (afterburner) power throttle setting. This can be done at the engine-level or in the propulsion_data of the p6dof_object_type.

subCommands.name: throttle_setting_reverser
subCommands.description: This specifies the control_value defined in flight_controls that will be used to control the thrust-reverser control setting. This can be done at the engine-level or in the propulsion_data of the p6dof_object_type.

subCommands.name: throttle_setting_yaw
subCommands.description: This specifies the control_value defined in flight_controls that will be used to control the yaw thrust vectoring control setting. This can be done at the engine-level or in the propulsion_data of the p6dof_object_type.

subCommands.name: throttle_setting_pitch
subCommands.description: This specifies the control_value defined in flight_controls that will be used to control the pitch thrust vectoring control setting. This can be done at the engine-level or in the propulsion_data of the p6dof_object_type.

subCommands.name: thrust_offset
subCommands.description: This is the location of the thrust relative to the engine’s reference point along the x-axis. A positive value is forward of the engine, negative is aft.

subCommands.name: inop_ref_area
subCommands.description: This specifies aerodynamic CD-area product for the engine when it is inoperative. It is the drag coefficient multiplied by the reference area.

subCommands.name: fuel_feed
subCommands.description: This specifies the name of the fuel_tank from which the engine will draw fuel. This is typically specified for a jet_engine_type instance rather than in the type definition.

subCommands.name: engine_smokes_above_power_setting
subCommands.description: This specifies the throttle level (MIL power) above which the engine will produce smoke. For example, a value of 0.8 will produce smoke when the throttle is above 80% power. If afterburner is selected, the smoke will cease. The default is a value of 1.0, which will not produce any smoke. This is useful for simulating engines that produce excessive smoke, such as old F-4 Phantoms and MiG-29s.

subCommands.name: ramjet_engine_type
subCommands.description: Definitions for each type of ramjet engine are performed within the ramjet_engine_type block. Since the definition is for a ‘type’ of engine and not an ‘instance’ of an engine, no installation position/attitude data is included. Typically, the fuel_feed is specified at the instance-level rather than at the type-level.

subCommands.name: tsfc_alt_mach_table
subCommands.description: This specifies the thrust specific fuel consumption as a function of altitude and Mach in lbs-thrust/lbs-fuel/hr. Altitude units are feet.

subCommands.name: thrust_alt_mach_table
subCommands.description: This specifies the thrust as a function of altitude and Mach in lbs. Altitude units are feet. Since the table will clamp rather than interpolate at the end values, it is important to ensure that data at the extreme points goes to zero values. Failure to do so could result in increasing thrust at high Mach, for example.

subCommands.description: This specifies the control_value defined in flight_controls that will be used to control the yaw thrust vectoring control setting. This can be done at the engine-level or in the propulsion_data of the p6dof_object_type.

subCommands.name: throttle_setting_pitch
subCommands.description: This specifies the control_value defined in flight_controls that will be used to control the pitch thrust vectoring control setting. This can be done at the engine-level or in the propulsion_data of the p6dof_object_type.

subCommands.description: This specifies aerodynamic CD-area product for the engine when it is inoperative. It is the drag coefficient multiplied by the reference area.

subCommands.name: fuel_feed
subCommands.description: This specifies the name of the fuel_tank from which the engine will draw fuel. This is typically specified for a ramjet_engine_type instance rather than in the type definition.

subCommands.name: afterburner_appearance_when_operating
subCommands.description: This specifies whether or not an afterburner appearance should be used when the ramjet is operating. This only effects the appearance, it has no physical/kinematic effect. When true, and the ramjet is operating, it will have the same appearance of a jet engine using afterburner.

subCommands.name: latch_fuel_injection
subCommands.description: When true, the fuel injection will be latched (locked) into the on condition. This will keep the engine operating, regardless of throttle command, as long as fuel is available. When false, normal throttle control is used. The default value is false.

subCommands.name: use_proportional_throttle
subCommands.description: When true, a proportional throttle control will be used. When false, normal on/off throttle control is used. The default value is false.

subCommands.name: minimum_proportional_thrust
subCommands.description: This is the minimum thrust level that may be used for proportional throttle control. It is often 0.8, but must always be greater than zero. The default value is 0.0.

subCommands.name: liquid_propellant_rocket_type
subCommands.description: Definitions for each type of liquid-propellant rocket engine are performed within the liquid_propellant_rocket_type block. Since the definition is for a ‘type’ of engine and not an ‘instance’ of an engine, no installation position/attitude data is included. Typically, the fuel_feed is specified at the instance-level rather than at the type-level.

subCommands.name: max_thrust_sealevel
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum thrust that can be produced at sea level conditions. Either max_thrust_sealevel or max_thrust_vacuum should be specified, not both.

subCommands.name: max_thrust_vacuum
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum thrust that can be produced at vacuum conditions. Either max_thrust_sealevel or max_thrust_vacuum should be specified, not both.

subCommands.name: normalized_thrust_vs_alt
subCommands.description: This is a simple table of “normalized-thrust” versus altitude. Normalized thrust is a value that will be multiplied with a nominal isp-calculated thrust, typically computed using max_thrust_sealevel and isp_vs_alt. This allows altitude-effects on thrust production:

subCommands.name: platform_type
subCommands.description: Defines a platform type that can be referenced by the platform command. The <new-type-name> must be unique to the simulation. Convention is to make <new-type-name> uppercase. The <source-type-name> can either be a previously defined platform type or be WSF_PLATFORM. WSF_PLATFORM is the only <source-type-name> predefined platform type in WSF.

subCommands.name: platform_type
subCommands.description: Defines a platform type that can be referenced by the platform command. The <new-type-name> must be unique to the simulation. Convention is to make <new-type-name> uppercase. The <source-type-name> can either be a previously defined platform type or be WSF_PLATFORM. WSF_PLATFORM is the only <source-type-name> predefined platform type in WSF.

subCommands.name: side
subCommands.description: Specify the ‘side’ (‘team’ or ‘affiliation’) to which platforms of this type belong. The side subcommand refers to blue, red, country or team name. Refer to the specific visualization application or tool to see what sides are supported.

subCommands.name: icon
subCommands.description: Specify the name of the icon to be used when platforms of this type are displayed and if the platform type does not have an associated entity_type subcommand in the dis_interface block.

subCommands.name: marking
subCommands.description: Specifies a marking to be applied to the platform. This text field is associated with this platform in the dis_interface.

subCommands.name: indestructible
subCommands.description: Indicates that the platform type is indestructible. Each hit will update the cumulative probability of survival according to the formula:

subCommands.name: on_broken
subCommands.description: Indicates what should be done when the platform is broken.

subCommands.name: spatial_domain
subCommands.syntax: spatial_domain [ land | air | subsurface | surface | space]
subCommands.description: Indicates the primary spatial domain in which the platform operates. This is sometimes used to classify if an object is a ‘land’ object, ‘space’ object, etc.

subCommands.name: acoustic_signature
subCommands.description: Specifies the acoustic signature definition for this platform type. The signature type must have been defined with acoustic_signature.

subCommands.name: infrared_signature
subCommands.description: Specifies the infrared signature definition for this platform type. The signature type must be previously defined with infrared_signature.

subCommands.name: inherent_contrast
subCommands.description: Default None.

subCommands.name: optical_reflectivity
subCommands.description: Specifies the optical reflectivity definition for this platform type. The signature type must have been defined with optical_reflectivity.

subCommands.name: optical_signature
subCommands.description: Specifies the optical signature definition for this platform type. The signature type must have been defined with optical_signature.

subCommands.name: radar_signature
subCommands.description: Specifies the radar signature definition for this platform type. The signature type must have been defined with radar_signature.

subCommands.name: geo_point
subCommands.description: Defines a named location with a latitude, longitude, altitude tuple. The location can be accessed using the WsfPlatform.GeoPoint script method.

subCommands.name: position
subCommands.description: Specifies the latitude and longitude of the platform. This command is only for static platforms without movers.

subCommands.name: nutation_update_interval
subCommands.description: Specifies the time interval between updates to nutation calculations that are used in WCS-ECI coordinate conversions.

subCommands.name: precession_nutation_update_interval
subCommands.description: Specifies the time interval between updates to nutation calculations that are used in WCS-ECI coordinate conversions.

subCommands.name: mgrs_coordinate
subCommands.description: Specifies the coordinates of the platform in the Military Grid Reference System. This command is only for static platforms without movers.

subCommands.name: altitude
subCommands.description: Specifies the altitude of the platform. This command is only for static platforms without movers. It is ignored if a mover is defined in the platform.

subCommands.name: creation_time
subCommands.description: Specifies the simulation time at which the platform is to be added to the simulation. The platform exists in memory but is not yet a player in the simulation.

subCommands.name: heading
subCommands.description: Specifies the orientation of the platform. This command is only for static platforms without movers. It is ignored if a mover is defined in the platform.

subCommands.name: empty_mass
subCommands.description: Specifies the empty mass of the platform, which is usually a fixed quantity.

subCommands.name: fuel_mass
subCommands.description: Specifies the fuel mass of the platform. When specified by a user in an input file, the value is assumed to be a fixed quantity. However, if the platform contains a fuel object, it is permitted and even expected to modify the fuel mass during run time, overwriting what was specified with this keyword.

subCommands.name: payload_mass
subCommands.description: Specifies the payload mass of the platform. When specified by a user in an input file, the value is assumed to be a fixed quantity. However, certain run-time events (e.g., dropping buoys) may change the payload mass.

subCommands.name: concealment_factor
subCommands.description: Used to denote how well a platform is VISUALLY concealed. A value of 0.0 means there is no attempt to hide. A factor of 1.0 means that it is hidden in such a way as to be undetectable (such as in a building or in an underground bunker). Values between the endpoints represent increasing amounts of camouflage. Most sensors will not detect platforms with a concealment factor of 1.0, but any lesser value has no effect.

subCommands.name: initial_damage_factor
subCommands.description: The damage factor is a value in the range [0 .. 1] and is used to indicate the amount of damage to the platform. A value of 0 indicates no damage while a value of 1 indicates the platform is ‘broken.’

subCommands.name: track_manager
subCommands.description: Commands within this block are processed by the platform’s master track manager. See track_manager.

subCommands.name: aux_data
subCommands.description: Defines auxiliary data for a platform. See aux_data.

subCommands.name: width
subCommands.description: Specifies the dimensions of the platform.

subCommands.name: category
subCommands.description: Specifies that the platform is a member of the category specified. Categories can be used to force sensors to ignore the platform. Categories are also accessible through the WsfPlatform.CategoryMemberOf script method.

subCommands.name: clear_categories
subCommands.description: Has the effect of canceling any previous category command.

subCommands.name: group_leave
subCommands.description: Adds or removes the platform from the specified group.

subCommands.name: command_chain
subCommands.description: commander specifies the platform’s immediate superior (commander) in the default chain of command.

subCommands.name: route
subCommands.description: The route subcommand provides a collection of waypoints that define a path, or route, for platform movers.

subCommands.name: mover
subCommands.description: A mover defines the domain in which a platform can move and how it moves within the domain.

subCommands.name: fuel
subCommands.description: A fuel object can be attached to a platform to model the effects of fuel consumption.

subCommands.name: delete
subCommands.description: Adds a component to the platform, modifies or removes an existing component.

subCommands.name: track
subCommands.description: Defines a pre-briefed track.

subCommands.name: use_zone
subCommands.description: Attach a copy of the specified zone to the platform under the name <zone-name>. If the specified zone does not define a pose, the copied zone uses the current pose of the platform. This command can be repeated as necessary.

subCommands.name: zone_set
subCommands.description: The zone and zone_set subcommands define:

subCommands.name: navigation_errors
subCommands.description: The navigation_errors block provides a method to define error in where the platform thinks it is located versus where it is really located. Please see navigation_errors for a description of the inputs.

subCommands.name: on_damage_received
subCommands.description: An optional script that can be defined which will receive control whenever there is damage to the platform.

subCommands.name: on_platform_deleted
subCommands.description: An optional script that can be defined which will receive control just before the platform is removed from the simulation.

subCommands.name: on_subordinate_deleted
subCommands.description: Optional scripts that can be defined which will be executed just before other platforms within the platform’s command_chain hierarchy are removed from the simulation. The single argument to each script is a reference to the platform pending removal.

subCommands.name: callback
subCommands.description: A callback is a named action that can be called via the execute command of a route when the platform reaches a particular waypoint within the route.

subCommands.name: weapon_effects_type
subCommands.description: This command defines name of the weapon_effects for the platform. This is typically used only when the platform is the WSF_EXPLICIT_WEAPON of WSF_EXPLICIT_WEAPON.

subCommands.name: non_critical

name: point_mass_vehicle_type
description: The definition of a point_mass_vehicle_type is performed within a point_mass_vehicle_type block. Each point_mass_vehicle_type defines a ‘type’ of vehicle, ranging from a simple, hand-launched drone to a complex spacecraft. A point_mass_vehicle_type may include the definition of mass properties, primary aerodynamics, propulsion system components (including engines and fuel systems), subobjects (such as weapons, fuel tanks, etc.), sequencers (which can produce an “action” based on an “event”), controls providers (which include manual pilots, synthetic pilots, autopilots, and guidance systems), flight control systems (which determine how control inputs are routed/mixed to move control surfaces), secondary aerodynamics (which includes control surface aerodynamics), size factor parameters (which allow an object’s size to vary, such as that of a parachute or balloon), relative positioning (which defines how a subobject is positioned relative to its parent while captive), separation effects (which impart a delta-V or angular rate to a subobject when it is jettisoned from its parent), and other special properties.

subCommands.name: point_mass_vehicle_type
subCommands.description: The definition of a point_mass_vehicle_type is performed within a point_mass_vehicle_type block. Each point_mass_vehicle_type defines a ‘type’ of vehicle, ranging from a simple, hand-launched drone to a complex spacecraft. A point_mass_vehicle_type may include the definition of mass properties, primary aerodynamics, propulsion system components (including engines and fuel systems), subobjects (such as weapons, fuel tanks, etc.), sequencers (which can produce an “action” based on an “event”), controls providers (which include manual pilots, synthetic pilots, autopilots, and guidance systems), flight control systems (which determine how control inputs are routed/mixed to move control surfaces), secondary aerodynamics (which includes control surface aerodynamics), size factor parameters (which allow an object’s size to vary, such as that of a parachute or balloon), relative positioning (which defines how a subobject is positioned relative to its parent while captive), separation effects (which impart a delta-V or angular rate to a subobject when it is jettisoned from its parent), and other special properties.

subCommands.name: mass
subCommands.description: The (empty) mass of the object, not including fuel.

subCommands.name: moment_of_inertia_ixx
subCommands.description: The (empty) moment of inertia about the x-axis the object, not including fuel.

subCommands.name: moment_of_inertia_iyy
subCommands.description: The (empty) moment of inertia about the y-axis the object, not including fuel.

subCommands.name: moment_of_inertia_izz
subCommands.description: The (empty) moment of inertia about the z-axis the object, not including fuel.

subCommands.name: center_of_mass_x
subCommands.description: The empty center of mass (in the object’s x-direction) relative to the reference point.

subCommands.name: center_of_mass_y
subCommands.description: The empty center of mass (in the object’s y-direction) relative to the reference point.

subCommands.name: center_of_mass_z
subCommands.description: The empty center of mass (in the object’s z-direction) relative to the reference point.

subCommands.name: integrator
subCommands.description: This sets the object’s integrator type to the specified name. If no integrator with the specified name exists, an exception will be thrown, since SixDOF objects cannot function without an integrator.

subCommands.name: fuel_transfer
subCommands.description: Regardless of whether a fuel transfer is defined within the propulsion_data block or the point_mass_vehicle_type block, a fuel transfer always consists of a source tank and a target tank. During runtime, the source tank will attempt to transfer fuel to the target tank, limited by the transfer rates of the two tanks.

subCommands.name: source_tank
subCommands.description: The source tank is defined by its string name.

subCommands.name: target_tank
subCommands.description: The target tank is defined by its string name.

subCommands.name: remove_fuel_transfer
subCommands.description: This removes the fuel transfer with the specified name. If a no transfer exists with the name, the command is ignored.

subCommands.name: remove_fuel_tank
subCommands.description: This removes the fuel tank with the specified name. If a no tank exists with the name, the command is ignored.

subCommands.name: modify_fuel_quantity
subCommands.description: This modifies the quantity of fuel in the fuel tank with the specified name. If a no tank exists with the name, the command is ignored.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_x
subCommands.description: This specifies the x-location of the object’s reference point relative to the parent’s reference point using the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_y
subCommands.description: This specifies the y-location of the object’s reference point relative to the parent’s reference point using the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_z
subCommands.description: This specifies the z-location of the object’s reference point relative to the parent’s reference point using the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_yaw
subCommands.description: This specifies the yaw of the object about its reference point relative to the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_pitch
subCommands.description: This specifies the pitch of the object about its reference point relative to the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_roll
subCommands.description: This specifies the roll of the object about its reference point relative to the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: separation_vx
subCommands.description: This specifies the x-component of velocity (in parent body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_vy
subCommands.description: This specifies the y-component of velocity (in parent body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_vz
subCommands.description: This specifies the z-component of velocity (in parent body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_omega_x
subCommands.description: This specifies the x-component of angular velocity (in subobject body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_omega_y
subCommands.description: This specifies the y-component of angular velocity (in subobject body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_omega_z
subCommands.description: This specifies the z-component of angular velocity (in subobject body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: size_factor_radius
subCommands.description: This is the “reference” radius that is the starting radius of the object. This radius is also used to calculate a reference area and a reference volume.

subCommands.name: size_factor_min
subCommands.description: This is the minimum factor (multiplier) that the reference radius is allowed to achieve.

subCommands.name: size_factor_max
subCommands.description: This is the maximum factor (multiplier) that the reference radius is allowed to achieve.

subCommands.name: size_factor_volume_rate_m3_per_sec
subCommands.description: This provides a volume-based rate of change of cubic meters per second. When volume-based mode is used, the area and radius modes should not be used.

subCommands.name: size_factor_area_rate_m2_per_sec
subCommands.description: This provides an area-based rate of change of square meters per second. When area-based mode is used, the volume and radius modes should not be used.

subCommands.name: size_factor_radius_rate_m_per_sec
subCommands.description: This provides an radius-based rate of change of meters per second. When radius-based mode is used, the volume and area modes should not be used.

subCommands.name: use_spherical_earth
subCommands.description: If ‘true’, the SixDOF object will use a spherical earth model rather than a WGS84 (oblate) earth model. This is often a useful simplification when using ballistic missiles and space launch vehicles, since it eliminates latitude issues for guidance associated with an oblate earth.

subCommands.name: use_rotating_earth
subCommands.description: If ‘true’, the SixDOF object will use a rotating earth model rather than a non-rotating earth model.

subCommands.name: ignore_jettisoned_objects
subCommands.description: If ‘true’, any subobjects that are jettisoned from the SixDOF object will be removed immediately and will never have an AFSIM platform. This is often used to speed up runtimes when spent stages from a ballistic missile or space launch vehicle are not needed.

subCommands.name: fixed_object
subCommands.description: If ‘true’, the SixDOF object will not perform kinematic calculations as part of its “update” but will instead remain motionless.

subCommands.name: nominal_max_mach
subCommands.description: This defines the maximum Mach expected by the object. This does not impose a limit on performance, rather it is a hint for functions that calculate performance and/or analysis.

subCommands.name: nominal_max_alpha

subCommands.name: nominal_max_beta
subCommands.description: This defines the maximum beta (angle of sideslip) expected by the object. This does not impose a limit on performance, rather it is a hint for functions that calculate performance and/or analysis.

name: post_processor
syntax: report [communication | detection | eclipse | engagement | dsv | trajectory]
description: Specifies the type of report that is being generated.

subCommands.name: report
subCommands.syntax: report [communication | detection | eclipse | engagement | dsv | trajectory]
subCommands.description: Specifies the type of report that is being generated.

subCommands.name: report_name
subCommands.description: Specifies the name of the report. If the folder(s) or file(s) already exist then it will be overwritten. The run number is automatically inserted at the end of the filename, but can be inserted manually also using the %d tag. The date and time tags, %D and %T may also be used to aid in file management.

subCommands.name: data_file
subCommands.description: Specifies the name of the file where the input file(s) are located. To process Monte-Carlo files insert the run number tag %d in the file name.

subCommands.name: output_directory
subCommands.description: Specifies the name of the folder where the output files will be generated. If the folder & files already exist then it will be overwritten. The run number is automatically inserted at the end of the filename, but can be inserted manually also using the %d tag. The date and time tags, %D and %T may also be used to aid in file management.

subCommands.name: monte_carlo_start
subCommands.description: Specifies the starting run number.

subCommands.name: monte_carlo_end
subCommands.description: Specifies the ending run number.

subCommands.name: single_output_file
subCommands.description: Specifies if all formatted run data should be output to a single file. (Currently not implemented)

subCommands.name: write_header_information
subCommands.description: Specifies if headers should be output to the report(s).

subCommands.name: delimiter
subCommands.description: Specifies the delimiter that separates the values.

subCommands.name: length_units
subCommands.description: Specifies the unit of measurement for distances. (Currently not implemented)

subCommands.name: angle_units
subCommands.description: Specifies the unit of measurement for angles. (Currently not implemented)

subCommands.name: track_number_options
subCommands.description: Specifies the track number format options. (Currently not implemented)

subCommands.name: start_time
subCommands.description: Specifies the start time of the desired data.

subCommands.name: end_time
subCommands.description: Specifies the end time of the desired data.

subCommands.name: lat_lon_format

subCommands.name: gmti_adjustment_table
subCommands.description: Defines a function that attempts to capture the effect that a slow moving target is harder for a MTI sensor to detect that a faster moving target of the same size, and that the effect is non-linear. The function defines an adjustment factor (degradation of the received signal) versus either the closing speed or Doppler frequency. The table is defined using one of the following two forms:

subCommands.name: mti_adjustment_file
subCommands.description: Specifies an external MTI table in a comma-separated-value (CSV) file. The file should have one header row and two columns. The 1st column is the independent speed values, while the 2nd column is the dependent attenuation values. All entries should be unit-less. This table only supports speed and dB entries. The assumed units are m/sec and dB.

subCommands.name: mti_adjustment_compound_file
subCommands.description: Specifies an external MTI table in a comma-separated-value (CSV) file. The file should have one header row and ‘more’ than two columns. The last column is the dependent attenuation, while all preceding columns are independent speed values which all map to the dependent attenuation. The convention is that each independent column represents a different frequency, and that frequency is indicated in its header. For example, a column header of “ATTN (db) 30” is the column for 30 MHz. The dependent attenuation column entry can by any string. All entries should be unit-less. Excluding the header, this table only supports speed and dB entries. The assumed units are m/sec and dB.

subCommands.name: mti_maximum_range
subCommands.description: Specifies a maximum range to be used with the MTI “tables” only. If the target is farther away, any MTI table will NOT be applied.

subCommands.name: maximum_range
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum ground range from the sensor to the target for which MTI processing will occur. MTI processing will be applied only if the target is within this range.

subCommands.name: interpulse_period_2
subCommands.description: Optional values that indicate the interpulse periods.

subCommands.description: Specifies the number of stages in the MTI processor.

subCommands.name: interpolation_type
subCommands.description: Specifies whether to use linear or logarithmic interpolation when interpolating data in the azimuth elevation tables.

subCommands.name: state
subCommands.description: Indicates that the following table definitions will be used when the platform is in the signature state <state-name>.

subCommands.name: polarization
subCommands.syntax: polarization [ horizontal | vertical | slant_45 | slant_135 | left_circular | right_circular | default ]
subCommands.description: Indicates that the following table(s) (up to the next polarization or state) are to be used when the sensing radar is operating with the specified polarization.

subCommands.name: frequency_limit
subCommands.description: Indicates the upper frequency bound to which the following table applies. These must occur in increasing order within a single state/polarization grouping. For a radar is operating with a particular polarization and frequency, the table selected will be the first one with the proper state and polarization where the frequency less than frequency_limit.

subCommands.name: plt_file
subCommands.description: Loads a PLT file, in either 3- or 5-column format, that includes multiple Az/El table definitions indexed by polarization and frequency. Because the polarization and frequency are embedded within the file, any previous polarization or frequency_limit command will be ignored. Optionally, a polarization (horizontal or vertical) to be used as the default may be specified. However, since every state must have a default polarization, if this optional argument is omitted, one must be defined explicitly using the polarization command.

subCommands.name: bistatic_signature
subCommands.description: Defines a bistatic radar signature for a platform type. This signature is used for bistatic interactions (i.e. interactions involving a transmitter and receiver not colocated). This input block is defined within the radar_signature block and defines a separate table to be used for bistatic interactions RCS lookups.

subCommands.name: interpolate_transmitter_angles
subCommands.description: Specifies whether or not to interpolate between the tables for the specified target->transmitter angles. If ‘false’ then the next lower azimuth/elevation angle table is used for the given target->transmitter azimuth/elevation pair.

subCommands.name: transmitter_angles_interpolation_type
subCommands.description: Specifies whether to use linear or logarithmic interpolation when interpolating target->transmitter angles.

subCommands.name: azimuth
subCommands.description: Specifies the minimum target->transmitter azimuth angle, between [-180.0, 180.0] degrees, for the entered table. Must specify at least two monotonically increasing angles with tables. Tables are a function of the target->receiver angles.

subCommands.name: elevation
subCommands.description: Specifies the minimum target->transmitter elevation angle, between [-90.0, 90.0] degrees, for the entered table. Must specify at least two monotonically increasing angles. Tables are a function of the target->receiver azimuth/elevation angles.

name: receiver
description: The receiver block defines the attributes of an electromagnetic receiver. Various sensor and communication objects make use of receivers.

subCommands.name: antenna_ohmic_loss
subCommands.description: This value, along with noise_figure and receive_line_loss, provides one method to determine the receiver noise power. It specifies the ohmic resistance of the antenna.

subCommands.name: antenna_pattern
subCommands.description: Specifies the name of the antenna gain pattern used by the receiver. The pattern must be defined using the antenna_pattern command.

subCommands.name: antenna_pattern_table
subCommands.description: This command allows the definition of frequency-dependent or polarization- and frequency-dependent antenna gain pattern. Each named antenna pattern must be defined using the antenna_pattern command.

subCommands.name: attenuation
subCommands.syntax: attenuation ….. (attenuation is a synonym for attenuation_model)
subCommands.description: Specify the attenuation model. See the global command attenuation_model for more information about the available attenuation models and how to configure the models.

subCommands.name: aux_data
subCommands.description: Defines application-specific ‘auxiliary data’. See aux_data.

subCommands.name: bandwidth
subCommands.description: [ frequency - 1/2 bandwidth, frequency + 1/2 bandwidth ]

subCommands.name: beam_tilt
subCommands.description: This is only to be used when defining systems that employ multiple beams (e.g., when using multiple beams in WSF_RADAR_SENSOR). It specifies the elevation angle of the beam center above the horizontal plane.

subCommands.name: check_terrain_masking
subCommands.description: Toggles the computation of terrain and horizon line of sight. This may be set to ‘off’ to either reduce computation or model sensors and comm devices which do not have line of sight limitations. By default, horizon masking is checked first, followed by a separate terrain masking check if terrain is loaded. The simple horizon masking check assumes a smooth bald spherical Earth and that any object below zero mean sea level is obscured. For subsurface sensors, horizon checking can be disabled by setting the terrain_masking_mode to terrain_only.

subCommands.name: check_transmitter_masking
subCommands.description: Toggles the computation of terrain and horizon line of sight for transmitter checks. This may be set to ‘off’ to either reduce computation or model sensors and comm devices which do not have line of sight limitations, e.g. bistatic sensors.

subCommands.name: terrain_masking_mode
subCommands.description: Sets the mode or type of masking checks to perform. By default, both horizon and terrain masking checks are enabled.

subCommands.name: detection_threshold
subCommands.description: Specifies the signal-to-noise ratio above which the signal is declared to be detectable.

subCommands.name: effective_earth_radius
subCommands.description: Specify either the multiplier for Earth’s radius, or the effective earth radius, used to compute the effects of atmospheric refraction of radio-frequency signals.

subCommands.name: wavelength
subCommands.description: Specifies the center frequency to which the receiver is tuned. The receiver will accept signals whose frequency is between:

subCommands.name: instantaneous_bandwidth
subCommands.description: Specifies the instantaneous bandwidth of the receiver. For a frequency hopping or scanning system, this would be the bandwidth that is processed during an individual hop or scan point.

subCommands.name: internal_loss
subCommands.description: A single number can be used account for miscellaneous losses. This value occurs in the denominator:

subCommands.name: noise_figure
subCommands.description: This value, along with antenna_ohmic_loss and receive_line_loss, provide one method to specify the receiver noise power.

subCommands.name: noise_power
subCommands.description: Specifies the explicit noise power. This is one mechanism for specifying the receiver noise.

subCommands.name: polarization
subCommands.syntax: polarization [ horizontal | vertical | slant_45 | slant_135 | left_circular | right_circular | default ]
subCommands.description: Specify the primary polarization of the signals which the receiving antenna will receive.

subCommands.name: polarization_effect
subCommands.syntax: polarization_effect [ horizontal | vertical | slant_45 | slant_135 | left_circular | right_circular ] <fraction>
subCommands.description: This command defines the fraction of a received signal of the specified polarization that will be processed. This allows one to override the default behavior when a receiver attempts to receive a signal that is of a different polarization that its primary polarization.

subCommands.name: propagation_model
subCommands.description: Specify the propagation model. See global command propagation_model for more information about the available propagation models and how to configure the models.

subCommands.name: receive_line_loss
subCommands.description: This value, along with antenna_ohmic_loss and noise_figure, provide one method to specify the receiver noise power. It specifies the RF component line loss between the antenna and the receiver.

subCommands.name: electronic_protect
subCommands.description: A block that defines the Electronic Protection (EP) capabilities within the receiver. See electronic_protect for the available commands.

name: Rendezvous
description: The desired time past the current time for execution of the maneuver. No Optimizations are performed.

subCommands.name: delta_time
subCommands.description: The desired time past the current time for execution of the maneuver. No Optimizations are performed.

subCommands.name: maximum_delta_time
subCommands.description: The maximum time after the current time to be considered for execution of the maneuver. Optimizations in time will occur between the time of the constraint and the provided time.

subCommands.name: maximum_delta_v
subCommands.description: The maximum delta_v to be considered for execution of the maneuver. Optimizations in time to find minimum delta-v will occur between the time of the constraint and any time limit set by maximum_delta_time.

subCommands.name: optimize_time
subCommands.description: Optimize the targeting solution such that it executes at the earliest possible time. This optimization is also constrained by the maximum_delta_v value, if provided.

subCommands.name: optimize_delta_v
subCommands.description: Optimize the targeting solution such that it executes at a time that minimizes total delta-v expended.

subCommands.name: optimize_cost
subCommands.description: Optimize the targeting solution such that the specified cost is minimized. The available cost functions are:

subCommands.name: tolerance
subCommands.description: Specify the solution search tolerance. The default tolerance is 1.0e-9.

name: rigid_body_vehicle_type
description: The definition of a rigid_body_vehicle_type is performed within a rigid_body_vehicle_type block. Each rigid_body_vehicle_type defines a ‘type’ of vehicle, ranging from a simple, hand-launched drone to a complex spacecraft. A rigid_body_vehicle_type may include the definition of mass properties, primary aerodynamics, propulsion system components (including engines and fuel systems), subobjects (such as weapons, fuel tanks, etc.), sequencers (which can produce an “action” based on an “event”), controls providers (which include manual pilots, synthetic pilots, autopilots, and guidance systems), flight control systems (which determine how control inputs are routed/mixed to move control surfaces), secondary aerodynamics (which includes control surface aerodynamics), size factor parameters (which allow an object’s size to vary, such as that of a parachute or balloon), relative positioning (which defines how a subobject is positioned relative to its parent while captive), separation effects (which impart a delta-V or angular rate to a subobject when it is jettisoned from its parent), and other special properties.

subCommands.name: rigid_body_vehicle_type
subCommands.description: The definition of a rigid_body_vehicle_type is performed within a rigid_body_vehicle_type block. Each rigid_body_vehicle_type defines a ‘type’ of vehicle, ranging from a simple, hand-launched drone to a complex spacecraft. A rigid_body_vehicle_type may include the definition of mass properties, primary aerodynamics, propulsion system components (including engines and fuel systems), subobjects (such as weapons, fuel tanks, etc.), sequencers (which can produce an “action” based on an “event”), controls providers (which include manual pilots, synthetic pilots, autopilots, and guidance systems), flight control systems (which determine how control inputs are routed/mixed to move control surfaces), secondary aerodynamics (which includes control surface aerodynamics), size factor parameters (which allow an object’s size to vary, such as that of a parachute or balloon), relative positioning (which defines how a subobject is positioned relative to its parent while captive), separation effects (which impart a delta-V or angular rate to a subobject when it is jettisoned from its parent), and other special properties.

subCommands.name: mass
subCommands.description: The (empty) mass of the object, not including fuel.

subCommands.name: moment_of_inertia_ixx
subCommands.description: The (empty) moment of inertia about the x-axis the object, not including fuel.

subCommands.name: moment_of_inertia_iyy
subCommands.description: The (empty) moment of inertia about the y-axis the object, not including fuel.

subCommands.name: moment_of_inertia_izz
subCommands.description: The (empty) moment of inertia about the z-axis the object, not including fuel.

subCommands.name: center_of_mass_x
subCommands.description: The empty center of mass (in the object’s x-direction) relative to the reference point.

subCommands.name: center_of_mass_y
subCommands.description: The empty center of mass (in the object’s y-direction) relative to the reference point.

subCommands.name: center_of_mass_z
subCommands.description: The empty center of mass (in the object’s z-direction) relative to the reference point.

subCommands.name: integrator
subCommands.description: This sets the object’s integrator type to the specified name. If no integrator with the specified name exists, an exception will be thrown, since SixDOF objects cannot function without an integrator.

subCommands.name: fuel_transfer
subCommands.description: Regardless of whether a fuel transfer is defined within the propulsion_data block or the rigid_body_vehicle_type block, a fuel transfer always consists of a source tank and a target tank. During runtime, the source tank will attempt to transfer fuel to the target tank, limited by the transfer rates of the two tanks.

subCommands.name: source_tank
subCommands.description: The source tank is defined by its string name.

subCommands.name: target_tank
subCommands.description: The target tank is defined by its string name.

subCommands.name: remove_fuel_transfer
subCommands.description: This removes the fuel transfer with the specified name. If a no transfer exists with the name, the command is ignored.

subCommands.name: remove_fuel_tank
subCommands.description: This removes the fuel tank with the specified name. If a no tank exists with the name, the command is ignored.

subCommands.name: modify_fuel_quantity
subCommands.description: This modifies the quantity of fuel in the fuel tank with the specified name. If a no tank exists with the name, the command is ignored.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_x
subCommands.description: This specifies the x-location of the object’s reference point relative to the parent’s reference point using the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_y
subCommands.description: This specifies the y-location of the object’s reference point relative to the parent’s reference point using the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_z
subCommands.description: This specifies the z-location of the object’s reference point relative to the parent’s reference point using the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_yaw
subCommands.description: This specifies the yaw of the object about its reference point relative to the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_pitch
subCommands.description: This specifies the pitch of the object about its reference point relative to the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_roll
subCommands.description: This specifies the roll of the object about its reference point relative to the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: separation_vx
subCommands.description: This specifies the x-component of velocity (in parent body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_vy
subCommands.description: This specifies the y-component of velocity (in parent body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_vz
subCommands.description: This specifies the z-component of velocity (in parent body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_omega_x
subCommands.description: This specifies the x-component of angular velocity (in subobject body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_omega_y
subCommands.description: This specifies the y-component of angular velocity (in subobject body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_omega_z
subCommands.description: This specifies the z-component of angular velocity (in subobject body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: size_factor_radius
subCommands.description: This is the “reference” radius that is the starting radius of the object. This radius is also used to calculate a reference area and a reference volume.

subCommands.name: size_factor_min
subCommands.description: This is the minimum factor (multiplier) that the reference radius is allowed to achieve.

subCommands.name: size_factor_max
subCommands.description: This is the maximum factor (multiplier) that the reference radius is allowed to achieve.

subCommands.name: size_factor_volume_rate_m3_per_sec
subCommands.description: This provides a volume-based rate of change of cubic meters per second. When volume-based mode is used, the area and radius modes should not be used.

subCommands.name: size_factor_area_rate_m2_per_sec
subCommands.description: This provides an area-based rate of change of square meters per second. When area-based mode is used, the volume and radius modes should not be used.

subCommands.name: size_factor_radius_rate_m_per_sec
subCommands.description: This provides an radius-based rate of change of meters per second. When radius-based mode is used, the volume and area modes should not be used.

subCommands.name: use_spherical_earth
subCommands.description: If ‘true’, the SixDOF object will use a spherical earth model rather than a WGS84 (oblate) earth model. This is often a useful simplification when using ballistic missiles and space launch vehicles, since it eliminates latitude issues for guidance associated with an oblate earth.

subCommands.name: use_rotating_earth
subCommands.description: If ‘true’, the SixDOF object will use a rotating earth model rather than a non-rotating earth model.

subCommands.name: ignore_jettisoned_objects
subCommands.description: If ‘true’, any subobjects that are jettisoned from the SixDOF object will be removed immediately and will never have an AFSIM platform. This is often used to speed up runtimes when spent stages from a ballistic missile or space launch vehicle are not needed.

subCommands.name: fixed_object
subCommands.description: If ‘true’, the SixDOF object will not perform kinematic calculations as part of its “update” but will instead remain motionless.

subCommands.name: nominal_max_mach
subCommands.description: This defines the maximum Mach expected by the object. This does not impose a limit on performance, rather it is a hint for functions that calculate performance and/or analysis.

subCommands.name: nominal_max_alpha
subCommands.description: This defines the maximum alpha (angle of attack) expected by the object. This does not impose a limit on performance, rather it is a hint for functions that calculate performance and/or analysis.

subCommands.name: nominal_min_alpha
subCommands.description: This defines the minimum alpha (angle of attack) expected by the object. This does not impose a limit on performance, rather it is a hint for functions that calculate performance and/or analysis.

subCommands.name: nominal_max_beta
subCommands.description: This defines the maximum beta (angle of sideslip) expected by the object. This does not impose a limit on performance, rather it is a hint for functions that calculate performance and/or analysis.

subCommands.description: The (empty) mass of the object, not including fuel.

subCommands.name: moment_of_inertia_ixx
subCommands.description: The (empty) moment of inertia about the x-axis the object, not including fuel.

subCommands.name: moment_of_inertia_izz

subCommands.name: center_of_mass_z
subCommands.description: The empty center of mass (in the object’s z-direction) relative to the reference point.

subCommands.name: integrator
subCommands.description: This sets the object’s integrator type to the specified name. If no integrator with the specified name exists, an exception will be thrown, since SixDOF objects cannot function without an integrator.

subCommands.name: fuel_transfer
subCommands.description: Regardless of whether a fuel transfer is defined within the propulsion_data block or the rigid_body_vehicle_type block, a fuel transfer always consists of a source tank and a target tank. During runtime, the source tank will attempt to transfer fuel to the target tank, limited by the transfer rates of the two tanks.

subCommands.name: source_tank
subCommands.description: The source tank is defined by its string name.

subCommands.name: target_tank
subCommands.description: The target tank is defined by its string name.

subCommands.name: remove_fuel_transfer
subCommands.description: This removes the fuel transfer with the specified name. If a no transfer exists with the name, the command is ignored.

subCommands.name: remove_fuel_tank
subCommands.description: This removes the fuel tank with the specified name. If a no tank exists with the name, the command is ignored.

subCommands.name: modify_fuel_quantity
subCommands.description: This modifies the quantity of fuel in the fuel tank with the specified name. If a no tank exists with the name, the command is ignored.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_x
subCommands.description: This specifies the x-location of the object’s reference point relative to the parent’s reference point using the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_y
subCommands.description: This specifies the y-location of the object’s reference point relative to the parent’s reference point using the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_z
subCommands.description: This specifies the z-location of the object’s reference point relative to the parent’s reference point using the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_yaw
subCommands.description: This specifies the yaw of the object about its reference point relative to the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_pitch
subCommands.description: This specifies the pitch of the object about its reference point relative to the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: parent_rel_roll
subCommands.description: This specifies the roll of the object about its reference point relative to the parent’s body coordinate system.

subCommands.name: separation_vx
subCommands.description: This specifies the x-component of velocity (in parent body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_vy
subCommands.description: This specifies the y-component of velocity (in parent body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_vz
subCommands.description: This specifies the z-component of velocity (in parent body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_omega_x
subCommands.description: This specifies the x-component of angular velocity (in subobject body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_omega_y
subCommands.description: This specifies the y-component of angular velocity (in subobject body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: separation_omega_z
subCommands.description: This specifies the z-component of angular velocity (in subobject body coordinates) that is imparted to the subobject when it separates from the parent.

subCommands.name: size_factor_radius
subCommands.description: This is the “reference” radius that is the starting radius of the object. This radius is also used to calculate a reference area and a reference volume.

subCommands.name: size_factor_min
subCommands.description: This is the minimum factor (multiplier) that the reference radius is allowed to achieve.

subCommands.name: size_factor_max
subCommands.description: This is the maximum factor (multiplier) that the reference radius is allowed to achieve.

subCommands.name: size_factor_volume_rate_m3_per_sec
subCommands.description: This provides a volume-based rate of change of cubic meters per second. When volume-based mode is used, the area and radius modes should not be used.

subCommands.name: size_factor_area_rate_m2_per_sec
subCommands.description: This provides an area-based rate of change of square meters per second. When area-based mode is used, the volume and radius modes should not be used.

subCommands.name: size_factor_radius_rate_m_per_sec
subCommands.description: This provides an radius-based rate of change of meters per second. When radius-based mode is used, the volume and area modes should not be used.

subCommands.name: use_spherical_earth
subCommands.description: If ‘true’, the SixDOF object will use a spherical earth model rather than a WGS84 (oblate) earth model. This is often a useful simplification when using ballistic missiles and space launch vehicles, since it eliminates latitude issues for guidance associated with an oblate earth.

subCommands.name: use_rotating_earth
subCommands.description: If ‘true’, the SixDOF object will use a rotating earth model rather than a non-rotating earth model.

subCommands.name: ignore_jettisoned_objects
subCommands.description: If ‘true’, any subobjects that are jettisoned from the SixDOF object will be removed immediately and will never have an AFSIM platform. This is often used to speed up runtimes when spent stages from a ballistic missile or space launch vehicle are not needed.

subCommands.name: fixed_object
subCommands.description: If ‘true’, the SixDOF object will not perform kinematic calculations as part of its “update” but will instead remain motionless.

subCommands.name: nominal_max_mach
subCommands.description: This defines the maximum Mach expected by the object. This does not impose a limit on performance, rather it is a hint for functions that calculate performance and/or analysis.

subCommands.name: nominal_max_alpha
subCommands.description: This defines the maximum alpha (angle of attack) expected by the object. This does not impose a limit on performance, rather it is a hint for functions that calculate performance and/or analysis.

subCommands.name: nominal_min_alpha
subCommands.description: This defines the minimum alpha (angle of attack) expected by the object. This does not impose a limit on performance, rather it is a hint for functions that calculate performance and/or analysis.

subCommands.name: nominal_max_beta
subCommands.description: This defines the maximum beta (angle of sideslip) expected by the object. This does not impose a limit on performance, rather it is a hint for functions that calculate performance and/or analysis.

subCommands.name: network
subCommands.description: Defines the attributes and vehicles that are generated on the defined route_network as specified by the <route-network-name>.

subCommands.name: vehicle_count
subCommands.description: The number of vehicles generated and placed on the road network. If the <vehicle_count> is not specified, it will be set using <vehicle_density>.

subCommands.name: vehicle_density
subCommands.description: Instead of specifying a specific number of vehicles, a density number of vehicles per unit length can be specified (i.e., 5 per 1km)

subCommands.name: maximum_speed
subCommands.description: The maximum speed any vehicle on the network can travel even if a faster speed is specified in the vehicle block. This could simulate a speed limit.

subCommands.name: mean_travel_time
subCommands.description: The average travel time of all the vehicles in the network.

subCommands.name: sigma_travel_time
subCommands.description: The travel time magnitude of one standard deviation. When a vehicle reaches the end of its path or travel time, it travels off road by some amount and then pauses for a given amount of time before being removed from the simulation. The following three items (<minimum_distance_off_road>, maximum_distance_off_road, and pause_time_off_road) define the parameters, which define this process.

subCommands.name: minimum_distance_off_road
subCommands.description: The minimum distance that a vehicle travels off-road.

subCommands.name: maximum_distance_off_road
subCommands.description: The maximum distance that a vehicle travels off-road.

subCommands.name: pause_time_off_road
subCommands.description: The time that a vehicle pauses at the end of its route after traveling off-road.

subCommands.name: end_of_path_option
subCommands.description: This determines what should be done to vehicles at the end of their route. By default vehicles are re-spawned with a different route.

subCommands.name: vehicle
subCommands.description: Defines the attributes of a specific vehicle type within the context of this net work. To define multiple vehicle types, create multiple vehicle blocks. The <platform-type> must be a previously defined platform_type.

subCommands.name: fraction
subCommands.description: If multiple vehicle blocks are defined, the fraction is the percentage (as a decimal value) of this specific vehicle type that would populate the road network. The sum of all the vehicle fractions must add up to 1.

subCommands.name: mean_speed
subCommands.description: The average speed of all the vehicles defined by this vehicle block.

subCommands.name: sigma_speed
subCommands.description: The speed magnitude of one standard deviation.

subCommands.name: convoy
subCommands.description: This command defines a convoy (a series of vehicles that follow each other), that moves between two endpoints.

subCommands.name: start_position
subCommands.description: This defines the initial location of the convoy with a latitude and longitude value.

subCommands.name: end_position
subCommands.description: This defines the final location of the convoy as a latitude and longitude value.

subCommands.name: spacing
subCommands.description: This defines the spacing between each of the vehicles in the convoy.

subCommands.name: speed
subCommands.description: This defines the speed that the convoy will travel.

subCommands.name: use_closest_waypoint
subCommands.description: If this option is present, the convoy will start at the closest waypoint to the specified start position and end at the closest waypoint to the end position.

subCommands.name: vehicle
subCommands.description: This defines a specific vehicle type and the number of that type in the convoy. This option can be specified multiple times to create multiple vehicle types.

subCommands.name: weighted_region
subCommands.description: This command defines a region in the network where a higher density of vehicles will be created. For instance, this command can be used to generate more vehicles in a city region than in the country. Weighted regions have an inner and outer radius and weight. The weights are linearly interpolated between the inner and outer radii. This allows the simulation to vary the density of vehicles linearly between the inner and outer radii.

subCommands.name: latitude
subCommands.description: Specifies the center latitude of the weighted region.

subCommands.name: longitude
subCommands.description: Specifies the center longitude of the weighted region.

subCommands.name: inner_radius
subCommands.description: Specifies the inner radius of the weighted region.

subCommands.name: outer_radius
subCommands.description: Specifies the outer radius of the weighted region.

subCommands.name: inner_weight
subCommands.description: Specifies the weight that corresponds to the inner radius. The larger the weight number, the higher the density of vehicles.

subCommands.name: outer_weight
subCommands.description: Specifies the weight that corresponds to the outer radius. The larger the weight number, the higher the density of vehicles.
