subCommands.name: navigation
subCommands.description: Defines the block input for Navigation Commands used to enter the route waypoints and other navigational data.

subCommands.name: aux_data
subCommands.description: Defines auxiliary data for a route. See aux_data for more commands and information.

subCommands.name: label
subCommands.description: Associates a string label with the immediately following waypoint definition. This can be used as the target of a goto command.

subCommands.name: position
subCommands.description: Specifies the latitude and longitude of the waypoint.

subCommands.name: mgrs_coordinate
subCommands.description: Specifies the coordinate of the waypoint in the Military Grid Reference System.

subCommands.name: offset
subCommands.description: Go to a point relative to the current location of the platform. Each offset waypoint is relative to the position of the previous waypoint (or platform’s position if it is the first waypoint), and orientation is set using the heading at the first offset waypoint and remains constant for all subsequent offset waypoints. The +X axis is in the direction of the initial heading and the +Y axis is 90 degrees to the right of the initial heading.

subCommands.name: turn_right
subCommands.description: Initiate a turn to effect the specified heading angle change.

subCommands.name: turn_to_heading
subCommands.description: Initiate a turn to the specified absolute heading angle. The direction of the turn will be in the direction that requires the least amount of heading angle change.

subCommands.name: goto
subCommands.description: When this waypoint is reached, go to the waypoint with the specified label in the current route.

subCommands.name: altitude
subCommands.description: Specifies the altitude at the waypoint. if agl or msl is omitted, the default altitude reference is defined by the mover. msl is assumed for WSF_AIR_MOVER and agl for all others.

subCommands.name: depth
subCommands.description: Specifies the sub-surface depth at the waypoint.

subCommands.name: heading
subCommands.description: Specifies the heading at the waypoint. This is really only effective for a route with one point. If more than one waypoint is given then heading will be determined automatically.

subCommands.name: turn
subCommands.description: Specifies the direction to turn if a turn is required.

subCommands.name: speed
subCommands.description: Specifies the speed at the waypoint.

subCommands.name: linear_acceleration
subCommands.description: Specifies the linear acceleration to be used for changing speed on the route segment that starts with this waypoint. <acceleration-value> may also be default to use the mover’s default linear_acceleration.

subCommands.name: radial_acceleration
subCommands.description: Specifies the radial acceleration to be used for turns when making heading changes on the route segment that starts with this waypoint. <acceleration-value> may also be default to use the mover’s default radial_acceleration.

subCommands.name: bank_angle_limit
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum bank angle to be used for turns when making heading changes on the route segment that starts with this waypoint. This effectively sets the radial_acceleration to .

subCommands.name: turn_g_limit
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum turn g-load to be used for turns when making heading changes on the route segment that starts with this waypoint. This effectively sets the radial_acceleration to .

subCommands.name: dive_rate
subCommands.description: Specifies the rate of climb or dive for changing altitude on the route segment that starts with this waypoint. <speed-value>* may also be default to use the mover’s default climb_rate. Note: the commands climb_rate and dive_rate are synonymous – specifying a dive_rate will replace a previously specified climb_rate.

subCommands.name: maximum_flight_path_angle
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum flight path angle for climbs and dives that happen after this waypoint. If default is specified, the mover will use its default value.

subCommands.name: pause_time
subCommands.description: When the waypoint is reached, stop moving for the specified time.

subCommands.name: execute
subCommands.description: Specify a script or callback to be executed upon reaching the waypoint. <script-name>/<callback-name> must be the name of a ‘script’ defined for the platform or platform_type.

subCommands.name: remove
subCommands.description: Indicates to the mover what is to be done when this waypoint is encountered and there are no more waypoints in the route. The possible actions are:

subCommands.name: switch_on_approach
subCommands.description: Defines the condition when the mover should declare that it has reached this waypoint and should start moving towards the next waypoint. switch_on_passing is sometimes known as ‘turn long’ and causes the switch to occur when the platform passes over or along side of the waypoint. switch_on_approach is sometimes known as ‘turn short’ and causes the switch to occur before the waypoint.

subCommands.name: time
subCommands.description: If the waypoint is a turn_left, turn_right or turn_to_heading and the next waypoint is also one of the same class, this command specifies how long or how far to move until switching to the next waypoint.

subCommands.name: time_to_point
subCommands.description: If specified, the mover will change speed in attempt to reach this waypoint after the specified duration. <time-value> is the length of time it should take the platform to move from the previous waypoint to the current one. time_to_point may only be specified for position waypoints.

subCommands.name: node_id
subCommands.description: This command is used only if the route is part of a route_network. Waypoints that share the same node_id within a set of routes within a route_network are assumed to intersect or connect at those points.

subCommands.name: aux_data
subCommands.description: Defines auxiliary data for a waypoint. See aux_data.

subCommands.name: insert_route
subCommands.description: Transforms the named route and inserts its waypoints into the route being defined. The named route should have already been defined as a ‘route type’. All points in the named route that were defined using the offset command are transformed to a new coordinate system whose origin and orientation are defined below and then internally converted to position points.

subCommands.name: insert_offset_route
subCommands.description: The insert_offset_route command is similar to insert_route. The insert_offset_route command converts offset waypoints to be relative to a single origin. This is different than offset waypoints explicitly defined in a route which are treated relative to the previous waypoint. This means a route explicitly containing offset waypoints will be a different route than one that implicitly includes those offset waypoints using the insert_route command.

subCommands.name: transform_absolute_route
subCommands.description: Translate the named route the specified about and insert it into the current route. Only position points will be translated.

subCommands.name: transform_route
subCommands.description: Transforms the named route and inserts its waypoints into the route being defined. The named route should have already been defined as a ‘route type’. All points in the named route that were defined using the offset command are transformed to a new coordinate system whose origin and orientation are defined below and then internally converted to position points.

subCommands.name: use_route
subCommands.description: Include the route type with the specified name as part of the route definition. Repeat as required to specify the route network.

subCommands.name: test
subCommands.description: During initialization, test all possible paths between each node_id in all route’s to solve the shortest path. A count of Nodes in the route_network tested is output to the console. See Example 1 - route_network with test command.

subCommands.name: test_nodes
subCommands.description: During initialization, test all routes to solve the shortest path between <from-node-id> and <to-node-id> (specified as integers).

subCommands.name: verbose
subCommands.description: Generates additional debug data when used with the test command. The following data is output to the console for each path tested:

subCommands.name: use_route
subCommands.description: Include the route type with the specified name as part of the route definition. Repeat as required to specify the route network.

subCommands.name: test
subCommands.description: During initialization, test all possible paths between each node_id in all route’s to solve the shortest path. A count of Nodes in the route_network tested is output to the console. See Example 1 - route_network with test command.

subCommands.name: test_nodes
subCommands.description: During initialization, test all routes to solve the shortest path between <from-node-id> and <to-node-id> (specified as integers).

subCommands.name: verbose
subCommands.description: Generates additional debug data when used with the test command. The following data is output to the console for each path tested:

subCommands.name: gateway_address
subCommands.description: If provided, defines the particular interface associated with this router that should be used to forward messages if the router is unable to find a destination for a message received on one of the router’s defined comm interfaces. The destination used for the selected comm gateway is defined on the comm itself.

subCommands.name: gateway
subCommands.description: If provided, defines the particular interface associated with this router that should be used to forward messages if the router is unable to find a destination for a message received on one of the router’s defined comm interfaces. The destination used for the selected comm gateway is defined on the comm itself.

subCommands.name: hop_limit
subCommands.description: Specifies the number of nodes/comms that a message may visit on the way to the destination before the message is simply discarded. Often referred to as time to live (TTL). The hop_limit applies to any messages initiated from this router’s interfaces. This value ensures that messages that may enter circular routing are eventually dropped.

subCommands.name: automated_interface_linking
subCommands.description: If set to true, all interfaces specified for this router will have connections created between members. This ensures that router interfaces are correctly represented as having direct connections to each other via the router hardware interface.

subCommands.name: use_default_protocol
subCommands.description: A convenience setting to determine if the router should use the default legacy routing protocol. True indicates to use this routing_protocol, false to remove it.

subCommands.name: use_multicast_protocol
subCommands.description: A convenience setting to determine if the router should use the default multicast routing protocol. True indicates to use this routing_protocol, false to remove it.

name: SAM_LAUNCH_COMPUTER_GENERATOR
description: Within this block are delineated the list of target track test conditions to be evaluated for successful missile intercept. Four different arrays are to be provided: lateral_offsets, altitudes, speeds, and ranges. Each of the four arrays may be set by using the following syntax: a) from <start-value> to <end-value> by <delta-value>, or b) a listing, such as <value-1> <value-2> <value-3> … <end-value>. All values must be in increasing order, but the intervals need not be even, and the from-to-by syntax and enumerated list may be used in combination.

subCommands.name: test_matrix
subCommands.description: Within this block are delineated the list of target track test conditions to be evaluated for successful missile intercept. Four different arrays are to be provided: lateral_offsets, altitudes, speeds, and ranges. Each of the four arrays may be set by using the following syntax: a) from <start-value> to <end-value> by <delta-value>, or b) a listing, such as <value-1> <value-2> <value-3> … <end-value>. All values must be in increasing order, but the intervals need not be even, and the from-to-by syntax and enumerated list may be used in combination.

subCommands.name: altitudes
subCommands.description: The altitudes at which tracks are evaluated for intercept. Format as given in test_matrix above.

subCommands.name: lateral_offsets
subCommands.description: The lateral_offsets at which tracks are evaluated for intercept. Format as given in test_matrix above.

subCommands.name: ranges
subCommands.description: The target ground ranges at which tracks are evaluated for intercept. Format as given in test_matrix above.

subCommands.name: speeds
subCommands.description: The speeds at which tracks are evaluated for intercept. Format as given in test_matrix above.

subCommands.name: post_generation_interpolation_tests
subCommands.description: For debug purposes only, and is optional. Inside this block one may place one or more lateral_offset, altitude, ground_range, and target_speed specifications. Each time the keyword ‘test’ appears, the most recent value of (offset, altitude, speed, range) is saved off as a test point, and stored into a test point array. After the launch computer is generated, each of these test points will be evaluated, and the corresponding time-of-flight value will be printed to the screen. The example given below saves off three points for testing.

subCommands.name: lateral_offset
subCommands.description: Specify the track lateral_offset of the interpolation test point.

subCommands.name: altitude
subCommands.description: Specify the track altitude of the interpolation test point.

subCommands.name: ground_range
subCommands.description: Specify the track ground_range of the interpolation test point.

subCommands.name: target_speed
subCommands.description: Specify the track target speed of the interpolation test point.

subCommands.name: test
subCommands.description: Save off the most recent values for (offset, altitude, range, and speed), and store them as a point to be interpolation tested. Results will be printed to the screen.

subCommands.name: re_parse_produced_input_file
subCommands.description: After generating and writing the launch computer, re-open the file and attempt to read it back in through normal stream input processing. The file is not checked by default.

subCommands.name: tracker_height
subCommands.description: Set the height above ground for a tracking radar. This is used in horizon masking calculations, which will disable weapon launch for a target engagement that is masked by curvature of earth. If no value is input for this parameter, horizon masking is not considered, and missile kinematics alone are used to calculate a launch envelope.

subCommands.name: tracker_name
subCommands.description: Alternate way to set the tracker height by specifying the sensor’s name. If a tracker height wasn’t specified and tracker name was, the tracker height is resolved from its definition. The specified sensor must be present on the launching platform.

subCommands.name: tracker_elevation_limits
subCommands.description: Set the minimum and maximum elevation angles at which the tracking radar will function. Target elevation angles outside these limits will inhibit weapon launch.

subCommands.name: effective_earth_radius
subCommands.description: Set the effective earth radius ratio. Must be greater than zero.

subCommands.name: test_matrix
subCommands.description: Within this block are delineated the list of target track test conditions to be evaluated for successful missile intercept. Four different arrays are to be provided: lateral_offsets, altitudes, speeds, and ranges. Each of the four arrays may be set by using the following syntax: a) from <start-value> to <end-value> by <delta-value>, or b) a listing, such as <value-1> <value-2> <value-3> … <end-value>. All values must be in increasing order, but the intervals need not be even, and the from-to-by syntax and enumerated list may be used in combination.

subCommands.name: altitudes
subCommands.description: The altitudes at which tracks are evaluated for intercept. Format as given in test_matrix above.

subCommands.name: lateral_offsets
subCommands.description: The lateral_offsets at which tracks are evaluated for intercept. Format as given in test_matrix above.

subCommands.name: ranges
subCommands.description: The target ground ranges at which tracks are evaluated for intercept. Format as given in test_matrix above.

subCommands.name: speeds
subCommands.description: The speeds at which tracks are evaluated for intercept. Format as given in test_matrix above.

subCommands.name: post_generation_interpolation_tests
subCommands.description: For debug purposes only, and is optional. Inside this block one may place one or more lateral_offset, altitude, ground_range, and target_speed specifications. Each time the keyword ‘test’ appears, the most recent value of (offset, altitude, speed, range) is saved off as a test point, and stored into a test point array. After the launch computer is generated, each of these test points will be evaluated, and the corresponding time-of-flight value will be printed to the screen. The example given below saves off three points for testing.

subCommands.name: lateral_offset
subCommands.description: Specify the track lateral_offset of the interpolation test point.

subCommands.name: altitude
subCommands.description: Specify the track altitude of the interpolation test point.

subCommands.name: ground_range
subCommands.description: Specify the track ground_range of the interpolation test point.

subCommands.name: target_speed
subCommands.description: Specify the track target speed of the interpolation test point.

subCommands.name: test
subCommands.description: Save off the most recent values for (offset, altitude, range, and speed), and store them as a point to be interpolation tested. Results will be printed to the screen.

subCommands.name: re_parse_produced_input_file
subCommands.description: After generating and writing the launch computer, re-open the file and attempt to read it back in through normal stream input processing. The file is not checked by default.

subCommands.name: tracker_height
subCommands.description: Set the height above ground for a tracking radar. This is used in horizon masking calculations, which will disable weapon launch for a target engagement that is masked by curvature of earth. If no value is input for this parameter, horizon masking is not considered, and missile kinematics alone are used to calculate a launch envelope.

subCommands.name: tracker_name
subCommands.description: Alternate way to set the tracker height by specifying the sensor’s name. If a tracker height wasn’t specified and tracker name was, the tracker height is resolved from its definition. The specified sensor must be present on the launching platform.

subCommands.name: tracker_elevation_limits
subCommands.description: Set the minimum and maximum elevation angles at which the tracking radar will function. Target elevation angles outside these limits will inhibit weapon launch.

subCommands.name: effective_earth_radius
subCommands.description: Set the effective earth radius ratio. Must be greater than zero.

subCommands.name: end_azimuth

subCommands.name: start_elevation

subCommands.name: end_elevation

name: Script Commands
description: Controls whether a trace of script method calls will be written to standard output. This can be very useful for debugging complex scripts. If enabled, a line indicating the time, platform, platform part name and script name is written prior to calling the method. Upon return from the method another line is written which contains the function return value.

subCommands.name: script_call_trace
subCommands.description: Controls whether a trace of script method calls will be written to standard output. This can be very useful for debugging complex scripts. If enabled, a line indicating the time, platform, platform part name and script name is written prior to calling the method. Upon return from the method another line is written which contains the function return value.

subCommands.name: script_debug_writes
subCommands.description: Controls whether the script debug write statements write_d and writeln_d are executed. If enabled, write_d and writeln_d statements are executed.

subCommands.name: script_abort_on_null_references
subCommands.description: When a script method is called with an invalid object or argument, an error is printed to the screen. When this option is enabled, the application will also terminate immediately. This command is only available in a global context.

subCommands.name: script_abort_on_assert
subCommands.description: When a call to assert() in script fails, the application will usually abort. Setting this option to ‘off’ will still print an error but will not abort the application.

subCommands.name: script
subCommands.description: Defines a script.

subCommands.name: script_variables
subCommands.description: Allows users to declare a set of variables that are accessible to scripts within a given context. For example, if the script_variables command is used inside the platform command, then all scripts defined within that platform have access to the variables that are defined. In addition, any scriptable platform parts can access their parents variables by using the extern keyword.

subCommands.name: script_interface
subCommands.description: Configures the scripting system. Multiple script_interface blocks may be provided. If the same subcommand is specified in multiple blocks then the last value given will be used

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: Tells the compiler to produce a source listing and any errors that may occur during compilation (by default debug output is turned off).

subCommands.name: no_debug
subCommands.description: Tells the compiler not to produce the source and detailed error listing. The compiler will still display a simple message if an error occurs during compilation.

subCommands.name: script
subCommands.description: Defines a script that is callable by all platforms in the simulation.

subCommands.name: no_debug

subCommands.description: Defines a script that is callable by all platforms in the simulation.

subCommands.name: uncloneable
subCommands.description: Specify that instances of this script_struct cannot be cloned.

subCommands.name: uncloneable
subCommands.description: Specify that instances of this script_struct cannot be cloned.

name: Scripted
description: Define a script that is executed when the event is initialized. This initialization occurs when the mission event is scheduled, which is either when the mission sequence is scheduled for the first event of a mission sequence, or immediately upon completion of the previous event of a mission sequence.

subCommands.name: on_initialize
subCommands.description: Define a script that is executed when the event is initialized. This initialization occurs when the mission event is scheduled, which is either when the mission sequence is scheduled for the first event of a mission sequence, or immediately upon completion of the previous event of a mission sequence.

subCommands.name: on_update
subCommands.description: Define a script that executes with the update_interval and duration of the event, starting from the time at which the event’s constraint is first met. If duration is not defined the script is always executed once. If the is_complete script is defined and the event is finite, it is also updated at subsequent constraint times, until the is_complete script returns true. Alternately, if duration is defined, the event will execute at the specified update_rate for the given duration (see examples, below).

subCommands.name: on_complete
subCommands.description: Define a script that executes on completion of a mission event.

subCommands.name: is_complete
subCommands.description: Define a script that determines whether the script event is complete. If false, the event continues to execute; if true, the event is considered complete, and the on_complete script is called. If defined, this script is called immediately after each event update, and it overrides any duration command.

subCommands.name: port
subCommands.description: Defines a port that ship traffic originates and terminates at.

subCommands.name: position
subCommands.description: Defines the location and size of the port. The third argument is used as a diameter so ships entering the port will end up inside of a circle with the given diameter, centered about the specified latitude and longitude.

subCommands.name: port_route
subCommands.description: Defines the route ship traffic uses for entering and exiting the port. This gives the ability to navigate ships around obstacles after leaving the main shipping lane. Specify multiple positions to build up a path entering the port. When ships leave a port they use the reverse of the defined port route.

subCommands.name: position
subCommands.description: Defines a waypoint along the route into the port. The third argument is used as a diameter so ships traveling along the port route will have a random path inside of the circle with the given diameter, centered about the specified latitude and longitude.

subCommands.name: local_traffic_region
subCommands.description: The region where local traffic from this port will travel to. The fraction specifies the fraction of traffic from this port that goes to this region.

subCommands.name: departure_interval
subCommands.description: Specifies the ship departure interval from the port.

subCommands.name: use_all_lanes
subCommands.description: Ship traffic departing and terminating at the port will use all available ship lane_s.

subCommands.name: lane
subCommands.description: Specifies a lane ship traffic can use. The weighting factor is used to spread traffic amongst the various lanes.

subCommands.name: position
subCommands.description: Specifies a point of the lane. The third argument is used as a diameter so ships traveling along the shipping lane will have a random path inside of the circle with the given diameter, centered about the specified latitude and longitude.

subCommands.name: ship
subCommands.description: Defines the attributes of a specific ship type.

subCommands.name: fraction
subCommands.description: Controls how much ship traffic will use this ship type.

subCommands.name: mean_speed
subCommands.description: The mean speed the ship traffic will travel at.

subCommands.name: sigma_speed
subCommands.description: The standard deviation for the ship’s speed.

subCommands.name: local_traffic
subCommands.description: Defines the shipping traffic that will leave a port and head to a local_traffic_region. The fractional-quantity is the percentage of ships that leave a port, which are going to a local region. This fraction and the departure_traffic fraction must sum to 1.0.

subCommands.name: ship
subCommands.description: Defines the attributes of a specific ship type.

subCommands.name: fraction
subCommands.description: Controls how much ship traffic will use this ship type.

subCommands.name: mean_loiter_time
subCommands.description: Specifies how long the ship type will loiter in a local_traffic_region.

subCommands.name: sigma_loiter_time
subCommands.description: The standard deviation of the ship’s loiter time.

subCommands.name: loiter_route
subCommands.description: The ship type will use the specified route for its loiter. More than 1 loiter_route can be entered.

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: Enable extra debugging output.

subCommands.name: detached
subCommands.description: For formations defined in the initial conditions, this will cause this formation to not be attached to its parent. After initialization any attached formation will have its members placed into the correct positions relative to the formation leader. The detached status on a formation also effects the way formation commands are propagated down through the hierarchy. See WsfFormationCommand.

subCommands.name: offset
subCommands.description: Specify the offset of the formation from its parent. This is the means by which the initial relative positioning of the members of a formation is specified. The offset is given as a triplet of a range from the reference point, a relative bearing from the direction of travel of the leader, and a vertical offset (or stack). For example, the following offset would be the point 100 m to the right of the reference point and at 1 m higher altitude.

subCommands.name: unit
subCommands.description: Define a unit sub-formation. See Unit Formation.

subCommands.name: lead
subCommands.description: Specify that the following unit sub-formation is to be the lead sub-formation of this section. Sections defined in input files must have one of their sub-formations designated as the lead sub-formation.

subCommands.name: ignore
subCommands.description: Indicates the sensor should ignore detection attempts against objects that are a member of the specified category. This command may be specified multiple times to ignore multiple categories.

subCommands.name: ignore_domain
subCommands.syntax: ignore_domain [ land | air | surface | subsurface | space ]
subCommands.description: Indicates the sensor should ignore detection attempts against platforms or objects contained on platforms that are of the specified spatial domain. This command may be specified multiple times to ignore multiple domain.

subCommands.name: ignore_side
subCommands.description: Indicates the sensor should ignore detection attempts against platforms or objects contained on platforms that are of the specified side. This command may be specified multiple times to ignore multiple sides.

subCommands.name: ignore_same_side
subCommands.description: Indicates the sensor should ignore detection attempts against platforms or objects contained on platforms that are on the same side of the platform to which the sensor is attached.

subCommands.name: ignore_nothing
subCommands.description: Has the effect of canceling the effect of any previous ignore, ignore_domain, ignore_side and ignore_same_side commands. This is useful if one wants to reuse a sensor definition with embedded ‘ignore’ commands but wished to eliminate or change what is ignored.

subCommands.name: message_length
subCommands.description: Specifies the logical length assigned to the track messages that are created from the sensor.

subCommands.name: message_priority
subCommands.description: Specifies the priority assigned to the track messages that are created from the sensor.

subCommands.name: modifier_category
subCommands.description: The category that maps to the Zone-based attenuation value defined in the zone_set. Setting this value tells the sensor to evaluate zones for attenuation.

subCommands.name: mode_template
subCommands.description: Defines the default values for the modes of the sensor. When a new mode is defined it is first populated with the values from the mode template. This is useful when a sensor has multiple modes and the parameters for each mode are the same with the exception of a few values.

subCommands.name: mode
subCommands.description: Defines a mode, which is nothing more than a selectable set of parameters. The initial or default values of a mode are defined by the mode_template (if provided).

subCommands.name: selection_mode
subCommands.description: Indicates if the sensor supports the simultaneous operation of multiple modes.

subCommands.name: initial_mode
subCommands.description: The operation of this command depends on if selection_mode is single or multiple.

subCommands.name: mode_select_delay
subCommands.description: Specifies the delay when selecting modes.

subCommands.name: OnSensorDetectionAttempt
subCommands.description: Defines an optional script that imposes additional detection constraints on a sensor model. This script is invoked immediately after a detection attempt occurs but prior to any SENSOR_DETECTION_ATTEMPT events in the observer. As a result, the WsfSensorInteraction parameter includes any relevant calculations from the sensor’s inbuilt detection checks and represents what the result would have been if this script was not defined.

subCommands.name: required_pd
subCommands.description: Specifies the constant ‘required_pd’ value to be used if the value of the global simulation command use_constant_required_pd was specified as true. This is applicable only for sensors which implement probabilistic detectors (e.g., The optional Marcum-Swerling detector in WSF_RADAR_SENSOR).

subCommands.name: cue_mode

subCommands.name: elevation_cue_limits

subCommands.name: elevation_cue_rate
subCommands.description: Specifies the angular velocities to be employed when slewing the part to satisfy a cueing request. This is primarily used for modeling systems that track single target. It is not used for scanning systems and should not be used for multiple-target tracking systems.

subCommands.name: lunar_exclusion_angle
subCommands.description: This sensor will not detect targets if the angle between its line-of-sight with the moon’s limb and the target is less than this value.

subCommands.name: target_solar_illumination_angle

subCommands.name: solar_elevation_at_target

subCommands.name: enable_moon_los_block
subCommands.description: If set to true, this sensor will not detect targets whose line-of-sight is blocked by the moon.

subCommands.name: update_interval
subCommands.description: This value is required when the scheduler is assigned a scheduler-type of physical_scan or sector_scan. It is used in conjunction with the frame_time value defined within the final mode that is read in from the input file for the sensor in order to calculate and physically sweep sectors for radar detections. For example, if the final frame-time value, which is read during the input loading sequence, is set to 20 sec, and if the update_interval is set to 2 sec, then 10 sectors are needed to sweep through 360 degrees during the 20-sec frame. For this example, each sector would cover 36 degrees of azimuth during each 2-sec update_interval.

subCommands.name: revisit_time

subCommands.name: dwell_time

subCommands.name: disables_search

name: Simulation Control Commands
description: Specify the number of simulation seconds for each second of wall clock time for a real-time simulation.

subCommands.name: clock_rate
subCommands.description: Specify the number of simulation seconds for each second of wall clock time for a real-time simulation.

subCommands.name: delta_universal_time
subCommands.description: Specify the difference between universal time (UT1, defined by the earth’s rotation), and Coordinated Universal Time (UTC, defined with a fixed offset to atomic clocks).

subCommands.name: delta_atomic_time
subCommands.description: Specify the fixed offset in integer seconds between atomic time (TAI) and Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). This is equivalent to the cumulative number of leap seconds inserted into the calendar until the start_epoch.

subCommands.name: end_time
subCommands.description: Specify the end time of the simulation.

subCommands.name: enumerate
subCommands.description: This command ‘enumerates’ (or lists) the registered type names of the specified list to the indicated file. <list-name> must be one of platform_types, sensor_types, processor_types, comm_types or dictionary. The format of the resulting file is a header line identifying the list followed by one line for each type where the line contains a unique number that represents the string followed by the actual string, enclosed in single quotes.

subCommands.name: frame_rate
subCommands.description: Specify the frame rate for the frame-stepped simulation executive. Either this command or frame_time can be used to define the length of time allocated for each frame.

subCommands.name: frame_time
subCommands.description: Specify the frame time for the frame-stepped simulation executive. Either this command or frame_rate can be used to define the length of time allocated for each frame.

subCommands.name: minimum_mover_timestep
subCommands.description: This is applicable only for event-stepped simulations. The value specifies the minimum amount of time that must elapse between two successive position updates for a given platform. During the course of a simulation, requests are made to platforms to update their position to the current simulation time. A position update for a given platform will be ignored if the elapsed time since the last position update is less than the value specified by this command.

subCommands.name: on_platform_injection
subCommands.description: Defines a script allowing the user to prevent or delay the injection of a platform. This script is executed prior to adding any platform to the simulation. true should be returned to continue adding the platform normally. false should be returned to prevent the platform from being injected. WsfPlatform.SetCreationTime may be used in this script to delay the creation of the platform.

subCommands.name: platform_availability
subCommands.description: This command is used to specify the availability of platforms when added during simulation initialization (i.e., it does not apply to platforms added after simulation initialization). One can define probabilistic constraints based on platform name or type or can define geographic constraints based on exclusion or inclusion within zones.

subCommands.name: quantitative_track_quality
subCommands.description: Specify whether track quality is to be computed based on quantitative simulation parameters, such as sensor measurement errors and target behavior models. If disabled, only the input track_quality information is used, and for a given sensor’s tracks, it generally does not change during the course of the simulation.

subCommands.name: random_seed
subCommands.description: Specify the random seed for the simulation. This command should typically be used when you want to run a single iteration with a particular random seed. For running multiple runs within a single execution of the program, consider the use of the generate_random_seeds command documented in Monte Carlo Iteration or the random_seeds defined below.

subCommands.name: random_seeds
subCommands.description: Specifies the random seeds for each run of Monte Carlo Iteration collection of runs. This command implicitly defines initial_run_number to be 1 and final_run_number to the number of seeds entered. The values of initial_run_number and final_run_number may be subsequently redefined and will be limited by the number of entries in the list. If an empty list is provided then only a single iteration will be run using the random seed defined by random_seed (or the default random seed if not specified).

subCommands.name: random_seed_time
subCommands.description: Use the clock to set the random seed for this run. This command should typically be used when you want to run a single iteration where the seed is not determined beforehand.

subCommands.name: randomize_radar_frequencies
subCommands.description: Forces the initial frequency to use at simulation startup to be chosen randomly for WSF_RADAR_SENSOR sensor types with alternate_frequency, frequency_channels or frequency_list defined.

subCommands.name: realtime
subCommands.description: Specify if the simulation is to run in real-time or non-real-time mode.

subCommands.name: timing_method
subCommands.description: Set the underlying timing method used when running real time. <method> may be Default:, performance_counter, system_time, or tick_count.

subCommands.name: simulation_name
subCommands.description: Specify a name to identify the simulation within Warlock and Mystic.

subCommands.name: start_date
subCommands.description: Specify the date that corresponds to the start of the simulation clock.

subCommands.name: start_time
subCommands.description: Specify the time of day, referenced to UT midnight and using a 24-hour clock, that corresponds to the start of the simulation clock.

subCommands.name: start_time_now
subCommands.description: Specify that the simulation start time will be synchronized to the system clock time.

subCommands.name: start_epoch
subCommands.description: Specify the epoch that corresponds to the start of the simulation clock.

subCommands.name: use_constant_required_pd
subCommands.description: This command is applicable only to sensors which implement probabilistic detectors (e.g., the optional Marcum-Swerling detection in WSF_RADAR_SENSOR). For each detection attempt, the simulation will determine the required probability of detection (required Pd) that is necessary to declare a successful detection. If the value of this command is false (the default), the required Pd will be determined randomly. If the value is true then the required Pd will be the value of the required_pd from the definition in the sensor mode (default of 0.5).

subCommands.name: use_default_radar_frequencies
subCommands.description: Force the use of the frequency for WSF_RADAR_SENSOR with alternate_frequency, frequency_channels or frequency_list defined instead of selecting from these lists.

subCommands.name: multi_thread
subCommands.description: This is an alias for ‘multi_threading on’.

subCommands.name: multi_threading
subCommands.description: Specifies whether to use multi-threading capabilities or not in an event-stepped or framed-step simulation. See the Multi-Threading Commands opening message in this section for more information on multi-threading capabilities.

subCommands.name: number_of_threads
subCommands.description: Specify the number of worker threads when multi-threading is enabled.

subCommands.name: multi_thread_update_interval
subCommands.description: Specify the multi-threading update time for the event-stepped simulation executive. Either this command or multi_thread_update_rate can be used to define the length of time allocated for each threading update cycle. This time is multiplied by a base rate for the individual platform and sensor updates via the platform_update_multiplier and sensor_update_multiplier, respectively.

subCommands.name: multi_thread_update_rate
subCommands.description: Specify the multi-threading update rate for the event-stepped simulation executive. Either this command or multi_thread_update_interval can be used to define the length of time allocated for each threading update cycle. This time is divided by a base rate for the individual platform and sensor updates via the platform_update_multiplier and sensor_update_multiplier, respectively.

subCommands.name: platform_update_multiplier
subCommands.description: Specify the platform update time multiplier in an event-stepped simulation executive that is multi-threaded. This multiplier effectively increases the multi_thread_update_interval in which thread updates are performed on the platforms by integer values.

subCommands.name: sensor_update_multiplier
subCommands.description: Specify the sensor update time multiplier in a event-stepped simulation executive that is multi-threaded. This multiplier effectively increases the multi_thread_update_interval in which thread updates are performed on the sensors by integer values.

subCommands.name: sensor_update_break_time
subCommands.description: Specify the sensor thread update break time in a realtime executive that is multi-threaded. This time will cause the sensor updates to end when the thread runtime is equal to or greater than this value.

subCommands.name: process_priority
subCommands.description: Specify the Windows OS process priority for realtime operation of simulation.

name: SixDOF Aerodynamics Data
description: The RB6 geometric data offers two modes: wing-based or reference area. When using wing-based mode, the wing_chord_ft, wing_span_ft, and wing_area_sqft should be specified. When using reference area mode, the ref_area_sqft should be specified. PM6 vehicles do not incorporate chord or span information, and so require only ref_area_sqft.

subCommands.name: aero_data
subCommands.description: The RB6 geometric data offers two modes: wing-based or reference area. When using wing-based mode, the wing_chord_ft, wing_span_ft, and wing_area_sqft should be specified. When using reference area mode, the ref_area_sqft should be specified. PM6 vehicles do not incorporate chord or span information, and so require only ref_area_sqft.

subCommands.name: wing_chord_ft
subCommands.description: The mean chord of the wing measured in feet. This should be used along with wing_span_ft and wing_area_sqft.

subCommands.name: wing_span_ft
subCommands.description: The wing span of the wing measured in feet. This should be used along with wing_chord_ft and wing_area_sqft.

subCommands.name: wing_area_sqft
subCommands.description: The area of the wing measured in square feet. This should be used along with wing_chord_ft and wing_span_ft.

subCommands.name: ref_area_sqft
subCommands.description: The aerodynamic reference area of the vehicle measured in square feet. If this is used, wing_chord_ft, wing_span_ft and wing_area_sqft should not be used.

subCommands.name: use_reduced_frequency
subCommands.description: This should be true when using the “reduced frequency” stability derivatives. If false, the rate derivatives (e.g. cLq_alpha_mach_table, cnr_mach_table) will be multiplied by their corresponding angular rates. If true, the rate derivatives will instead be multiplied by a non-dimensional reduced frequency. For pitching moment and lift coefficient derivatives, the reduced frequency is calculated as the angular rate times the wing_chord_ft divided by twice the speed. All other coefficient derivatives use wing_span_ft instead of chord. See P6DOF Theory for more information.

subCommands.name: aero_center_x
subCommands.description: The aerodynamic center (x-axis) of the vehicle relative to the reference point in object coordinates. This “aero-center” is the “aerodynamic reference point” at which aerodynamic forces and moments will be calculated. The typical definition of aerodynamic center (as it relates to longitudinal stability) is the location at which the moment does not change regardless of the angle of attack. Thus, the pitching moment remains constant at that particular point. Hence, the aerodynamic center, rather than the center of pressure, is used in the analysis of longitudinal stability.

subCommands.name: aero_center_y
subCommands.description: The aerodynamic center (y-axis) of the vehicle relative to the reference point in object coordinates.

subCommands.name: aero_center_z
subCommands.description: The aerodynamic center (z-axis) of the vehicle relative to the reference point in object coordinates.

subCommands.name: cL_alpha_beta_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 3-dimensional regular_table that outputs the lift coefficient (cL) based on Mach, angle of attack (alpha), and angle of sideslip (beta), with a table order of Mach-alpha-beta-value.

subCommands.name: cLq_alpha_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 3-dimensional regular_table that outputs the lift coefficient (cL) based on Mach, angle of attack (alpha), and pitch rate (q), with a table order of Mach-alpha-q-value.

subCommands.name: cL_alphadot_alpha_mach_table

subCommands.name: flaps_dcL_mach_table

subCommands.name: spoilers_dcL_mach_table

subCommands.name: aero_component
subCommands.description: The use of aero components can be simple, such as having three “generic” yaw, pitch and roll aero components, or can be more complex and realistic, such as having sixteen specific components: LeftAileron, RightAileron, LeftStabilator, RightStabilator, LeftRudder, RightRudder, LeftSpeedbrake, RightSpeedbrake, LeftFlap, RightFlap, LeftSpoiler, RightSpoiler, NoseLandingGear, LeftLandingGear, RightLandingGear, and ArrestingHook. During runtime, the position of aero components is controlled by the SixDOF Flight Control System Definition.

subCommands.name: type

subCommands.name: ref_area_sqft
subCommands.description: This is the reference aerodynamic area for the aero component. If this is not specified, the wing_area_sqft defined in aero_data is used.

subCommands.description: This is a 2-dimensional regular_table that outputs the drag coefficient (cd) based on the Mach and the angle of the control surface, with a table order of Mach-angle-value. This derivative should be used when drag is a function of both alpha and beta. (Although this function does not include either alpha or beta, it is more appropriate than either the pro-alpha or pro-beta derivatives.) When this derivative is used, cd_angle_alpha_mach_table and cd_angle_beta_mach_table should not be used.

subCommands.name: cy_angle_beta_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 3-dimensional regular_table that outputs the side force coefficient (cy) based on the Mach, angle of sideslip (beta), and angle of the control surface, with a table order of Mach-beta-angle-value..

subCommands.name: cm_angle_alpha_mach_table

subCommands.name: cmq_angle_mach_table

subCommands.name: cn_angle_beta_mach_table

subCommands.name: cnr_angle_mach_table

subCommands.name: cl_angle_alpha_beta_table
subCommands.description: This is a 3-dimensional regular_table that outputs the roll coefficient (cl) based on the angle of the attack (alpha), the angle of slideslip (beta) and the angle of the control surface, with a table order of alpha-beta-angle-value.

subCommands.name: clp_angle_mach_table

subCommands.name: clq_angle_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is a 2-dimensional regular_table that outputs the roll damping coefficient due to pitch rate (clq) based on Mach and the angle of the control surface.

subCommands.name: clr_angle_mach_table

subCommands.name: autopilot_config
subCommands.description: The autopilot_config block is structured as follows:

subCommands.name: vertical_middle_loop_rate_factor
subCommands.description: This specifies how many times the vertical channel inner-loop activates before the vertical channel middle-loop activates.

subCommands.name: vertical_outer_loop_rate_factor
subCommands.description: This specifies how many times the vertical channel middle-loop activates before the vertical channel outer-loop activates.

subCommands.name: lateral_middle_loop_rate_factor
subCommands.description: This specifies how many times the lateral channel inner-loop activates before the lateral channel middle-loop activates.

subCommands.name: lateral_outer_loop_rate_factor
subCommands.description: This specifies how many times the lateral channel middle-loop activates before the lateral channel outer-loop activates.

subCommands.name: speed_middle_loop_rate_factor
subCommands.description: This specifies how many times the speed channel inner-loop activates before the speed channel middle-loop activates.

subCommands.name: speed_outer_loop_rate_factor
subCommands.description: This specifies how many times the speed channel middle-loop activates before the speed channel outer-loop activates.

subCommands.name: control_method
subCommands.description: This sets the control method. There are two main methods – bank-to-turn and yaw-to-turn. Bank-to-turn involves banking/rolling in order to perform a turn, like a normal aircraft. Yaw-to-turn involves simply yawing to perform a turn – no rolling/banking is used. The command string should be one of the following:

subCommands.name: use_legacy_beta
subCommands.description: This enables/disables the use of the legacy_beta flag. This should be set to false when the new/improved beta calculations are desired. For example, Mover Creator uses the new beta calculations, so data files created by Mover Creator always set the use_legacy_beta command to false.

subCommands.name: min_taxi_turn_radius
subCommands.description: The defines the minimum taxi turning radius that will be used by the autopilot when performing taxi ground operations.

subCommands.name: use_simple_yaw_damper
subCommands.description: If true, a very “simple” (but not realistic) yaw damper action will be used to zero any sideslip (beta), making the RB6 more like a 5DOF. This will negate any sideslip, and so should only be used for bank-to-turn objects such as fixed-wing aircraft.

subCommands.name: update_interval
subCommands.description: This specifies the update rate of the PID. This is optional and, when defined, takes priority over the loop rate factors defined above. This limits the update rate from below and does not trigger a mover update.

subCommands.name: kp
subCommands.description: This specifies the proportional gain of the PID. When not defined, the gain will be zero.

subCommands.name: ki
subCommands.description: This specifies the integral gain of the PID. When not defined, the gain will be zero.

subCommands.name: kd
subCommands.description: This specifies the derivative gain of the PID. When not defined, the gain will be zero.

subCommands.name: max_error_accum
subCommands.description: This limits the maximum integrated error accumulation to the specified value. If not defined, no limit will be used.

subCommands.name: low_pass_alpha
subCommands.description: This specifies the value for the low-pass filter alpha for the derivative gain.

subCommands.name: ignore_large_error_accum
subCommands.description: This specifies that the PID will not accumulate integrated error if the current error value is greater than the specified value.

subCommands.name: ignore_small_error_accum
subCommands.description: This specifies that the PID will not accumulate integrated error if the current error value is less than the specified value.

subCommands.name: kt_anti_windup_gain
subCommands.description: This specifies the Kt anti-windup gain of the PID. When not defined, the gain will be zero.

subCommands.name: control_value
subCommands.description: This specifies the “control value” for which the PID parameters are used. The value is specified in lbs/ft^2 of dynamic pressure. The PID will interpolate between the appropriate control_value pairs based on the current dynamic pressure.

subCommands.name: afterburner_threshold
subCommands.description: This specifies the value above which afterburner will be used instead of limiting to military power.

subCommands.name: speedbrake_threshold
subCommands.description: This specifies the value below which the speed brake will be used to help slow down.

subCommands.name: pitch_gload_min
subCommands.description: This specifies the minimum pitch g-load value.

subCommands.name: pitch_gload_max
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum pitch g-load value.

subCommands.name: alpha_min
subCommands.description: This specifies the minimum angle of attack (alpha) in degrees.

subCommands.name: alpha_max
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum angle of attack (alpha) in degrees.

subCommands.name: pitch_rate_min
subCommands.description: This specifies the minimum pitch rate in degrees/sec.

subCommands.name: pitch_rate_max
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum pitch rate in degrees/sec.

subCommands.name: vert_speed_min
subCommands.description: This specifies the minimum vertical speed in ft/minute.

subCommands.name: vert_speed_max
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum vertical speed in ft/minute.

subCommands.name: yaw_gload_max
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum yaw g-load.

subCommands.name: beta_max
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum sideslip angle (beta) in degrees.

subCommands.name: yaw_rate_max
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum yaw rate in degrees/sec.

subCommands.name: roll_rate_max
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum roll rate in degrees/sec.

subCommands.name: bank_angle_max
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum bank angle in degrees.

subCommands.name: forward_accel_min
subCommands.description: This specifies the minimum forward acceleration in g’s.

subCommands.name: forward_accel_max
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum forward acceleration in g’s.

subCommands.name: taxi_speed_max_fps
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum taxi speed in feet/sec.

subCommands.name: taxi_yaw_rate_max
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum taxi yaw rate in degrees/sec.

subCommands.name: turn_roll_in_multiplier
subCommands.description: This is a multiplier that can shorten (less than than 1) or extend (greater than 1) the time/distance used when turning when following a route (waypoints).

subCommands.name: route_allowable_angle_error
subCommands.description: This specifies the angular error that is tolerated when rolling-out on a turn when following a route (waypoints). A larger value will allow the vehicle to consider the turn to be complete and switch to route segment control rather than continuing to use turn control.

It is important to define Control Signal Modifiers before they are referenced in the Control Surfaces and Components blocks.

subCommands.name: scalar_gain
subCommands.description: The scalar gain consists of a name and a gain value. Once defined, a scalar gain can be used repeatedly within the control_surface, control_value, and control_boolean blocks to scale a control signal.

subCommands.name: gain

subCommands.name: clamp_gain

subCommands.name: min_clamp

subCommands.name: max_clamp

subCommands.name: control_surface
subCommands.description: This defines a “control surface” or other component that can produce aerodynamic effects on the platform. Control surfaces include ailerons, elevators, elevons, rudders, spoilers, speedbrakes, etc. but also include things like landing gear, which can produce drag. See Sample Control Surface for an example of a control_surface block.

subCommands.name: min_angle
subCommands.description: This sets the minimum angle of this control surface.

subCommands.name: max_angle
subCommands.description: This sets the maximum angle of this control surface.

subCommands.name: current_angle

subCommands.name: inputs
subCommands.description: Inputs provide a means to modify a “control input/signal” from the active pilot object. If multiple inputs blocks are used, the output from each block is summed with the other inputs for a given control_surface. This can provide a means to “mix” control inputs/signals to drive a particular control surface. For example, an elevon may mix signals from stick_right and stick_back inputs to allow the elevon to be used for both pitch and roll forces/moments.

subCommands.name: control_input

subCommands.name: modifier

subCommands.name: angle_mapping_table
subCommands.description: This table provides a means to “shape” the mapping of input to control surface angle. In many situations, a non-linear mapping will be used, with a reduced slope near zero and increased slope near the endpoints. This often improves the “feel” of controls and provides more control sensitivity near the zero point. Data in the table is normalized input mapping to a control surface angle in degrees.

subCommands.name: max_value

subCommands.name: current_angle

subCommands.name: control_boolean
subCommands.description: This defines a “control boolean” that can be used to drive “button”, “trigger”, and “switch” types of controls on the platform. A control boolean’s output is either true (on) or false (off).

subCommands.name: current_value
subCommands.description: This should be ‘0’ if the control boolean is false (off) or ‘1’ if the control boolean is true (on).

subCommands.name: threshold_value

name: SixDOF Sequencers
description: A sequencer block has an identifier, which is the string argument after ‘sequencer’. This identifier must be unique within the vehicle type. The sequencer block has to include at least one Sequencer Actions, which is the action the sequencer shall perform when it is activated. The sequencer block may include one or more Sequencer Events, if no Sequencer Events are provided the sequencer may only be activated through the WsfSixDOF_Mover.ActivateSequencer script function. The sequencer block may include one or more Nested Sequencers which will be used once the containing sequencer has been activated – this allows for sequential events, where the second event cannot occur until the first event has occurred.

subCommands.name: sequencer
subCommands.description: A sequencer block has an identifier, which is the string argument after ‘sequencer’. This identifier must be unique within the vehicle type. The sequencer block has to include at least one Sequencer Actions, which is the action the sequencer shall perform when it is activated. The sequencer block may include one or more Sequencer Events, if no Sequencer Events are provided the sequencer may only be activated through the WsfSixDOF_Mover.ActivateSequencer script function. The sequencer block may include one or more Nested Sequencers which will be used once the containing sequencer has been activated – this allows for sequential events, where the second event cannot occur until the first event has occurred.

subCommands.name: event_timer
subCommands.description: This event is based on reaching the specified time. The timer will begin counting once the sequencer is being tested. For top-level sequencers, this is equivalent to event_lifetime but if the sequencer is nested, its counter will not begin running until its parent sequencer has been activated.

subCommands.name: event_timer_int_msec
subCommands.description: This event is based on reaching the specified time, which is an integer number of milliseconds. The timer will begin counting once the sequencer is being tested. For top-level sequencers, this is equivalent to event_lifetime_int_msec but if the sequencer is nested, its counter will not begin running until its parent sequencer has been activated.

subCommands.name: event_timer_int_nanosec
subCommands.description: This event is based on reaching the specified time, which is an integer number of nanoseconds. The timer will begin counting once the sequencer is being tested. For top-level sequencers, this is equivalent to event_lifetime_int_nanosec but if the sequencer is nested, its counter will not begin running until its parent sequencer has been activated.

subCommands.name: event_lifetime
subCommands.description: This event is based on reaching the specified lifetime. The lifetime timer begins counting once the platform is active (alive). This timer is different from the event_timer since it uses a platform-centric timer as opposed to a sequencer-centric timer.

subCommands.name: event_lifetime_int_msec
subCommands.description: This event is based on reaching the specified lifetime, which is an integer number of milliseconds. The lifetime timer begins counting once the platform is active (alive). This timer is different from the event_timer_int_msec since it uses a platform-centric timer as opposed to a sequencer-centric timer.

subCommands.name: event_lifetime_int_nanosec
subCommands.description: This event is based on reaching the specified lifetime, which is an integer number of nanoseconds. The lifetime timer begins counting once the platform is active (alive). This timer is different from the event_timer_int_nanosec since it uses a platform-centric timer as opposed to a sequencer-centric timer.

subCommands.name: event_above_alt
subCommands.description: This event is based on the platform being above the specified altitude (MSL).

subCommands.name: event_below_alt
subCommands.description: This event is based on the platform being below the specified altitude (MSL).

subCommands.name: event_dynamic_pressure_above
subCommands.description: This event is based on the platform having a dynamic pressure above the specified value.

subCommands.name: event_dynamic_pressure_below
subCommands.description: This event is based on the platform having a dynamic pressure below the specified value.

subCommands.name: event_static_pressure_above
subCommands.description: This event is based on the platform having a static pressure above the specified value.

subCommands.name: event_static_pressure_below
subCommands.description: This event is based on the platform having a static pressure below the specified value.

subCommands.name: event_fuel_percent_below
subCommands.description: Specify the fuel value as a normalized number (50% is 0.50). This event is based on the fuel level in the “main tank” being below the specified value. The main tank is considered to be the first tank specified in the propulsion_data block.

subCommands.name: event_ground_distance
subCommands.description: This event is based on the platform being beyond the specified distance (great circle) from the point at which it started.

subCommands.name: event_nx_above
subCommands.description: This event is based on the x-acceleration, known as Nx, (in body coordinates) being above the specified value.

subCommands.name: event_nx_below
subCommands.description: This event is based on the y-acceleration, known as Nx, (in body coordinates) being below the specified value.

subCommands.name: event_ny_above
subCommands.description: This event is based on the y-acceleration, known as Ny, (in body coordinates) being above the specified value.

subCommands.name: event_ny_below
subCommands.description: This event is based on the y-acceleration, known as Ny, (in body coordinates) being below the specified value.

subCommands.name: event_nz_above
subCommands.description: This event is based on the z-acceleration, known as Nz, (in body coordinates) being above the specified value.

subCommands.name: event_nz_below
subCommands.description: This event is based on the z-acceleration, known as Nz, (in body coordinates) being below the specified value.

subCommands.name: event_released_from_parent
subCommands.description: This event is based on the platform being newly released from its parent.

subCommands.name: event_manual_input_trigger
subCommands.description: This event allows a trigger pulled input from the P6Net interface to activate.

subCommands.name: event_manual_input_button
subCommands.description: This event allows an input button down from the P6Net interface to activate.

subCommands.name: event_manual_input_button_released
subCommands.description: This event allows an input button release from the P6Net interface to activate.

subCommands.name: event_boolean_input
subCommands.description: This event is based on a control_boolean within flight_controls being true. This allows an event to be controlled by a ManualPilot or SyntheticPilot, for example.

subCommands.name: event_null

subCommands.name: all_events
subCommands.description: This flag indicates that the sequencer will be activated only if all events for the sequencer are true.

subCommands.name: action_null

subCommands.name: action_jett_obj

subCommands.name: action_jett_self

subCommands.name: action_ignite_subobject
subCommands.description: This action will “ignite” all engines on the specified subobject.

subCommands.name: action_ignite_self
subCommands.description: This action will “ignite” all engines on the object.

subCommands.name: action_terminate_thrust
subCommands.description: This action will terminate the thrust for all engines on the object (shutdown the engines).

subCommands.name: action_shutdown_engine
subCommands.description: This action will “shutdown” the specified engine and set thrust (if applicable) to 0%.

subCommands.name: action_shutdown_subobject

subCommands.name: action_change_aero_mode
subCommands.description: This action will change the object’s aero_mode to the specified mode.

subCommands.name: action_enable_size_factor

subCommands.name: action_set_graphical_model

subCommands.name: action_enable_controls
subCommands.description: This action will enable control input for normal operation. See action_disable_controls to turn off the controls.

subCommands.name: action_disable_controls

subCommands.name: remove_sequencer

name: SixDOF Subobjects
description: Depending on the defining data, subobjects may effect the performance of their parent platform. For example, a bomb carried on an external pylon may produce additional drag on the parent. It is also possible for a subobject to contribute thrust forces to the parent (such as running Hound Dog missiles on a B-52 during takeoff, or having SRB thrust contribute to the total thrust of a Space Shuttle orbiter). In addition, subobjects will contribute mass properties and inertia to their parent.
