name: SixDOF Thrust Producer Types
description: Definitions for each type of engine are performed within the rigid_body_engine_type block. Since the definition is for a ‘type’ of engine and not an ‘instance’ of an engine, no installation position/attitude data is included. Typically, the fuel_feed is specified at the instance-level rather than at the type-level.

subCommands.name: rigid_body_engine_type
subCommands.description: Definitions for each type of engine are performed within the rigid_body_engine_type block. Since the definition is for a ‘type’ of engine and not an ‘instance’ of an engine, no installation position/attitude data is included. Typically, the fuel_feed is specified at the instance-level rather than at the type-level.

subCommands.name: thrust_offset
subCommands.description: This is the location of the thrust relative to the engine’s reference point along the x-axis. A positive value is forward of the engine, negative is aft. This can have significant kinematic effects for rigid-body vehicles, but only affects visuals for point-mass systems.

subCommands.name: inop_ref_area
subCommands.description: This specifies aerodynamic CD-area product for the engine when it is inoperative. It is the drag coefficient multiplied by the reference area.

subCommands.name: fuel_feed
subCommands.description: This specifies the name of the fuel_tank from which the engine will draw fuel. This is typically specified for an engine instance rather than in the type definition.

subCommands.name: throttle_setting_mil
subCommands.description: This specifies the control_value defined in flight_controls that will be used to control the MIL (military) power throttle setting. This can be done in this block or in the propulsion_data of the rigid_body_vehicle_type.

subCommands.name: throttle_setting_ab
subCommands.description: This specifies the control_value defined in flight_controls that will be used to control the AB (afterburner) power throttle setting. This can be done in this block or in the propulsion_data of the rigid_body_vehicle_type.

subCommands.name: throttle_setting_reverser
subCommands.description: This specifies the control_value defined in flight_controls that will be used to control the thrust-reverser control setting. This can be done in this block or in the propulsion_data of the rigid_body_vehicle_type.

subCommands.name: throttle_setting_yaw
subCommands.description: This specifies the control_value defined in flight_controls that will be used to control the yaw thrust vectoring control setting. This can be done in this block or in the propulsion_data of the rigid_body_vehicle_type.

subCommands.name: throttle_setting_pitch
subCommands.description: This specifies the control_value defined in flight_controls that will be used to control the pitch thrust vectoring control setting. This can be done in this block or in the propulsion_data of the rigid_body_vehicle_type.

subCommands.name: point_mass_engine_type
subCommands.description: Definitions for each type of engine are performed within the point_mass_engine_type block. Since the definition is for a ‘type’ of engine and not an ‘instance’ of an engine, no installation position/attitude data is included. Typically, the fuel_feed is specified at the instance-level rather than at the type-level.

subCommands.name: jet
subCommands.description: A jet block is intended to approximate engines incorporating a gas turbine, including turbojets and turbofans. The jet model leans heavily on input data, and so may also be suitable for aproximating propeller engines.

subCommands.name: tsfc_idle_pph
subCommands.description: This specifies the thrust specific fuel consumption at idle in lbs-thrust/lbs-fuel/hr.

subCommands.name: tsfc_mil_pph
subCommands.description: This specifies the thrust specific fuel consumption at military power (full power without afterburner) in lbs-thrust/lbs-fuel/hr.

subCommands.name: tsfc_ab_pph
subCommands.description: This specifies the thrust specific fuel consumption using full afterburner in lbs-thrust/lbs-fuel/hr.

subCommands.name: rated_thrust_idle
subCommands.description: This specifies the thrust at idle. Since thrust varies with various conditions, this is a reference value.

subCommands.name: rated_thrust_mil
subCommands.description: This specifies the thrust at military power (full power without afterburner). Since thrust varies with various conditions, this is a reference value.

subCommands.name: rated_thrust_ab
subCommands.description: This specifies the thrust using full afterburner. Since thrust varies with various conditions, this is a reference value.

subCommands.name: thrust_table_idle
subCommands.description: This is a simple table of idle thrust versus altitude. Note that is does not consider Mach-effects. The thrust_idle_mach_alt_table or thrust_idle_alt_mach_table are preferable, but if no Mach data is available, this table can be used.

subCommands.name: thrust_idle_mach_alt_table
subCommands.description: This is an improved table over thrust_table_idle, since it includes Mach-effects. However, most users will prefer the format of the thrust_idle_alt_mach_table instead.

subCommands.name: thrust_idle_alt_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is typically the best thrust table format – it includes Mach-effects and organizes its data in a preferred manner. The thrust_idle_mach_alt_table is an alternative format.

subCommands.name: thrust_table_mil
subCommands.description: This is a simple table of military (MIL) thrust versus altitude. Note that is does not consider Mach-effects. The thrust_mil_mach_alt_table or thrust_mil_alt_mach_table are preferable, but if no Mach data is available, this table can be used.

subCommands.name: thrust_mil_mach_alt_table
subCommands.description: This is an improved table over thrust_table_mil, since it includes Mach-effects. However, most users will prefer the format of the thrust_mil_alt_mach_table instead.

subCommands.name: thrust_mil_alt_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is typically the best thrust table format – it includes Mach-effects and organizes its data in a preferred manner. The thrust_mil_mach_alt_table is an alternative format.

subCommands.name: thrust_table_ab
subCommands.description: This is a simple table of afterburner (AB) thrust versus altitude. Note that is does not consider Mach-effects. The thrust_ab_mach_alt_table or thrust_ab_alt_mach_table are preferable, but if no Mach data is available, this table can be used.

subCommands.name: thrust_ab_mach_alt_table
subCommands.description: This is an improved table over thrust_table_ab, since it includes Mach-effects. However, most users will prefer the format of the thrust_ab_alt_mach_table instead.

subCommands.name: thrust_ab_alt_mach_table
subCommands.description: This is typically the best thrust table format – it includes Mach-effects and organizes its data in a preferred manner. The thrust_ab_mach_alt_table is an alternative format.

subCommands.name: spin_up_mil_per_sec
subCommands.description: This defines how quickly the engine will “spool-up” as the power level is advanced. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-up from idle to MIL power in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-up from idle to MIL power.

subCommands.name: spin_up_table_mil_per_sec
subCommands.description: This defines how quickly the engine will “spool-up” as the power level is advanced. Rather than a single value, this command uses a table that is a function of the throttle level (normalized), allowing a more realistic spin-up as a function of current power condition. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-up from idle to MIL power in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-up from idle to MIL power.

subCommands.name: spin_up_ab_per_sec
subCommands.description: This defines how quickly the engine will “spool-up” as the power level is advanced. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-up from MIL to Full AB power in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-up from MIL to Full AB power.

subCommands.name: spin_up_table_ab_per_sec
subCommands.description: This defines how quickly the engine will “spool-up” as the power level is advanced. Rather than a single value, this command uses a table that is a function of the throttle level (normalized), allowing a more realistic spin-up as a function of current power condition. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-up from MIL to Full AB power in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-up from MIL to Full AB power.

subCommands.name: spin_down_mil_per_sec
subCommands.description: This defines how quickly the engine will “spool-down” as the power level is reduced. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-down from MIL power to idle in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-down from MIL power to idle.

subCommands.name: spin_down_table_mil_per_sec
subCommands.description: This defines how quickly the engine will “spool-down” as the power level is reduced. Rather than a single value, this command uses a table that is a function of the throttle level (normalized), allowing a more realistic spin-down as a function of current power condition. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-down from MIL power to idle in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-down from MIL power to idle.

subCommands.name: spin_down_ab_per_sec
subCommands.description: This defines how quickly the engine will “spool-down” as the power level is reduced. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-down from Full AB power to MIL power in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-down from Full AB power to MIL power.

subCommands.name: spin_down_table_ab_per_sec
subCommands.description: This defines how quickly the engine will “spool-down” as the power level is reduced. Rather than a single value, this command uses a table that is a function of the throttle level (normalized), allowing a more realistic spin-down as a function of current power condition. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-down from Full AB power to MIL power in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-down from Full AB power to MIL power.

subCommands.name: engine_smokes_above_power_setting
subCommands.description: This specifies the throttle level (MIL power) above which the engine will produce smoke. For example, a value of 0.8 will produce smoke when the throttle is above 80% power. If afterburner is selected, the smoke will cease. The default is a value of 1.0, which will not produce any smoke. This is useful for simulating engines that produce excessive smoke, such as old F-4 Phantoms and MiG-29s.

subCommands.name: ramjet
subCommands.description: Definitions for each type of ramjet engine are performed within the ramjet block.

subCommands.name: tsfc_alt_mach_table
subCommands.description: This specifies the thrust specific fuel consumption as a function of altitude and Mach in lbs-thrust/lbs-fuel/hr. Altitude units are feet.

subCommands.name: thrust_alt_mach_table
subCommands.description: This specifies the thrust as a function of altitude and Mach in lbs. Altitude units are feet. Since the table will clamp rather than interpolate at the end values, it is important to ensure that data at the extreme points goes to zero values. Failure to do so could result in increasing thrust at high Mach, for example.

subCommands.name: afterburner_appearance_when_operating
subCommands.description: This specifies whether or not an afterburner appearance should be used when the ramjet is operating. This only effects the appearance, it has no physical/kinematic effect. When true, and the ramjet is operating, it will have the same appearance of a jet engine using afterburner.

subCommands.name: latch_fuel_injection
subCommands.description: When true, the fuel injection will be latched (locked) into the on condition. This will keep the engine operating, regardless of throttle command, as long as fuel is available. When false, normal throttle control is used. The default value is false.

subCommands.name: use_proportional_throttle
subCommands.description: When true, a proportional throttle control will be used. When false, normal on/off throttle control is used. The default value is false.

subCommands.name: minimum_proportional_thrust
subCommands.description: This is the minimum thrust level that may be used for proportional throttle control. It is often 0.8, but must always be greater than zero. The default value is 0.0.

subCommands.name: liquid_propellant_rocket
subCommands.description: Definitions for each type of liquid-propellant rocket engine are performed within the liquid_propellant_rocket block.

subCommands.name: max_thrust_sealevel
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum thrust that can be produced at sea level conditions. Either max_thrust_sealevel or max_thrust_vacuum should be specified, not both.

subCommands.name: max_thrust_vacuum
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum thrust that can be produced at vacuum conditions. Either max_thrust_sealevel or max_thrust_vacuum should be specified, not both.

subCommands.name: normalized_thrust_vs_alt
subCommands.description: This is a simple table of “normalized-thrust” versus altitude. Normalized thrust is a value that will be multiplied with a nominal isp-calculated thrust, typically computed using max_thrust_sealevel and isp_vs_alt. This allows altitude-effects on thrust production:

subCommands.name: isp_vs_alt
subCommands.description: This is a simple table of specific impulse (Isp) versus altitude:

subCommands.name: normalized_spinup
subCommands.description: This specifies the spin-up rate in normalized-position/second. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-up from zero to full thrust in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-up from zero to full thrust.

subCommands.name: normalized_spindown
subCommands.description: This specifies the spin-down rate in normalized-position/second. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-down from full thrust to zero thrust in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-down from full thrust to zero thrust.

subCommands.name: creates_smoke_trail
subCommands.description: This determines whether or not the rocket will generate a smoke trail appearance. By default, liquid-propellant rockets do not produce a smoke trail, but solid-propellant rockets do produce a smoke trail.

subCommands.name: solid_propellant_rocket
subCommands.description: Definitions for each type of solid-propellant rocket motor are performed within the solid_propellant_rocket block. Note that unlike jet engines, ramjets/scramjets, and liquid-propellant rocket engines, a solid-propellant rocket motor does not specify a fuel_feed, since it contains its own propellant properties.

subCommands.name: rated_thrust
subCommands.description: This specifies the “rated thrust” of the solid-propellant motor. Since thrust depends on a range of conditions, this is a reference number, often used to calculate percent thrust.

subCommands.name: thrust_vs_time_sealevel
subCommands.description: This is a simple table of thrust in lbs as a function of time in seconds at sea level pressure conditions. Either thrust_vs_time_sealevel or thrust_vs_time_vacuum should be specified, but not both.

subCommands.name: thrust_vs_time_vacuum
subCommands.description: This is a simple table of thrust in lbs as a function of time in seconds at vacuum pressure conditions. Either thrust_vs_time_sealevel or thrust_vs_time_vacuum should be specified, but not both.

subCommands.name: isp_vs_alt
subCommands.description: This is a simple table of specific impulse (Isp) in seconds versus altitude in feet.

subCommands.name: creates_smoke_trail
subCommands.description: This determines whether or not the rocket will generate a smoke trail appearance. By default, liquid-propellant rockets do not produce a smoke trail, but solid-propellant rockets do produce a smoke trail.

subCommands.name: propellant_mass
subCommands.description: This specified the propellant mass in the solid-propellant motor. The value here should be moved to the max_fuel_quantity and current_fuel_qty values of a fuel_tank created for the engine.

subCommands.name: propellant_rel_pos_x
subCommands.description: This specified the center of mass (in the x-direction of rocket-coordinates) of the propellant mass relative to the reference point of the rocket. To avoid changing the vehicle’s performance, the value here should be moved as-is to the cg_full_x and cg_empty_x values of a fuel_tank created for the engine. For more accuracy, this value may be added to the engine’s rel_pos_x value in migrating to cg_full_x and cg_empty_x.

subCommands.name: propellant_rel_pos_y
subCommands.description: This specified the center of mass (in the y-direction of rocket-coordinates) of the propellant mass relative to the reference point of the rocket. To avoid changing the vehicle’s performance, the value here should be moved as-is to the cg_full_y and cg_empty_y values of a fuel_tank created for the engine. For more accuracy, this value may be added to the engine’s rel_pos_y value in migrating to cg_full_y and cg_empty_y.

subCommands.name: propellant_rel_pos_z
subCommands.description: This specified the center of mass (in the z-direction of rocket-coordinates) of the propellant mass relative to the reference point of the rocket. To avoid changing the vehicle’s performance, the value here should be moved as-is to the cg_full_z and cg_empty_z values of a fuel_tank created for the engine. For more accuracy, this value may be added to the engine’s rel_pos_z value in migrating to cg_full_z and cg_empty_z.

If afterburner is selected, the smoke will cease. The default is a value of 1.0, which will not produce any smoke. This is useful for simulating engines that produce excessive smoke, such as old F-4 Phantoms and MiG-29s.

subCommands.name: ramjet
subCommands.description: Definitions for each type of ramjet engine are performed within the ramjet block.

subCommands.name: tsfc_alt_mach_table
subCommands.description: This specifies the thrust specific fuel consumption as a function of altitude and Mach in lbs-thrust/lbs-fuel/hr. Altitude units are feet.

subCommands.name: thrust_alt_mach_table
subCommands.description: This specifies the thrust as a function of altitude and Mach in lbs. Altitude units are feet. Since the table will clamp rather than interpolate at the end values, it is important to ensure that data at the extreme points goes to zero values. Failure to do so could result in increasing thrust at high Mach, for example.

subCommands.name: afterburner_appearance_when_operating
subCommands.description: This specifies whether or not an afterburner appearance should be used when the ramjet is operating. This only effects the appearance, it has no physical/kinematic effect. When true, and the ramjet is operating, it will have the same appearance of a jet engine using afterburner.

subCommands.name: latch_fuel_injection
subCommands.description: When true, the fuel injection will be latched (locked) into the on condition. This will keep the engine operating, regardless of throttle command, as long as fuel is available. When false, normal throttle control is used. The default value is false.

subCommands.name: use_proportional_throttle
subCommands.description: When true, a proportional throttle control will be used. When false, normal on/off throttle control is used. The default value is false.

subCommands.name: minimum_proportional_thrust
subCommands.description: This is the minimum thrust level that may be used for proportional throttle control. It is often 0.8, but must always be greater than zero. The default value is 0.0.

subCommands.name: liquid_propellant_rocket
subCommands.description: Definitions for each type of liquid-propellant rocket engine are performed within the liquid_propellant_rocket block.

subCommands.name: max_thrust_sealevel
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum thrust that can be produced at sea level conditions. Either max_thrust_sealevel or max_thrust_vacuum should be specified, not both.

subCommands.name: max_thrust_vacuum
subCommands.description: This specifies the maximum thrust that can be produced at vacuum conditions. Either max_thrust_sealevel or max_thrust_vacuum should be specified, not both.

subCommands.name: normalized_thrust_vs_alt
subCommands.description: This is a simple table of “normalized-thrust” versus altitude. Normalized thrust is a value that will be multiplied with a nominal isp-calculated thrust, typically computed using max_thrust_sealevel and isp_vs_alt. This allows altitude-effects on thrust production:

subCommands.name: isp_vs_alt
subCommands.description: This is a simple table of specific impulse (Isp) versus altitude:

subCommands.name: normalized_spinup
subCommands.description: This specifies the spin-up rate in normalized-position/second. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-up from zero to full thrust in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-up from zero to full thrust.

subCommands.name: normalized_spindown
subCommands.description: This specifies the spin-down rate in normalized-position/second. A value of 1.0 implies that the engine will spin-down from full thrust to zero thrust in 1 second, while a value of 0.1 implies that it will take 10 seconds to spin-down from full thrust to zero thrust.

subCommands.name: creates_smoke_trail
subCommands.description: This determines whether or not the rocket will generate a smoke trail appearance. By default, liquid-propellant rockets do not produce a smoke trail, but solid-propellant rockets do produce a smoke trail.

subCommands.name: solid_propellant_rocket
subCommands.description: Definitions for each type of solid-propellant rocket motor are performed within the solid_propellant_rocket block. Note that unlike jet engines, ramjets/scramjets, and liquid-propellant rocket engines, a solid-propellant rocket motor does not specify a fuel_feed, since it contains its own propellant properties.

subCommands.name: rated_thrust
subCommands.description: This specifies the “rated thrust” of the solid-propellant motor. Since thrust depends on a range of conditions, this is a reference number, often used to calculate percent thrust.

subCommands.name: thrust_vs_time_sealevel
subCommands.description: This is a simple table of thrust in lbs as a function of time in seconds at sea level pressure conditions. Either thrust_vs_time_sealevel or thrust_vs_time_vacuum should be specified, but not both.

subCommands.name: thrust_vs_time_vacuum
subCommands.description: This is a simple table of thrust in lbs as a function of time in seconds at vacuum pressure conditions. Either thrust_vs_time_sealevel or thrust_vs_time_vacuum should be specified, but not both.

subCommands.name: isp_vs_alt
subCommands.description: This is a simple table of specific impulse (Isp) in seconds versus altitude in feet.

subCommands.name: creates_smoke_trail
subCommands.description: This determines whether or not the rocket will generate a smoke trail appearance. By default, liquid-propellant rockets do not produce a smoke trail, but solid-propellant rockets do produce a smoke trail.

subCommands.name: propellant_mass
subCommands.description: This specified the propellant mass in the solid-propellant motor. The value here should be moved to the max_fuel_quantity and current_fuel_qty values of a fuel_tank created for the engine.

subCommands.name: propellant_rel_pos_x
subCommands.description: This specified the center of mass (in the x-direction of rocket-coordinates) of the propellant mass relative to the reference point of the rocket. To avoid changing the vehicle’s performance, the value here should be moved as-is to the cg_full_x and cg_empty_x values of a fuel_tank created for the engine. For more accuracy, this value may be added to the engine’s rel_pos_x value in migrating to cg_full_x and cg_empty_x.

subCommands.name: propellant_rel_pos_y
subCommands.description: This specified the center of mass (in the y-direction of rocket-coordinates) of the propellant mass relative to the reference point of the rocket. To avoid changing the vehicle’s performance, the value here should be moved as-is to the cg_full_y and cg_empty_y values of a fuel_tank created for the engine. For more accuracy, this value may be added to the engine’s rel_pos_y value in migrating to cg_full_y and cg_empty_y.

subCommands.name: propellant_rel_pos_z
subCommands.description: This specified the center of mass (in the z-direction of rocket-coordinates) of the propellant mass relative to the reference point of the rocket. To avoid changing the vehicle’s performance, the value here should be moved as-is to the cg_full_z and cg_empty_z values of a fuel_tank created for the engine. For more accuracy, this value may be added to the engine’s rel_pos_z value in migrating to cg_full_z and cg_empty_z.

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: Enable extra debugging output.

subCommands.name: detached
subCommands.description: For formations defined in the initial conditions, this will cause this formation to not be attached to its parent. After initialization any attached formation will have its members placed into the correct positions relative to the formation leader. The detached status on a formation also effects the way formation commands are propagated down through the hierarchy. See WsfSixDofFormationCommand.

subCommands.name: offset
subCommands.description: Specify the offset of the formation from its parent. This is the means by which the initial relative positioning of the members of a formation is specified. The offset is given as a triplet of a range from the reference point, a relative bearing from the direction of travel of the leader, and a vertical offset (or stack). For example, the following offset would be the point 100 m to the right of the reference point and at 1 m higher altitude.

subCommands.name: member_platform
subCommands.description: Set the member platform of the unit formation to be the platform with the given name.

subCommands.name: cache_directory
subCommands.description: Specifies the name of the directory to which cached binary files (produced as the result of enabling write_cache_files) are to be written.

subCommands.name: ignore_cache_files
subCommands.description: Indicates if the binary cache files created as a result of the write_cache_files or fast_detection_mode commands should be used. If true, any cached files will be ignored and all data will be read from the original text files.

subCommands.name: write_cache_files
subCommands.description: Indicates if binary files for tables read from text files or generated as a result of enabling fast_detection_mode should be written to the cache directory. Subsequent runs that use the same data will read the data from the cache directory instead of reading the original text data or regenerating the fast detection mode tables.

subCommands.name: load_atmosphere
subCommands.description: Loads the SOSM atmosphere definition from the specified file and associates it with the name specified by <sosm-atmosphere-type>. See SOSM_atmosphere_model for directions on how to create atmosphere definitions.

subCommands.name: load_sensor
subCommands.description: Loads the SOSM sensor definition from the specified file and associates it with the name specified by <sosm-sensor-type>.

subCommands.name: load_target
subCommands.description: Loads the SOSM target model definition from the specified file and associates it with the name specified by <sosm-target-type>.

subCommands.name: map_sensor_type
subCommands.description: Indicates the SOSM sensor type <sosm-sensor-type> should be used when WSF wants to create an instance of WSF_SOSM_SENSOR of type <wsf-sensor-type>.

subCommands.name: map_target_type
subCommands.description: Indicates that the SOSM target type <sosm-target-type> should be used when WSF wants to perform a detection attempt on an WSF platform type of <wsf-platform-type>.

subCommands.name: default_atmosphere
subCommands.description: Specifies the SOSM atmosphere type to be used when an SOSM sensor definition does not explicitly refer to a specific atmosphere type.

subCommands.name: fast_detection_mode
subCommands.description: Indicate if ‘fast_detection_mode’ should be used. ‘fast_detection_mode’ is a special operating mode that is used to reduce computational overhead at the expense of a small loss in fidelity. Use of this mode is typically warranted when running real-time.

subCommands.name: debug_level
subCommands.description: Specifies the level of debugging information to be printed.

subCommands.name: spectral_print_format
subCommands.description: Specifies the output format for spectral data when debug_level is greater than 1.

subCommands.name: show_iripp_data
subCommands.description: If specified, spectral detection data will be produced in a format similar to IRIPP ‘spec’ data.

subCommands.name: sosm_sensor_type
subCommands.description: An optional command that specifies the SOSM sensor type to be used. See map_sensor_type for how this is used.

subCommands.name: ranging_time

subCommands.name: ranging_time_track_quality
subCommands.description: If the ranging time is used to generate a track with range information, this parameter controls the track quality once range is valid. The quality-value must be non-negative.

name: Table Values
description: The table being processed is non-dimensional, representing a constant function (i.e. y = c).

subCommands.name: constant
subCommands.description: The table being processed is non-dimensional, representing a constant function (i.e. y = c).

subCommands.name: regular_table
subCommands.description: With regular tables, all slices through the table must have the same number of breakpoints. This is efficient but requires the same density of sample points across slices.

subCommands.name: irregular_table
subCommands.description: An irregular table provides greater flexibility by removing the restriction that all slices through the table require the same number of break points. The dependent variable values are assigned according to the number of independent variables defined to complete the cross sections of the table.

subCommands.name: interval_table
subCommands.description: The interval table is similar to the irregular_table, except interval tables provide no option for independent variable extrapolation.

subCommands.name: curve
subCommands.description: A curve is a special form of a regular_table limited to specifying one independent variable.

subCommands.name: file
subCommands.description: The file option is used to read in a file containing the table definition. The table defined in the file must be constructed exactly as it would be defined inline within the program.

subCommands.name: independent_variable
subCommands.description: Specifies the name and units for an independent variable. Optionally, precision and extrapolation may be added. This command may be repeated up to eight times to define the independent variables present in the table.

subCommands.name: dependent_variable
subCommands.description: Specifies the units and optional precision of the dependent variable.

subCommands.name: units
subCommands.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the given variable and must be a valid unit type for the variable defined. For example:

subCommands.name: precision
subCommands.description: An optional subcommand that specifies the precision used to store values in memory. double is at least 64 bits and float is at least 32 bits.

subCommands.name: interpolation
subCommands.description: An optional subcommand that specifies whether table lookups should use multilinear interpolation of the data values, or the nearest value in the table.

subCommands.name: extrapolate
subCommands.description: An optional subcommand used to indicate extrapolation will be performed if the value of the independent_variable is outside the limits of its definition.

subCommands.name: num_points
subCommands.description: An optional subcommand used to specify the number of points that the variable list will have.

subCommands.name: linear_equation
subCommands.description: An optional subcommand used to represent the independent variables values using a linear equation between <point_1> and <point_n> (inclusive) with num_points points.

subCommands.name: binary_data_file
subCommands.description: An optional subcommand that maps the specified file to a raw binary array of floats/doubles for use as a list of datapoints.

subCommands.name: save_as_rectangular_indexed_binary_file
subCommands.description: Save the generated table to file, which can then be passed to the binary_data_file command.

name: Tangent
description: The given delta-V to be applied. Positive values will be applied in the same direction as the velocity vector, and negative values will be applied in the opposite direction.

subCommands.name: delta_v
subCommands.description: The given delta-V to be applied. Positive values will be applied in the same direction as the velocity vector, and negative values will be applied in the opposite direction.

name: Target
description: The desired time past the current time for execution of the maneuver. No Optimizations are performed.

subCommands.name: delta_time
subCommands.description: The desired time past the current time for execution of the maneuver. No Optimizations are performed.

subCommands.name: maximum_delta_time
subCommands.description: The maximum time after the current time to be considered for execution of the maneuver. Optimizations in time will occur between the time of the constraint and the provided time.

subCommands.name: maximum_delta_v
subCommands.description: The maximum delta_v to be considered for execution of the maneuver. Optimizations in time to find minimum delta-v will occur between the time of the constraint and any time limit set by maximum_delta_time.

subCommands.name: optimize_time
subCommands.description: Optimize the targeting solution such that it executes at the earliest possible time. This optimization is also constrained by the maximum_delta_v value, if provided.

subCommands.name: optimize_delta_v
subCommands.description: Optimize the targeting solution such that it executes at a time that minimizes total delta-v expended.

subCommands.name: optimize_cost
subCommands.description: Optimize the targeting solution such that the specified cost is minimized. The available cost functions are:

subCommands.name: tolerance
subCommands.description: Specify the solution search tolerance. The default tolerance is 1.0e-9.

description: These commands specify the target of a targeting-class orbital maneuver (Target, Intercept, and Rendezvous). When specifying a target, one selects both a base target, and an optional offset from that base target.

subCommands.name: platform
subCommands.description: Use the platform with the given name as the base target.

subCommands.name: libration_point
subCommands.description: Use the given libration point of the given system as the base target. Allowed values of the system are:

subCommands.name: eci_position
subCommands.description: Use the given ECI position as the base target. This is equivalent to eci_state with a velocity of zero.

subCommands.name: eci_state
subCommands.description: Use the given ECI position and velocity as the base target.

subCommands.name: offset
subCommands.description: Specify a position offset from the specified base target, expressed in the given frame. The available frame options are:

subCommands.name: velocity_offset
subCommands.description: Specify a velocity offset from the specified base target, expressed in the given frame. The available frame options are:

subCommands.name: offset_time
subCommands.description: For targets that have a kinematic offset (at least one of position_offset or velocity_offset is provided), also specifying an offset_time will indicate at what time after the end of the maneuver that the provided kinematic offset will be achieved. For example, this command can be used to target a state such that 1 hour after the maneuver the maneuvering platform will attain the given target.

subCommands.name: lag_time
subCommands.description: Specify a lag time for the target. If a lag time is specified, the actual target will be advanced by the specified time along its motion relative to where the targeting operation is aimed. For example, the performer of a Rendezvous maneuver that has a lag_time specified will achieve an orbit that follows along the orbit of the target platform, but will be the given time behind the target in its orbit.

name: Teardrop
description: Specify the platform relative to which the executing platform will perform a Teardrop maneuver.

subCommands.name: target_platform
subCommands.description: Specify the platform relative to which the executing platform will perform a Teardrop maneuver.

subCommands.name: radial_offset_at_poca
subCommands.description: Specify the distance at the point of closest approach. This distance will be entirely in the radial direction, with a positive value indicating that the teardrop will be above the target_platform. The provided value must be non-zero.

subCommands.name: period
subCommands.description: Specify the time taken to execute the teardrop maneuver. This period must be no greater than about 40.6 percent of the orbital period of the target_platform. The period covers from when the executing platform first passes directly under (over) the target, and when it passes under (over) the target for the last time. These times are at half the given period before the point of closest approach and half the period after the point of closest approach.

subCommands.name: time_to_poca
subCommands.description: Specify the duration after the executing platform is inserted onto the teardrop orbit at which it reaches the point of closest approach to the target_platform. This value must be greater than half of the specified period.

subCommands.name: repetitions
subCommands.description: Specify the number of times the executing platform should traverse the teardrop. This provided value must be positive.

subCommands.name: delta_time
subCommands.description: The desired time past the current time for execution of the maneuver. No Optimizations are performed.

subCommands.name: maximum_delta_time
subCommands.description: The maximum time after the current time to be considered for execution of the maneuver. Optimizations in time will occur between the time of the constraint and the provided time.

subCommands.name: maximum_delta_v
subCommands.description: The maximum delta_v to be considered for execution of the maneuver. Optimizations in time to find minimum delta-v will occur between the time of the constraint and any time limit set by maximum_delta_time.

subCommands.name: optimize_time
subCommands.description: Optimize the targeting solution such that it executes at the earliest possible time. This optimization is also constrained by the maximum_delta_v value, if provided.

subCommands.name: optimize_delta_v
subCommands.description: Optimize the targeting solution such that it executes at a time that minimizes total delta-v expended.

subCommands.name: optimize_cost
subCommands.description: Optimize the targeting solution such that the specified cost is minimized. The available cost functions are:

subCommands.name: tolerance
subCommands.description: Specify the solution search tolerance. The default tolerance is 1.0e-9.

subCommands.description: Specify the location of a directory that contains DTED as it would exist if it were copied directly from a NIMA CD. This command assumes the ‘dmed’ file exists and properly reflects the extent of the data contained in the directory. This command may be specified multiple times to indicate multiple sources of DTED.

subCommands.name: raw-dted
subCommands.description: This is an alternative method to specify the location of DTED. This is used if the ‘dmed’ file does not exist, is corrupted, or in some way does not properly reflect the extent of the data contained in the directory. This command may be specified multiple times to indicate multiple sources of DTED. Where:

subCommands.name: validate_terrain
subCommands.description: Immediately checks all of the currently supplied DTED-format terrain for reasonable values. This command should occur AFTER any dted or raw_dted commands for the terrain data to be checked. Progress messages will be issued as directories are processed and error messages will be issued if suspicious data is found.

subCommands.name: dted_checksum
subCommands.description: Enable or disable the checksum operation when loading DTED terrain. If enabled, and a specified DTED file does not pass the checksum test, it is not used. Set this flag to “disabled” if one must use DTED files with invalid checksums.

subCommands.name: float_grid
subCommands.description: Specify that the source of elevation data is in ‘float grid’ format. This is essentially United States Geological Survey (USGS) Digital Elevation Model (DEM) data that has been reprocessed to a form that is compatible with the ESRI ArcGIS® products (http://www.esri.com).

subCommands.name: float_grid_file
subCommands.description: Specify that the source of elevation data is in ‘float grid’ format (see float_grid). Multiple float_grid_file inputs can be provided.

subCommands.name: float_grid_vegetation
subCommands.description: Same as float_grid but specifies a vegetation layer that is accessed primarily for the purpose of sensor line-of-sight masking. For example, a bush occludes the line of sight between a sensor and target, the vegetation layer can be utilized to determine this block. Note that the vegetation layer is defined to be the bare earth terrain elevation plus height of vegetation above bare earth.

subCommands.name: float_grid_vegetation_file
subCommands.description: Specify that the source of vegetation layer data is in ‘float grid’ format (see float_grid_vegetation). Multiple float_grid_vegetation_file inputs can be provided.

subCommands.name: geotiff
subCommands.description: Specify that the source of elevation data is in the geotiff format. The command may be called multiple times; in the event of overlap the last geotiff command will produce the result.

subCommands.name: bathymetry
subCommands.description: Specify a bathymetry source file in ASCII XYZ format. This command may be used more than once to indicate multiple sources of bathymetry.

subCommands.name: visual_db
subCommands.description: Specify that the source of elevation data is from a ‘visual database’ file (xxxx.eld file). This is a proprietary file format that is correlated the a visual database used by Boeing St. Louis Center for Integrated Defense Simulation (CIDS). The visual_db command can only be used once. If multiple eld files are to be read in, create a new text file that lists the eld files and reference the new text file with the visual_db command.

subCommands.name: load_cme_terrain
subCommands.description: Load terrain as directed by using the Common Modeling Environment (CME) configuration files. In order to locate the configuration files, the environment variable CME_REL_BASE must be defined and point to the CME root directory. The file $CME_REL_BASE/site/geodata.dat should contain the commands that define the terrain sources.

subCommands.name: cme_path
subCommands.description: Used in conjunction with the load_cme_terrain command to specify the path to the CME configuration files. If specified, this will override any path defined in the environment variable CME_REL_BASE.

subCommands.name: maximum_data_size
subCommands.description: Specify the maximum amount of terrain elevation data that can remain in memory.

subCommands.name: maximum_terrain_height
subCommands.description: Specify the maximum terrain height in the region. This is optional and is used to improve performance when performing terrain-masking checks.

subCommands.name: minimum_allowable_step_size
subCommands.description: Specify the minimum allowable step size to be used when performing terrain-masking checks. Increasing this value above the resolution of the terrain will improve performance at the expense of reducing fidelity.

subCommands.name: use_fast_masking_check
subCommands.description: Specify that the ‘fast masking check’ should be used for performing terrain-masking checks. This algorithm makes certain assumptions about the terrain slope in order to increase the step size. There is a small probability that an obscuration will be missed if the terrain has very steep gradients (> 71 degrees, or more precisely > atan(3)).

subCommands.name: disable
subCommands.description: Prevent the use of terrain elevation data by the framework. This is typically used to temporarily disable the use of terrain for the current simulation.

subCommands.description: This is only to be used when defining systems that employ multiple beams (e.g., when using multiple beams in WSF_RADAR_SENSOR). It specifies the elevation angle of the beam center above the horizontal plane.

subCommands.name: check_terrain_masking
subCommands.description: Toggles the computation of terrain and horizon line of sight. This may be set to ‘off’ to either reduce computation or model sensors and comm devices which do not have line of sight limitations. By default, horizon masking is checked first, followed by a separate terrain masking check if terrain is loaded. The simple horizon masking check assumes a smooth bald spherical Earth and that any object below zero mean sea level is obscured. For subsurface sensors, horizon checking can be disabled by setting the terrain_masking_mode to terrain_only.

subCommands.name: terrain_masking_mode
subCommands.description: Sets the mode or type of masking checks to perform. By default, both horizon and terrain masking checks are enabled.

subCommands.name: duty_cycle
subCommands.description: Specifies the transmit duty-cycle for a pulsed transmitter. If entered then this value is multiplied by the peak power entered and used as the average power in any calculations not specifically calling out for peak power.

subCommands.name: effective_earth_radius

subCommands.name: pulse_compression_ratio

subCommands.name: pulse_repetition_interval
subCommands.description: Specify the pulse rate or inter-pulse spacing for a pulsed transmitter, using one of the following methods: - The average number pulses per unit second (pulse_repetition_frequency}}. - The average time between the leading edge of the pulses (pulse_repetition_interval).

subCommands.name: pulse_width

subCommands.name: use_peak_power

subCommands.name: alternate_frequency
subCommands.description: Specifies alternate frequencies that a comm in conjunction with jamming_perception_timeout and jamming_perception_threshold or a WSF_RADAR_SENSOR in conjuction with jamming_perception_timeout and jamming_perception_threshold and the electronic_protect WSF_AGILITY_EFFECT technique in the case that jamming is perceived. Defines the initial state of the weapon when introduced into the simulation.

subCommands.name: update_interval
subCommands.description: Specifies the update interval for those weapon types that require it.

subCommands.name: launch_computer
subCommands.description: Specifies the launch computer for those weapon types that require it.

subCommands.name: quantity
subCommands.description: Specifies the number of rounds that are initially available.

subCommands.name: maximum_quantity
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum number of rounds that may exist on the weapon. This is used to constrain weapon reloading.

subCommands.name: firing_delay
subCommands.description: This is only applicable to firing requests initiated by WsfWeapon.FireSalvo or WsfTaskManager.FireAt. It specifies the time that will elapse between the time the request is issued and the time the first (or only) shot of the request is fired. This may cause a weapon to be fired at a nonexistent track (i.e., the target platform was removed from the simulation after the Fire command was issued), which in turn makes the weapon have an erratic trajectory.

subCommands.name: firing_interval
subCommands.description: Specifies the amount of time that must elapse between when a weapon last completed a firing request and when it is next fired. This is different from salvo_interval in that this value specifies the minimum time delay that occurs before another Fire() request can be prosecuted.

subCommands.name: salvo_interval
subCommands.description: This is only applicable to firing requests initiated by WsfWeapon.FireSalvo or WsfTaskManager.FireAt. It specifies the time amount of time that will elapse between rounds in a multiple shot request. The times of each shot in a salvo will be: * T<sub>1</sub> = T + firing_delay * T<sub>2</sub> = T<sub>1</sub> + salvo_interval * T<sub>N</sub> = T<sub>N-1</sub> + salvo_interval

subCommands.name: maximum_request_count
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum number of salvo firing requests (WsfWeapon.FireSalvo or WsfTaskManager.FireAt) that may be active simultaneously.

subCommands.name: automatic_target_cueing
subCommands.description: This is only applicable to firing requests initiated by WsfWeapon.FireSalvo or WsfTaskManager.FireAt. If ‘true’ and if the weapon supports cueing, the weapon will be cued to the track specified on the request. If ‘false’ then the weapon will not be cued.

subCommands.name: cue_to_predicted_intercept
subCommands.description: If automatic_target_cueing is true, specify if weapon should be cued to the track location (false) or the the predicted intercept location (true).

subCommands.name: unknown_target_range
subCommands.description: Specifies the range to be used for deriving a target location if either a target track was not specified on the fire request or if the target track was specified and did not contain enough information to derive a location.

subCommands.name: unknown_target_altitude
subCommands.description: Specifies the altitude to be used when deriving a target location. This command only has an effect if unknown_target_range is also specified.

subCommands.name: reload_increment
subCommands.description: Specifies the amount of weapons inventory taken from an External Replenishment Magazine (ERM) added to the weapon when a reload event occurs.

subCommands.name: reload_inventory
subCommands.description: Specifies the amount of weapons inventory available from an External Replenishment Magazine (ERM), the finite source for weapons reloading.

subCommands.name: reload_threshold
subCommands.description: Specifies the amount of weapons inventory at which a reload event is started. Reload potential is evaluated only after a successful weapon Fire().

subCommands.name: reload_time
subCommands.description: Specifies the time elapsed from the start of a weapon reload until the reload completes.

subCommands.name: inhibit_while_reloading
subCommands.description: Indicates if firing is inhibited while reloading is in progress. If this is false, firings will continue to take place until the available quantity is 0. If true, any request will be ignored.

subCommands.name: weapon_effects
subCommands.description: Specifies the type of the weapon_effects to be used for determining weapon effectiveness. See the page on weapon_effects for more details.

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: Debugging information will be sent to standard output.

subCommands.name: draw_endgame_pk
subCommands.description: Forces a pk draw on a target at time of end game regardless of whether or not the target is indestructible, or is internally or externally controlled.

subCommands.name: excluded_category
subCommands.description: Defines a platform category the weapon will not affect. If the target platform being considered for damage is of this category, no neutralizing effect will be possible.

subCommands.name: incidental_damage_allowed
subCommands.description: Defines whether any “incidental” platform damage is possible. Incidental is damage to a platform other than the intended one. For air-to-air missile engagements, a missile typically will kill its intended target, or none at all (no incidental damage), but if a bomb is dropped with the intention of destroying a train station and misses, it could easily destroy an adjacent building (incidental damage).

subCommands.name: launch_pk
subCommands.description: The probability of kill assuming a valid intercept. If use_intercept_pk, then launch_pk will be ignored, conversely, if use_launch_pk, then the intercept_pk will be ignored. In the event a PkTable is present and enabled by the use_pk_table command, then the intercept_pk value will be overridden by the pk fetched from the table.

subCommands.name: remove_weapon_platform
subCommands.description: Determines whether the explicit weapon platform causing the effect is removed upon completion of the engagement. The setting is ignored for implicit engagements. Setting this to ‘false’ allows the platform to remain after the completion of the engagement.

subCommands.name: use_intercept_pk
subCommands.description: Sets an internal flag indicating that the intercept_pk value (either as user input, or calculated internally, depending upon the specific effects model) will be used to determine the end effect upon the target.

subCommands.name: use_launch_pk
subCommands.description: Sets an internal flag indicating that the launch_pk value (either as user input, or calculated internally, depending upon the specific effects model) will be used to determine the end effect upon the target.

subCommands.name: on_target_damaged
subCommands.description: Perform a custom scripted action when the weapon_effects algorithm determines a target platform has been damaged. This action is performed instead of the default action (which is to assign a numeric damage value to the target platform). The variable DAMAGE, indicating the numeric value of the damage, is available when executing this script.

subCommands.name: on_target_killed
subCommands.description: Perform a custom scripted action when the weapon_effects algorithm determines a target platform has been killed. This action is performed instead of the default action (which is to remove the platform from the simulation, if possible) The variable DAMAGE, indicating the numeric value of the damage, is available when executing this script; however, this value should be equal to 1.0.

subCommands.description: When a position update is requested by the simulation, if the time since the previous update is less than or equal to this value then the mover will ignore the update.

subCommands.name: altitude_offset
subCommands.description: When set, this offset will offset the parent platform’s location by the given amount from the current waypoint’s altitude.

subCommands.name: at_end_of_path
subCommands.description: Specify the action to take when the mover reaches the end of its defined path.

subCommands.name: draw_route
subCommands.description: This command is the same as print_route, except the route text is not printed, only drawn with WsfDraw.

subCommands.name: on_turn_failure
subCommands.description: Defines the behavior of the mover when a point on a route cannot be reached exactly due to the turn radius.

subCommands.name: pathfinder
subCommands.description: The name of the pathfinder object to use.

subCommands.name: print_route
subCommands.description: When enabled, the route is printed to the screen whenever it is modified. Additionally, WsfDraw is used to output a visual of the route, which can be viewed with many visualization tools.

subCommands.name: start_at
subCommands.description: The label identifying the waypoint in the route to use as the starting location.

subCommands.name: start_time
subCommands.description: Indicates the platform is to start moving at the time specified. The current velocity is set to zero and once the simulation time is reached, the platform starts moving at the speed specified in the first waypoint. If an elapse time is desired at a waypoint, use the subcommand pause_time.

subCommands.name: switch_on_approach
subCommands.description: Switches to the next waypoint when approaching within one turn radius of the current target waypoint.

subCommands.name: switch_on_passing
subCommands.description: Switches to the next waypoint only when abreast of the current target waypoint.

subCommands.name: turn_failure_threshold
subCommands.description: Defines the threshold for which the on_turn_failure behavior is triggered, given as a ratio of the turn radius. For example, a turn_failure_threshold of 0.01 and a turn radius of 1000 meters, on_turn_failure logic would be triggered if the point is missed by more than 10 meters.

subCommands.name: use_route
subCommands.description: Supplies the name of the route to follow. The route is assumed to be a predefined absolute route.

subCommands.name: angle_of_attack_table
subCommands.description: speed <speed-value> angle <angle-value> speed <speed-value> angle <angle-value>

subCommands.name: altitude
subCommands.description: Specifies the altitude that the subsequent data is valid for. The altitude blocks must be in increasing numerical order. Linear interpolation of the altitude blocks is used.

subCommands.name: speed
subCommands.description: Specifies the speed that the listed angle of attack is valid for. The speed entries must be in increasing numerical order. The angle of attack will be computed using a linear interpolation of the speed data.

subCommands.name: angle
subCommands.description: The angle of attack. The angle of attack entries must be in increasing numerical order.

subCommands.name: bank_angle_limit
subCommands.description: The roll angle limit. Value must be between 0 degrees to 85 degrees. Used to calculate the maximum radial acceleration.

subCommands.name: body_g_limit
subCommands.description: The body g-limit. Value must be greater than the acceleration of earth’s gravity.

subCommands.name: heading_pursuit_gain
subCommands.description: The heading pursuit gain.

subCommands.name: maximum_climb_rate
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum climb rate and dive rate used when changing altitude. Other climb rates specified by waypoints or scripts are bounded by this value.

subCommands.name: maximum_flight_path_angle
subCommands.description: Specifies maximum flight path angle (angle of climb/dive). Value must be greater than or equal to 0.

subCommands.name: maximum_linear_acceleration
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum linear acceleration to use when acceleration is necessary. This value is used if the waypoint does not include a linear _acceleration specification.

subCommands.name: maximum_radial_acceleration
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum radial acceleration to use when turning. This value is used if the waypoint does not include a radial_acceleration specification.

subCommands.name: maximum_altitude
subCommands.description: Maximum altitude constraint.

subCommands.name: minimum_altitude
subCommands.description: Minimum altitude constraint.

subCommands.name: maximum_speed
subCommands.description: Maximum speed constraint. Value must be greater than 0.

subCommands.name: minimum_speed
subCommands.description: Minimum speed constraint. Value must be greater than or equal to 0.

subCommands.name: path_variance_radius
subCommands.description: This value will randomly vary the location of the waypoint within the radius given. A random bearing and distance are chosen and applied to the next waypoint when calculating the path.

subCommands.name: roll_rate_limit
subCommands.description: The roll rate limit. Value must be greater than 0. Note: When applied to a WSF_AIR_MOVER or other waypoint mover types, the roll rate will not affect the platform’s movement along a route. To affect route following behavior use maximum_radial_acceleration.

subCommands.name: speed_variance_percent
subCommands.description: This value will randomly vary the speed at each waypoint as the mover travels within +/- the pct given. Value must be greater than 0.

subCommands.name: turn_rate_limit
subCommands.description: The turn rate limit. Value must be greater than 0.

subCommands.name: no_pitch
subCommands.description: Restricts the mover from pitching the platform. This has no effect on kinematics.

subCommands.name: on_road
subCommands.description: Restricts the mover from rolling the platform. This has no effect on kinematics.

subCommands.name: off_road
subCommands.description: Turns off the ‘on_road’ option. This allows the platform to roll.

subCommands.name: path_compute_timestep
subCommands.description: Waypoint movers precompute movement along paths. This behavior forces turns to have a constant radius. If path_compute_timestep is specified as a positive value, the turn rate will update on that interval if any changes in speed occur.

subCommands.name: maximum_impact_speed
subCommands.description: Specify the maximum speed above which the associated platform intersects terrain and is considered ‘crashed into the ground’. A crashed platform will notify observers via the WsfSimulationObserver::CrashedIntoGround() method and remove itself from the simulation. If impact speed is below this maximum, the platform is considered to be ‘landing’. The default behavior is to always land, rather than crash.

name: WSF_AIR_TO_AIR_LAUNCH_COMPUTER
description: Specifies a separate file to include. This included file must contain the launch_computer_table block.

subCommands.name: load_table
subCommands.description: Specifies a separate file to include. This included file must contain the launch_computer_table block.

subCommands.name: launch_computer_table
subCommands.description: Specifies the data table for expected results for weapon engagements. This block may be included in-line in the launch computer block, and need not be in a separate file as in load_table above. All of the subcommand inputs listed below are to be embedded within this block.

subCommands.name: no_escape_manuever
subCommands.description: The acceleration used to define the target “turn tail to missile” evade tactic capability. Begins at missile launch.

subCommands.name: independent_variables
subCommands.description: This block contains the data that defines the valid ranges of each of the independent variables for the engagement. Each IV must be given in increasing values. If there are N shooter altitudes, M shooter Machs, P target altitudes, Q target Machs, R target aspect angles, and S target lead angles, then the intercept_results block must have NxMxPxQxRxS x 6 data values in it.

subCommands.name: shooter_altitudes
subCommands.description: Specifies the shooter altitudes. May be uneven but must be in increasing numerical order. (Minimum delta = 100.0 m)

subCommands.name: shooter_machs
subCommands.description: Specifies the shooter Mach numbers. May be uneven but must be in increasing numerical order. (Minimum delta = 0.05)

subCommands.name: target_altitudes
subCommands.description: Specifies the target altitudes. May be uneven but must be in increasing numerical order. (Minimum delta = 100.0 m)

subCommands.name: target_machs
subCommands.description: Specifies the target Mach numbers. May be uneven but must be in increasing numerical order. (Minimum delta = 0.05)

subCommands.name: target_aspect_angles
subCommands.description: Specifies the target aspect angles (nose on = 0 deg). May be uneven but must be in increasing numerical order. (Minimum delta = 2.0 deg)

subCommands.name: target_lead_angles
subCommands.description: Specifies the target lead angles. May be uneven but must be in increasing numerical order. (Minimum delta = 2.0 deg)

subCommands.name: target_lead_angle_limits
subCommands.description: Specifies the target lead angles using a shorten notation. This is an alternate to the previous target_lead_angles command. (Minimum delta = 2.0 deg)

subCommands.name: intercept_results
subCommands.description: This block contains all the data points that define the intercept envelope. There must be as many entries/lines as there are engagement conditions (see independent_variables). Any value of -1.0 indicates not-achievable. It is recommended that this data be generated using the LAR generator tool called weapon_tools.

subCommands.name: Rmin
subCommands.description: Minimum range and time-of-flight for this condition, below which intercept is unsuccessful.

subCommands.name: Rne
subCommands.description: No-escape range and time-of-flight for this condition.

subCommands.name: Rmax
subCommands.description: Maximum range and time-of-flight for this condition, beyond which intercept is unsuccessful.

name: WSF_ARGO8_MOVER
description: Specifies the ARGO library for the missile. Do not include the file extension (.so or .dll). These libraries sit in the library directory in the build.

subCommands.name: library_name
subCommands.description: Specifies the ARGO library for the missile. Do not include the file extension (.so or .dll). These libraries sit in the library directory in the build.

subCommands.name: missile_name
subCommands.description: Specifies name of missile. Necessary but doesn’t actually affect flyout so can be named anything.

subCommands.name: missile_type
subCommands.description: Specifies the ARGO missile model type to use. Currently standard will cover most Brawler missile models.

subCommands.name: argo_log_file_path
subCommands.description: Specifies the log file path in which to log the ARGO output too for debug purposes. Automatically turns on logging when specified.

subCommands.name: guidance_update_interval
subCommands.description: Specifies the update rate of guidance track data. Affects truth and track data rate. This rate is also dependent on sensor frame rate, if sensor frame rate polls at slower interval, the missile will not update at rate specified by this command.

subCommands.name: guidance_method
subCommands.description: Specifies whether to use truth or track data while the missile is being guided by the shooter. An uplink is not necessary for truth.

subCommands.name: seeker_method
subCommands.description: Specifies once seeker turns on whether it guides on truth or track. Seeker will turn on from argo output or if seeker is defined on missile, script user has control over when seeker turns on. Once the sensor turns on in script, the model will recognize it as on and no longer abide by the guidance update interval.

subCommands.name: output_fuze_data
subCommands.description: If included as command, will output fuze state for all missiles launched. If engagement of missile is ended through other means than the argo mover, no output will be displayed.

subCommands.name: endgame_gees
subCommands.description: Specifies minimum number of g’s at endgame is required for the missile to fuze.

name: WSF_BALLISTIC_MISSILE_LAUNCH_COMPUTER
description: Specify the file name to use when computing a launch solution associated with this missile. The launch computer assumes that the missile is computing a ground intercept.

subCommands.name: surface_to_surface_table
subCommands.description: Specify the file name to use when computing a launch solution associated with this missile. The launch computer assumes that the missile is computing a ground intercept.

subCommands.name: surface_to_air_table
subCommands.description: Specify the file name to use when computing a launch solution associated with this missile. The launch computer assumes that the missile is computing an air intercept.

subCommands.name: maximum_launch_slant_range
subCommands.description: Specify the maximum slant range to the target that is defined to be acceptable for launch. This is typically used to enforce the need for the target to be within range of a tracking sensor (assumed to be colocated with the launcher) at the time of launch.

subCommands.name: maximum_intercept_slant_range
subCommands.description: Specify the maximum allowable slant range to the intercept point. This is typically used to enforce the need for the target to be within the range of a tracking sensor (that is is colocated with the launcher) at the time of intercept.

subCommands.name: minimum_intercept_altitude
subCommands.description: Specify the minimum altitude at which a surface-to-air intercept is defined to be acceptable.

subCommands.name: maximum_intercept_altitude
subCommands.description: Specify the maximum altitude at which a surface-to-air intercept is defined to be acceptable.

subCommands.name: maximum_intercept_angle
subCommands.description: Specify the maximum intercept angle for which a surface-to-air intercept is defined to be acceptable. A value of 0 degrees represents a head-on impact while a value of 180 degrees is an impact from the rear.

subCommands.name: minimum_intercept_velocity
subCommands.description: Specify the minimum relative intercept velocity for which a surface-to-air intercept is defined to be acceptable.

subCommands.name: integration_timestep
subCommands.description: For surface-to-air launch solutions, specify the integration step for which the ballistic target representation is propagated forward in time. The smaller the time interval, the more accurate the forward ballistic representation, and the more accurate the launch solution will be. Typically this value should be of the same order as the time steps of entries in the launch computer’s table. For example if the time steps in the table are spaced 0.1 sec apart, a good value would also be 0.1 sec.

subCommands.name: ground_range_sample_interval
subCommands.description: Specify the sample interval for creating the internal surface-to-air intercept table.

subCommands.name: allow_boost_phase_intercept
subCommands.description: Specify if intercepts are allowed during boost phase. By default intercept calculations are not performed while the target is still in ‘boost phase’ because trajectory prediction is very inaccurate. Setting this to ‘true’ allows intercepts to be attempted.

subCommands.name: compute_end_point
subCommands.description: Specify if the launch computer should compute the weapon ‘end point and time’ for surface-to-air intercept calculations. The ‘end point and time’ is an estimate of where the weapon (interceptor) would hit the Earth’s surface if it followed a ballistic trajectory and did not hit its intended target. The results can be extracted using the methods described in WsfLaunchComputer.

subCommands.name: predicted_trajectory_error_limit
subCommands.description: Specify the maximum allowable error between the predicted target trajectory and the actual target trajectory before forcing a recalculation of the predicted target trajectory.

subCommands.name: show_graphics
subCommands.description: For surface-to-air engagements, show graphics for maximum kinematic envelope, projected ballistic trajectory, intercept calculation, and intercept points (these graphical displays are drawn in many visualization tools). The kinematic envelope shows the maximum extent to which intercepts can occur from the parent platform’s launcher, displayed in cyan. Projected ballistic trajectory is drawn in green when an initial intercept time is calculated, and a green point is plotted at the first possible intercept point. Otherwise, for detailed intercept solutions, the trajectories are plotted in red, with red points indicating test points at which the launch computer attempts to calculate a solution (these may not be valid, however). Valid intercept points are plotted along these red trajectories in purple.

subCommands.name: show_results
subCommands.description: Show the results of a surface-to-air or surface-to-surface intercept calculation. If successful, the intercept point and loft angle / burn time will be displayed on the standard output and will be transmitted/saved in the DIS stream as a comment.

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: In addition to show_results, display detailed information associated with the determination of the launch solution.

subCommands.name: aero
subCommands.description: Specify the name of the aero type to be used for computing drag data.

subCommands.name: mass

description: Specifies a table that maps signal-to-noise-ratio values to message transfer rates. The SNR-Transfer-Rate table will be interpolated. If a table is specified, the table transfer rate values will override the value specified with the transfer_rate command.

subCommands.name: snr_transfer_rate_table
subCommands.description: Specifies a table that maps signal-to-noise-ratio values to message transfer rates. The SNR-Transfer-Rate table will be interpolated. If a table is specified, the table transfer rate values will override the value specified with the transfer_rate command.

subCommands.name: bit_error_probability
subCommands.description: Optional parameter that defines the system designed bit error rate probability. It is used to pick the Eb/No values from the Eb/No vs. BER table. Must be greater than or equal to zero.

subCommands.name: error_correction
subCommands.description: Optional parameter that determines how much error correction will be applied when using Eb/No to calculate data rate. Must be between 0.0 and 1.0. Units are assumed dB.

subCommands.name: bit_error_rate_ebno_table
subCommands.description: Optional table that defines the Energy per Bit to the Spectral Noise Density (Eb/No) vs. Bit Error Rate (BER). Used in conjunction with the bit_error_probability and error_correction to calculate the data transfer rate over the medium. When using this table Data Rate = SNR* Error Correction * ( Bandwidth / Eb/No ). The Bit-Error-Rate-EbNo-Table will be interpolated. If a table is specified, the table transfer rate values will override the value specified with the transfer_rate command.

name: WSF_COMM_ROUTER_PROTOCOL_OSPF
description: Defines the area this comm/router belongs to in the OSPF AS. Multiple areas may be assigned if this member has a direct connection to another member in that area, defining this member as a “border router”.

subCommands.name: ospf_area
subCommands.description: Defines the area this comm/router belongs to in the OSPF AS. Multiple areas may be assigned if this member has a direct connection to another member in that area, defining this member as a “border router”.

subCommands.name: remove_ospf_area
subCommands.description: Removes an area defined for this protocol. Specifically provided for editing derived objects in input.

subCommands.name: backbone
subCommands.description: Defines the specified area as a backbone. This only has to be done on a protocol instance for this setting to be applied across an entire OSPF connected AS.

subCommands.name: remove_backbone
subCommands.description: This command removes the backbone specification for this protocol type or instance. Used in cases where a protocol type is inherited from, but the specified backbone setting is not wanted.

subCommands.name: ospf_dr_priority
subCommands.description: Sets the priority for this router becoming the “designated router” or “backup designated router” (DR, BDR) for its network within an area. These routers hold all of the detailed routing data for a specific area as common points of communication for all other routers in the same network. This value must be positive, where a lower value indicates a higher priority. This value also affects subsequent re-selection of these routers dynamically at runtime. Any router entering a network and area does not preempt any already established DR or BDR, even if it has a higher priority.

subCommands.name: hello_interval
subCommands.description: Defines the amount of time between sending the OSPF heartbeat, the “hello” packet. If these are not received before the defined hold time, the router will be considered non-connected or non-functional and removed from network state data for routing purposes. In addition, this defines how soon a new member is detected, as this is also the method in which new members are detected.

subCommands.name: hold_timer
subCommands.description: Defines the amount of time that before a member is dropped if a hello packet is not received. Note that the default value allows multiple hello packet transmission windows before actually being dropped due to hold time. Ensure that this value is greater than the hello_interval to avoid dropping all members from network state knowledge.

name: WSF_COMM_ROUTER_PROTOCOL_RIPv2
description: Specifies how often a router will send an update to other routers. As specified for the RIPv2 spec (RFC 2543), this is base time. Each time an update is scheduled, the time can change by +/- 5 seconds.

subCommands.name: update_interval
subCommands.description: Specifies how often a router will send an update to other routers. As specified for the RIPv2 spec (RFC 2543), this is base time. Each time an update is scheduled, the time can change by +/- 5 seconds.

subCommands.name: invalidation_timeout
subCommands.description: The amount of time that must pass before a route is marked as inactive. Once a router has not been heard from for this amount of time, routes learned from that router are marked as inactive.

subCommands.name: garbage_collection_timeout
subCommands.description: The amount of time that once a route has been marked as inactive, it will be purged from the routing table.

subCommands.name: poisoned_reverse
subCommands.description: Specifies whether to use split horizon, or split horizon with poisoned reverse. Split horizon is a scheme for avoiding sending routes in updates to routers from which they were learned. Poisoned reverse includes such routes in updates, but sets their metrics to be unusable.

name: WSF_COMPOSITE_SENSOR
description: Defines how the constituent sensors are managed.

subCommands.name: operating_mode
subCommands.description: Defines how the constituent sensors are managed.

subCommands.name: sensor
subCommands.description: Defines the name of a constituent sensor. This command must be repeated one or more times specifying the names of the ‘constituent’ sensors that make up the ‘composite’ sensor. In general, all of the constituent sensors should be of the same general type. At the current time the sensors should be a type that reports tracks (WSF_RADAR_SENSOR, WSF_IRST_SENSOR, WSF_PASSIVE_SENSOR).

subCommands.name: filter
subCommands.description: Defines a filter to be applied to the stream of tracks for a target when the operating_mode is independent.

subCommands.name: track_quality
subCommands.description: Specifies the track quality to be assigned to the composite tracks produced by this sensor when the operating_mode is independent. This value is used only if it is greater than zero. If the value is zero then the track quality for the constituent tracks will be used.
