subCommands.description: Use the coverage grid with the given name as the grid over which this coverage will be computed.

subCommands.name: assets
subCommands.description: Specify the free assets to use for this coverage.

subCommands.name: platform
subCommands.description: Specify the platform with the given name is to be included among the free assets for this coverage. Unless ‘none’ is supplied as the device name, the given platform must have a relevant device with the given name.

subCommands.name: platform_type
subCommands.description: Specify that all platforms with the given type are to be included among the free assets for this coverage. Unless ‘none’ is supplied as the device name, the given platform type must have a relevant device with the given name.

subCommands.name: category

subCommands.name: group
subCommands.description: Specify that any platform in the given group with a relevant device are to be included among the free assets for this coverage. If ‘none’ is specified as the device name, then all platforms in this group will be added to the set of free assets for this coverage.

subCommands.description: Set the start of the coverage interval to the given simulation time. Either this command or start_epoch can be used to specify the coverage interval’s start time. If no start time is specified the coverage interval’s start is set to the simulation’s start time.

subCommands.name: end_time
subCommands.description: Set the end time of the coverage interval to the given simulation time. Either this command or end_epoch can be used to specify the coverage interval’s end time. If no end time is specified the coverage interval’s end is set to the simulation’s end time.

subCommands.name: start_epoch

subCommands.name: end_epoch

subCommands.description: Set the size of the grid. The first value gives the number of rows in the grid. The second value gives the number of points in each row. The resulting number of grid points will be the product of the two provided values.

subCommands.name: step_distance
subCommands.description: Specify the distance between adjacent grid points. The first value gives the separation distance between one row and the next. The second value gives the separation distance between points in the same row.

subCommands.name: origin_index
subCommands.description: Specify the position in the grid that is at the location given by the origin command. These values start from 0 and count from the south west corner. For example:

subCommands.name: origin
subCommands.description: Set the origin point in the grid, the point from which the other rows and members in each row are spaced. There will be one row in the grid at the given latitude, and there will be one point in each row of the grid at the given longitude.

subCommands.name: altitude
subCommands.description: Set the altitude of the grid points. <altitude-reference> can be either ‘msl’, in which case the altitude refers to a height above the mean sea level, or ‘agl’, in which case the altitude refers to a height above the ground level set by any terrain in the scenario.

subCommands.name: asset
subCommands.description: Specify the assets associated with this grid will be instances of <platform-type> and will use the device with the name <device-name>. The given <device-name> may also be ‘none’ if the grid points are passive targets for the coverage computation in question.

subCommands.name: background_radiance_below_horizon

If the target is within the transition region defined by these angles, the resulting background radiance will be linearly interpolated between the above horizon and below horizon values.

description: Defines how the ESM sensor reports target type information in tracks.

subCommands.name: reported_target_type
subCommands.description: Defines how the ESM sensor reports target type information in tracks.

subCommands.name: default_time_to_declare
subCommands.description: Defines the duration of time after the initial detection that is required to make a determination of the target type.

subCommands.name: default_time_to_reevaluate
subCommands.description: Defines the time interval used for reevaluating the identification of the target. A value of 0 seconds indicates no reevaluation will take place.

subCommands.name: type
subCommands.description: Specifies the truth type to which the following subcommands apply.

subCommands.name: default_type
subCommands.description: Specifies that the following type subcommands apply for any type not defined with the type command.

subCommands.name: time_to_declare
subCommands.description: Defines the duration of time after the initial detection that is required to make a determination of the target type.

subCommands.name: time_to_reevaluate
subCommands.description: Defines the time interval used for reevaluating the identification of the target.

subCommands.name: report_type
subCommands.description: Defines the reporting type-name as the target type based on the listed emitter-type(s) being reported in the emitter list. Currently exact matches between the emitter’s defined for the report_type and a track’s emitter list must happen for the given report_type to be reported. If there are differences another report_type or the default_type will be reported.

subCommands.name: report_type
subCommands.description: Defines the probability of reporting type-name as the target type. The probability parameter is a value between 0.0 and 1.0. Any number of report_type commands may be specified as long as the probability parameters add up to 1.0. For greater ease of use, the value remainder may be used as the probability parameter to specify whatever value is required to add up to 1.0.

subCommands.name: report_truth
subCommands.description: Specifies that the sensor will report the truth type. This is only valid under the default_type command.

subCommands.name: reported_emitter_type
subCommands.description: Defines how the ESM sensor reports emitter type information in tracks.

subCommands.name: default_time_to_reevaluate

subCommands.description: Specifies that the sensor will report the truth type. This is only valid under the default_type command.

subCommands.name: unframed_detection_optimization
subCommands.description: This command indicates if unframed detection optimization will be used. If enabled, once the sensor successfully detects a given transmitter within a frame, subsequent attempts to detect the same transmitter in the same frame will be suppressed. For instance, if multiple messages are sent from a single transmitter during the ESM frame, the ESM sensor will only report on the first message that it can detect (if any). If the first message cannot be detected because of transmitter antenna pointing, it will report the second message if it can be detected, an so on.

subCommands.name: unframed_detection_coast_time
subCommands.description: If the ESM sensor is running at a faster frame time than the sensors it is trying to detect, it may detect the transmitter one frame and not the next. This can cause a lot of track creation and deletion. This value indicates how long a successful detection from a transmitter will be reported.

subCommands.name: frequency_band
subCommands.description: Defines a band of frequencies this sensor can detect. This command may be specified more than once if the sensor can detect multiple bands.

subCommands.name: revisit_time
subCommands.description: These two commands pertain to the immediately preceding frequency_band and define how long the sensor dwells in the band and the interval between dwells. These commands are effectively only when the scan_on_scan_model is enabled and are used to determine the temporal probability that the sensor would be looking at the frequency of the target emitter when a detection chance occurs.

subCommands.name: detection_sensitivity
subCommands.description: Defines the minimum signal strength that can be ‘reliably’ detected. If detection_probability is defined then this is the signal strength that would result in a Pd of 0.5. If detection_probability is not defined then this defines the signal strength for which a successful detection will be declared.

subCommands.name: detection_sensitivities
subCommands.description: This command allows the definition of frequency-dependent or signal-type- and frequency-dependent detection sensitivities.

subCommands.name: detection_threshold
subCommands.description: This is an alternative to detection_sensitivity. It defines the minimum signal-to-noise ratio that can be ‘reliably’ detected. If detection_probability is defined then this is the signal-to-noise ratio that would result in a Pd of 0.5. If detection_probability is not defined then this defines the signal-to-noise ratio for which a successful detection will be declared.

subCommands.name: detection_thresholds
subCommands.description: This command allows the definition of frequency-dependent or signal-type- and frequency-dependent detection thresholds.

subCommands.name: detection_probability
subCommands.description: Defines a function of probability of detection (Pd) versus received signal strength (expressed as a ratio of the received power to the detection sensitivity). The table is defined as follows:

subCommands.name: scan_on_scan_model
subCommands.description: Specifies if the Probabilistic Scan-On-Scan (PSOS) model should be employed. This model attempts to probabilistically capture the temporal effects in which the ESM sensor is scanning in frequency and the emitter may be scanning in angle.

subCommands.name: range_error_sigma_table
subCommands.description: These commands provide the ability to define error sigmas that are a function of the frequency of the received signal instead of the fixed sigmas that are provided by the single-valued azimuth_error_sigma, elevation_error_sigma and range_error_sigma commands. The points define a curve on a plot whose x-axis is the log_10 of the frequency and the y-axis is the error sigma. Linear interpolation is used to derive the values for intermediate frequencies. Signals whose frequencies are outside the range of the table use the value from the appropriate endpoint (i.e., extrapolation is not performed).

subCommands.description: If the ranging time is used to generate a track with range information, this parameter controls the track quality once range is valid. The quality-value must be non-negative.

name: WSF_EXCHANGE_PROCESSOR
description: A tender of ‘commodity’ is to propose an exchange of some named tangible goods, noting the kind, amount, and rate of a planned requested or offered exchange. It does _not_ specify the direction of flow, which is dictated by the transactor is_offeror or is_requestor setting.

subCommands.name: commodity
subCommands.description: A tender of ‘commodity’ is to propose an exchange of some named tangible goods, noting the kind, amount, and rate of a planned requested or offered exchange. It does _not_ specify the direction of flow, which is dictated by the transactor is_offeror or is_requestor setting.

subCommands.name: service
subCommands.description: A tender of ‘service’ is to propose an exchange of some named intangible service, noting the kind, amount, and rate of a planned requested or offered exchange. It does _not_ specify the direction of flow, which is dictated by the transactor is_offeror or is_requestor setting.

subCommands.name: quantity
subCommands.description: Specifies the current number of services available or desired.

subCommands.name: maximum_quantity
subCommands.description: Specifies the limiting number of services available or desired. Syntactical convenience to indicate the maximum size of a container (see below).

subCommands.name: mass_quantity
subCommands.description: Specifies the current mass of commodity available or desired.

subCommands.name: maximum_mass_quantity
subCommands.description: Specifies the limiting quantity of commodity available or desired. Syntactical convenience to indicate the maximum size of a container (see below).

subCommands.name: rate
subCommands.description: Specifies the rate of services offered per unit time.

subCommands.name: service_interval
subCommands.description: Specifies the time required to accomplish a unit of service. 30 minutes = Two repairs per hour.

subCommands.name: mass_rate
subCommands.description: Specifies the rate of commodities exchanged services offered per unit time. The real value must be followed with a correct mass rate specification, such as kg/sec, etc.

subCommands.name: container
subCommands.description: The <container-name> specifies the name of the object, as a way for the WSF_EXCHANGE_PROCESSOR to differentiate between perhaps several containers owned by the processor. The container block quantifies a container; its name, what it holds, maximum, and current quantities of the commodity or service. While a service (i.e. engine-repair) is not a tangible to be held in a container, for the purposes of simulation book-keeping, it is treated as such. Transactions are always “piped” into or out of a named container. No transaction is permitted which transfers more of a commodity or service than may be added to or decremented from a container, given its maximum capacity and current quantity. A constraining operation will always bound/clamp the transaction to abide by the container’s constraint. Any convenient number of containers may be defined as needed, and a container may have more than one transaction “piped” into it, such as a tanker aircraft which may both on-load fuel from another tanker and offload fuel to a receiver simultaneously, both linked to the same container.

subCommands.name: service

subCommands.name: transactor
subCommands.description: The <transactor-name> specifies the name of the object, as a way for the WSF_EXCHANGE_PROCESSOR to differentiate between perhaps several transactors owned by the processor. The transactor block quantifies a transaction; its name, the direction of flow of the commodity or service, and current quantities of the transaction in-progress. Regardless of direction, quantities tend toward zero as the transaction progresses (is_offeror starts with amount available and reaches zero when exhausted, is_requestor starts with amount desired and reaches zero as fully satisfied). Transactions are always “piped” into or out of a named container. Regardless of the initial amount of Reserve() or Request(), the transaction starts only after being constrained to what may come from or fit into the named container.

subCommands.name: is_requestor

subCommands.name: hook_to_payload

If a request is received, and a corresponding offer is sent out, and then no response is subsequently received, the offer is canceled after this period of time, in order to allow the transactor to be freed up to offer to another requestor.

(See example input above.) Other bits may indicate that fuel or payload can be provided, but only if they are properly indicated with the keyword above. Multiple pairings may be provided.

subCommands.name: service_and_capability_pairing

subCommands.description: Restricts the mover from pitching the platform. This has no effect on kinematics.

subCommands.name: on_road
subCommands.description: Restricts the mover from rolling the platform. This has no effect on kinematics.

subCommands.name: off_road
subCommands.description: Turns off the ‘on_road’ option. This allows the platform to roll.

subCommands.name: path_compute_timestep
subCommands.description: Waypoint movers precompute movement along paths. This behavior forces turns to have a constant radius. If path_compute_timestep is specified as a positive value, the turn rate will update on that interval if any changes in speed occur.

name: WSF_GUIDANCE_COMPUTER
description: Specifies that information should be written to standard output whenever a phase or stage transition occurs.

subCommands.name: show_status
subCommands.description: Specifies that information should be written to standard output whenever a phase or stage transition occurs.

subCommands.name: show_diagnostics
subCommands.description: Specifies that diagnostic information from guidance programs should be written to standard output. This is typically used when attempting to tune the guidance computer for generating orbital launch computers with weapon_tools.

subCommands.name: show_commands
subCommands.description: Specifies that calls from script commands should be written to standard output.

subCommands.name: show_evaluations
subCommands.description: Specifies that phase change rule evaluations should be written to standard output.

subCommands.name: guide_to_truth
subCommands.description: Specifies if the guidance target should be the location specified in the current target track (false), or should be the true location of the platform specified in the current target track (true).

subCommands.name: phase
subCommands.description: The ‘phase’ block is used to define the guidance for the various phases of flight and the rules to transition between phases.

subCommands.name: edit
subCommands.description: This command is typically used when creating a new guidance computer type by deriving from another guidance computer type.

subCommands.name: program
subCommands.description: Defines a guidance program with the specified <name> using the predefine guidance program <type> (See Guidance Program Types.) The program can then be selected for use in a phase by specifying use_program <name>.

subCommands.name: guidance_delay
subCommands.description: Specifies the elapsed time since the start of the phase when guidance commands should start being computed. This is useful during lift-off and other phases where pursuit of the target is not desirable.

subCommands.name: on_entry
subCommands.description: These commands define scripts to be executed when entering and exiting the phase.

subCommands.name: on_update
subCommands.description: Define a script to be executed on every phase update.

subCommands.name: guidance_target
subCommands.description: Overrides the top-level guide_to_truth command for the current phase. This is expanded to include the options:

subCommands.name: aimpoint_altitude_offset
subCommands.description: Modify the aimpoint to be above or below the perceived target location. This is typically used to create an air burst.

subCommands.name: aimpoint_azimuth_offset
subCommands.description: These commands provide a method to produce an aimpoint that is laterally offset from the perceived target location. This is typically used to meet some tactical requirement.

subCommands.name: aimpoint_evaluation_interval
subCommands.description: Controls how often a new aimpoint is computed when using aimpoint_azimuth_offset and aimpoint_range_offset. This is a fairly time-consuming operation that does not need to be performed on every call to the guidance computer.

subCommands.name: allow_route_following
subCommands.description: If true, the computer will follow a route if it has been provided to the associated mover. If the mover does not have a route then this command has no effect. Conventional target point selection will resume at the end of the route.

subCommands.name: use_program
subCommands.description: Specifies that the named program defined in a program block outside of the phase will be used. It is useful to define a program if it is going to be used in multiple phases.

subCommands.name: program
subCommands.description: Defines a program of the specified <type> and uses it for the current phase. <type> must be one of the predefined guidance program types (see Guidance Program Types.)

subCommands.name: proportional_navigation_gain
subCommands.description: Specifies the gain for proportional navigation. A value of zero indicates proportional navigation will not be performed.

subCommands.name: proportional_navigation_limit_angle
subCommands.description: Specifies the 3D aspect angle of the target with respect to the weapon at which the navigation method will switch between proportional and velocity pursuit. Proportional navigation will be used if the target aspect angle is less than or equal to this value, otherwise velocity pursuit will be used.

subCommands.name: proportional_navigation_method
subCommands.description: Specifies whether additional acceleration should be commanded because of current target acceleration.

subCommands.name: velocity_pursuit_gain
subCommands.description: Specifies the gain for velocity pursuit navigation. A value of zero indicates velocity pursuit navigation will not be performed.

subCommands.name: g_bias
subCommands.description: Specifies the bias factor used to overcome gravity. This is typically used during mid-course to prevent the trajectory from sagging. If zero is specified then gravity bias will not be applied.

subCommands.name: lateral_g_bias
subCommands.description: Specifies the bias factor used skew the horizontal component of the trajectory in a particular direction. If zero is specified then gravity bias will not be applied.

subCommands.name: commanded_altitude
subCommands.description: Specifies a commanded altitude. Typically used to climb or dive to a cruise altitude and hold the altitude. The altitude reference tag (’msl’, or ‘above mean sea level’; ‘agl’, or ‘above ground level’) may be omitted, in which case ‘msl’ is assumed.

subCommands.name: commanded_azimuth_offset
subCommands.description: Specifies the azimuth angle to the target that should be maintained. The angle is defined to be the angle in the local horizontal plane between the weapon velocity vector and the line-of-sight vector from the weapon to the target. (This is consistent with the ‘target_azimuth’ conditional tests in the next_phase command.)

subCommands.name: commanded_flight_path_angle
subCommands.description: Specifies a commanded flight path angle. If from_launch_computer is specified then the value produced by the launch computer will be used (if present).

subCommands.name: commanded_mach
subCommands.description: Specifies the commanded speed/mach to be used during this phase. Typically used for cruise.

subCommands.name: commanded_throttle
subCommands.description: Specifies a throttle factor in the range [0..1] that overrides and throttle specification in the mover.

subCommands.name: maximum_commanded_g
subCommands.description: Specifies the magnitude of the maximum acceleration that can be commanded.

subCommands.name: maximum_ascent_rate
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum rate of ascent or descent to be used to reach the commanded_altitude.

subCommands.name: maximum_pitch_angle
subCommands.description: Specifies the absolute value of the maximum flight path angle that may be used to ascend or descend to the commanded_altitude.

subCommands.name: pitch_change_gain
subCommands.description: Specifies the gain factor for changing the pitch angle when trying to achieve the commanded_altitude.

subCommands.name: next_phase
subCommands.description: The next_phase command defines a condition under which a phase transition occurs. A phase block may have multiple next_phase commands to define a number of conditions that might trigger a phase change. The next_phase commands are evaluated on each guidance update and are evaluated in the order specified.

name: WSF_GUIDED_MOVER
description: Specifies the integration timestep to be used. If a value of zero is specified the mover will not break update requests into smaller intervals.

subCommands.name: integration_timestep
subCommands.description: Specifies the integration timestep to be used. If a value of zero is specified the mover will not break update requests into smaller intervals.

subCommands.name: integration_method
subCommands.description: Select the method for integrating the equations of motion as one of the following:

subCommands.name: compute_all_forces_each_substep
subCommands.description: Specify whether Runge-Kutta methods should compute all forces for each integration sub-step. If this is false, then only the gravitational force will be computed for each sub-step, and the aerodynamic and thrust forces will be computed once from the state at the start of the integration step. This option is ignored when the integration_method is trapezoidal. The default value for this option is false, which matches how the WSF_GUIDED_MOVER had been implemented in pre-2.9 versions of AFSIM.

subCommands.name: coordinate_frame
subCommands.description: Specify the coordinate frame in which the equations of motion are integrated as either:

subCommands.name: maintain_inclination
subCommands.description: When modeling an orbital launch vehicle (using coordinate_frame eci), the inclination of the parking orbit is a function of the launch latitude and launch azimuth (or heading). For a non-rotating spherical Earth, the inclination of the orbit is defined by:

subCommands.name: show_status
subCommands.description: Causes a message to be written to standard output whenever a staging operation takes place. This is automatically enabled if debug is also enabled.

subCommands.name: show_trajectory
subCommands.description: Enables a printout of downrange distance, speed, Mach number, and applied aerodynamic forces to standard output.

subCommands.name: align_heading_with_velocity
subCommands.description: If true, use the velocity of the owning platform (if non-zero) to determine the projected heading. Otherwise, use orientation.

subCommands.name: check_for_ground_impact
subCommands.description: Enables internal checking for ground impact. This can be used where the mover is simply being used to model an orbital launch vehicle or the spent stage of a rocket. Formerly one had to define an instance of WSF_GROUND_TARGET_FUSE on such platforms to detect if they crashed into the ground. If this was not done the platform would keep going and never be deleted.

subCommands.name: time_history_path
subCommands.description: If specified, indicates the path.

subCommands.name: aero
subCommands.description: Specifies the aerodynamics type name for this stage. Type must be known at initialization time.

subCommands.name: empty_mass
subCommands.description: Specifies the mass of the stage without fuel.

subCommands.name: fuel_mass
subCommands.description: Specifies the mass of the fuel on the stage.

subCommands.name: total_mass
subCommands.description: Specifies the total mass of the stage, which is the sum of empty_mass and fuel_mass but does not include the mass of any upper stages on top of this one (considered payload).

subCommands.name: vacuum_thrust
subCommands.description: Specifies the thrust of the propulsion system.

subCommands.name: vacuum_thrust_table
subCommands.description: Defines thrust as a function of time.

subCommands.name: reverse_thrust
subCommands.description: Indicates the thrust is to be applied in the reverse direction (i.e., it is acting as a braking force instead of a propelling force).

subCommands.name: vacuum_specific_impulse
subCommands.description: Specify the specific impulse of the propulsion system with respect to a particular condition.

subCommands.name: nozzle_exit_area
subCommands.description: Specifies the exit area of the engine nozzle. This is used to adjust a sea level or vacuum reference thrust or specific impulse values from the reference value to the value at the current operating altitude.

subCommands.name: thrust_duration
subCommands.description: Specifies the amount of time the engine will produce the specified thrust.

subCommands.name: burn_rate
subCommands.description: Specifies the propellant burn rate while thrusting.

subCommands.name: burn_rate_table
subCommands.description: Defines propellant burn rate as a function of time.

subCommands.name: throttle
subCommands.description: This provides a function to adjust the current thrust and burn rate (The adjustment is just a multiplication). The dependent value is the non-dimensional throttle factor is greater than or equal to zero. A value of zero corresponds to no thrust and one corresponds to full thrust. Values greater than one are allowed when the base thrust and burn rate values are less than the maximum.

subCommands.name: thrust_vectoring_angle_limit
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum angle to which the thrust vector can be steered.

subCommands.name: thrust_vectoring_time_limits
subCommands.description: Specifies the minimum and maximum times (relative to the ignition time of the current stage) in which thrust vectoring can be employed.

subCommands.name: lateral_thrust_gain
subCommands.description: Lateral forces may be applied by vectoring the thrust of the engine or through the use of thrusters. These forces typically typically have a large moment arm (the engine is at the end of a rocket and is some distance from the center of gravity) and as such, introduces a rotation which then causes a change in the direction of the velocity vector. This issue is that this model treats the body as a point-mass (See Overview) and does not consider angular rates - it operates by ‘pushing’ the mass to change direction. It takes more force to ‘push’ the mass to change direction by a given angle than it takes to rotate the same amount. Because more force is needed, a higher vectoring angle is needed, thus stealing more thrust from the axial component.

subCommands.name: divert_thrust
subCommands.description: Specifies the amount of thrust to be considered available from thrusters. The ‘divert’ capability is a trivial implementation of real thrusters. It was initially provided so vehicles could still maneuver at high altitudes where available aerodynamic forces are small or non-existent.

subCommands.name: divert_fuel_mass
subCommands.description: Specifies the initial mass of fuel available for divert thrust. When divert_thrust is used it will expend the divert fuel until it is no longer available.

subCommands.name: divert_fuel_flow_rate
subCommands.description: Specifies the rate at which the divert fuel will be used when full divert thrust is employed. If only some of the divert thrust is required to satisfy the current request then the fuel flow rate will be decreased proportionally.

subCommands.name: divert_altitude_limits
subCommands.description: Specifies the minimum and maximum altitudes in which divert thrust will be considered for use.

subCommands.name: pre_ignition_coast_time
subCommands.description: Specifies the amount of time that will elapse between the start of the stage and when the engine will ignite.

subCommands.name: pre_separation_coast_time
subCommands.description: Specifies the amount of time that will elapse between the burnout of this stage and its separation from the vehicle. This command has no effect for single-stage vehicles or the last stage of a multistage vehicle.

subCommands.name: integration_timestep
subCommands.description: Specifies the integration timestep for this stage.

subCommands.name: ignition_failure_probability
subCommands.description: A value in the range [ 0 .. 1 ] that specifies the probability that the engines on this stage will fail to ignite. If ignition fails the results are as follows:

subCommands.name: separation_failure_probability
subCommands.description: A value in the range [ 0 .. 1 ] that specifies the probability that this stage will be unable to separate from the succeeding stage. If separation fails the results are as follows:

subCommands.name: angle_of_attack
subCommands.description: By default the model simply aligns the platform with the velocity vector with no angle-of-attack (See Overview). This provides a mechanism to apply an angle of attack.

subCommands.name: skid_to_turn
subCommands.description: By default the model simply aligns the vehicle with the velocity vector with no roll (See Overview) ‘bank_to_turn’ indicates that a bank angle should be imposed. This angle is proportional to the amount of sideways aerodynamic forces being applied.

subCommands.name: on_stage_ignition
subCommands.description: Process the ignition of stage ‘aStage’.

subCommands.name: on_stage_burnout
subCommands.description: Process the burnout of stage ‘aStage’.

subCommands.name: on_stage_separation
subCommands.description: Process the separation of stage ‘aStage’.

subCommands.description: Indicates the thrust is to be applied in the reverse direction (i.e., it is acting as a braking force instead of a propelling force).

subCommands.name: vacuum_specific_impulse
subCommands.description: Specify the specific impulse of the propulsion system with respect to a particular condition.

subCommands.name: nozzle_exit_area
subCommands.description: Specifies the exit area of the engine nozzle. This is used to adjust a sea level or vacuum reference thrust or specific impulse values from the reference value to the value at the current operating altitude.

subCommands.name: thrust_duration
subCommands.description: Specifies the amount of time the engine will produce the specified thrust.

subCommands.name: burn_rate
subCommands.description: Specifies the propellant burn rate while thrusting.

subCommands.name: burn_rate_table
subCommands.description: Defines propellant burn rate as a function of time.

subCommands.name: throttle
subCommands.description: This provides a function to adjust the current thrust and burn rate (The adjustment is just a multiplication). The dependent value is the non-dimensional throttle factor is greater than or equal to zero. A value of zero corresponds to no thrust and one corresponds to full thrust. Values greater than one are allowed when the base thrust and burn rate values are less than the maximum.

subCommands.name: thrust_vectoring_angle_limit
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum angle to which the thrust vector can be steered.

subCommands.name: thrust_vectoring_time_limits
subCommands.description: Specifies the minimum and maximum times (relative to the ignition time of the current stage) in which thrust vectoring can be employed.

subCommands.name: lateral_thrust_gain
subCommands.description: Lateral forces may be applied by vectoring the thrust of the engine or through the use of thrusters. These forces typically typically have a large moment arm (the engine is at the end of a rocket and is some distance from the center of gravity) and as such, introduces a rotation which then causes a change in the direction of the velocity vector. This issue is that this model treats the body as a point-mass (See Overview) and does not consider angular rates - it operates by ‘pushing’ the mass to change direction. It takes more force to ‘push’ the mass to change direction by a given angle than it takes to rotate the same amount. Because more force is needed, a higher vectoring angle is needed, thus stealing more thrust from the axial component.

subCommands.name: divert_thrust
subCommands.description: Specifies the amount of thrust to be considered available from thrusters. The ‘divert’ capability is a trivial implementation of real thrusters. It was initially provided so vehicles could still maneuver at high altitudes where available aerodynamic forces are small or non-existent.

subCommands.name: divert_fuel_mass
subCommands.description: Specifies the initial mass of fuel available for divert thrust. When divert_thrust is used it will expend the divert fuel until it is no longer available.

subCommands.name: divert_fuel_flow_rate
subCommands.description: Specifies the rate at which the divert fuel will be used when full divert thrust is employed. If only some of the divert thrust is required to satisfy the current request then the fuel flow rate will be decreased proportionally.

subCommands.name: divert_altitude_limits
subCommands.description: Specifies the minimum and maximum altitudes in which divert thrust will be considered for use.

subCommands.name: pre_ignition_coast_time
subCommands.description: Specifies the amount of time that will elapse between the start of the stage and when the engine will ignite.

subCommands.name: pre_separation_coast_time
subCommands.description: Specifies the amount of time that will elapse between the burnout of this stage and its separation from the vehicle. This command has no effect for single-stage vehicles or the last stage of a multistage vehicle.

subCommands.name: integration_timestep
subCommands.description: Specifies the integration timestep for this stage.

subCommands.name: ignition_failure_probability
subCommands.description: A value in the range [ 0 .. 1 ] that specifies the probability that the engines on this stage will fail to ignite. If ignition fails the results are as follows:

subCommands.name: separation_failure_probability
subCommands.description: A value in the range [ 0 .. 1 ] that specifies the probability that this stage will be unable to separate from the succeeding stage. If separation fails the results are as follows:

subCommands.name: angle_of_attack
subCommands.description: By default the model simply aligns the platform with the velocity vector with no angle-of-attack (See Overview). This provides a mechanism to apply an angle of attack.

subCommands.name: skid_to_turn
subCommands.description: By default the model simply aligns the vehicle with the velocity vector with no roll (See Overview) ‘bank_to_turn’ indicates that a bank angle should be imposed. This angle is proportional to the amount of sideways aerodynamic forces being applied.

subCommands.name: on_stage_ignition
subCommands.description: Process the ignition of stage ‘aStage’.

subCommands.name: on_stage_burnout
subCommands.description: Process the burnout of stage ‘aStage’.

subCommands.name: on_stage_separation
subCommands.description: Process the separation of stage ‘aStage’.

subCommands.name: velocity

subCommands.description: Specify the epoch that corresponds with the reference epoch at which the orbital elements are valid.

subCommands.description: Specify the eccentricity of the orbit. The specified value must be greater than or equal to zero (circular orbit).

subCommands.name: semi_major_axis
subCommands.description: Specify the semi-major axis of the ellipse defining the orbit.

subCommands.name: revolutions_per_day
subCommands.description: Specify the number revolutions per day the satellite orbits the Earth.

subCommands.name: periapsis_radius
subCommands.description: Specify the periapsis radius of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the smallest distance between the satellite and the center of the central body.

subCommands.name: apoapsis_radius
subCommands.description: Specify the apoapsis radius of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the largest distance between the satellite and the center of the central body.

subCommands.name: periapsis_altitude
subCommands.description: Specify the periapsis altitude of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the smallest distance between the satellite and the surface of the central body.

subCommands.name: apoapsis_altitude
subCommands.description: Specify the apoapsis altitude of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the largest distance between the satellite and the surface of the central body.

subCommands.name: raan
subCommands.description: Specify the right ascension of the ascending node (“raan”). This is the angle, measured counterclockwise along the celestial equator from the vernal equinox (the angle of right ascension) that the satellite crosses the equator from south to north (the ascending node).

subCommands.name: inclination
subCommands.description: Specify the separation angle of the tangent to the orbital plane with the Earth’s axis of rotation.

subCommands.name: mean_anomaly
subCommands.description: Specify the angular location of the satellite in its orbit at the epoch time. This angle is measured from the periapsis and represents the angle the satellite would traverse at a constant angular rate.

subCommands.name: true_anomaly
subCommands.description: Specify the angular location of the satellite in its orbit at the epoch time. This angle is measured from the periapsis and represents the true angular location of the satellite.

subCommands.name: argument_of_periapsis
subCommands.description: Specify the angle of the perigee (periapsis) with respect to the Earth’s surface. This angle is measured from the ascending node.

subCommands.name: j2000
subCommands.description: Specify that the initial kinematics are given in the J2000 frame. If this command is absent, the specified kinematics are taken to be in the ECI frame.

subCommands.name: integrator
subCommands.description: Specify the integrator used to propagate the state of the platform. Each integrator will have its own set of inputs that control its behavior.

subCommands.name: dynamics
subCommands.description: Specify the dynamical model used by the WSF_INTEGRATING_SPACE_MOVER. The dynamical model is used to update the state of the owning platform during the simulation. Dynamical models are collections of dynamical terms representing the various contributions to spacecraft dynamics.

subCommands.name: term
subCommands.description: Specify a term to be added into the orbital dynamics. Each term will have its own set of input commands to control its contribution to the dynamics.

subCommands.name: conjunction_setup
subCommands.description: Set this spacecraft’s initial conditions such that a conjunction with a given target spacecraft will occur at a specified time. During initialization an attempt will be made to find a solution with the given boundary conditions. If successful, this platform’s state will be set so that the specified conjunction occurs. If there is no solution (for example, the orbit would take the satellite through the Earth), the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to a default value (see below).

subCommands.name: from_lla
subCommands.description: Set the initial position of this spacecraft to the given latitude, longitude and altitude. If there is no solution to the conjunction, the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to that of a circular orbit with a heading of 90 degrees.

subCommands.name: from_eci
subCommands.description: Set the initial position of this spacecraft to the given position in the ECI frame. If there is no solution to the conjunction, the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to that of a circular orbit with a heading of 90 degrees.

subCommands.name: from_initial
subCommands.description: Set the initial position of this spacecraft using other means to specify the initial orbit of the spacecraft. If there is no solution to the conjunction, the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to that provided by the other initialization methods.

subCommands.name: with_target
subCommands.description: Specify the name of the target platform of the conjunction. This spacecraft will move to the position of the target platform at the time specified in the at_time command. The specified target must be the name of a platform that moves in the space spatial domain.

subCommands.name: at_time
subCommands.description: Specify the time at which this spacecraft should suffer a conjunction with the specified target.

subCommands.name: tolerance
subCommands.description: Specify the tolerance for the conjunction solution. The default value of the tolerance is 1.0e-9.

subCommands.name: attitude_controller
subCommands.description: Specify the attitude controller for the platform. All platforms having a WSF_SPACE_MOVER or WSF_NORAD_SPACE_MOVER will have an attitude controller of some kind. If no attitude controller block is specified, the mover will operate as if the instant attitude controller was selected.

subCommands.name: maneuvering
subCommands.description: Specifiy a model for executing orbital maneuvers in space.

subCommands.name: mission_sequence
subCommands.description: Specify a sequence of pre-determined orbital mission events. The first mission event specified is executed first, then the second, etc. An optional constraint can be specified to delay execution of the sequence; otherwise the mission event will begin executing at the creation time of the platform.

name: WSF_IRST_SENSOR
description: The fraction of the signal (in the closed range 0 to 1) that is attenuated per unit of distance traveled at sea level. The attenuation is adjusted to account for the density of air with the change in a altitude.

subCommands.name: atmospheric_attenuation

subCommands.name: background_radiance
subCommands.description: Specifies the radiance of the background. If ‘dynamic’ is specified then the experimental dynamic background model will be used. The dynamic model is currently valid only for targets at a positive elevation angle from from the sensor (i.e.: looking up at something like a satellite).

subCommands.name: background_radiance_below_horizon
subCommands.description: These two commands provide an alternative to the fixed background radiance provided by background_radiance. This is useful for airborne sensors where the sensor may be looking up and the sky is the background, or looking down where the ground is the background.

subCommands.name: background_transition_angle
subCommands.description: This command is used along with background_radiance_above_horizon and background_radiance_below_horizon to specify a region where the transition is made from using the below horizon and above horizon background radiance values. The specified angles are relative to the local angle to the horizon with positive values being above the horizon and negative values being below the horizon. If the target is within the transition region defined by these angles, the resulting background radiance will be linearly interpolated between the above horizon and below horizon values.

subCommands.name: detect_negative_contrast
subCommands.description: Declares if the sensor will detect targets who contrast versus the background is negative (i.e. the radiant intensity of the target is less than the radiant intensity of the background). If this is true then a negative contrast will be treated as positive, and thus potentially be detected. If this is false, then a negative contrast will be clamped to zero and detection will not occur.

subCommands.description: Defines the ratio of signal to noise required to declare a successful detection.

subCommands.description: Specify the number revolutions per day the satellite orbits the Earth.

subCommands.description: Specify the periapsis radius of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the smallest distance between the satellite and the center of the central body.

subCommands.name: apoapsis_radius
subCommands.description: Specify the apoapsis radius of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the largest distance between the satellite and the center of the central body.

name: WSF_KINEMATIC_MOVER
description: Enables debug output to the standard output.

subCommands.name: detailed_debug
subCommands.description: Enables debug output to the standard output.

subCommands.name: prefer_canopy_up
subCommands.description: Causes the platform to roll to the local vertical at all times. Mutually exclusive to bank_to_turn.

subCommands.name: bank_to_turn
subCommands.description: Causes the platform to roll into the acceleration vector, but still prefers the vertical when not accelerating in a turn. Mutually exclusive to prefer_canopy_up.

subCommands.name: broach_at_sea_level
subCommands.description: This mover was originally developed to define a torpedo mover. However, the capability of the model is such that it can be used above sea level. This flag assures that the motion must remain below local sea level, once subsurface.

subCommands.name: target_speed
subCommands.description: Once supplied, the platform will accelerate or decelerate to match the target (desired) speed, subject to maximum_linear_acceleration constraint.

subCommands.name: initial_speed
subCommands.description: Initial linear speed. After initialization, speed is varied to maintain target_speed.

subCommands.name: initial_flight_path_angle
subCommands.description: Initial flight path angle. After initialization, flight path angle will vary to guide to a desired waypoint in a defined route.

subCommands.name: maximum_linear_acceleration
subCommands.description: Defines the linear (velocity direction) acceleration limit constraint.

subCommands.name: maximum_radial_acceleration
subCommands.description: Defines the radial (normal to velocity direction) acceleration limit constraint. This constraint is imposed simultaneously with maximum_body_turn_rate, the most restrictive is used.

subCommands.name: maximum_body_roll_rate
subCommands.description: Defines the maximum rate at which the platform will try to capture desired target bank angle.

subCommands.name: maximum_body_turn_rate
subCommands.description: Defines the maximum rate at which the velocity vector will rotate in three-dimensional space. This constraint is imposed simultaneously with maximum_radial_acceleration, the most restrictive is used.

subCommands.name: velocity_pursuit_gain
subCommands.description: Defines the factor of proportion between target azimuth and elevation (in radians), and the applied lateral or vertical acceleration (in m/sec^2) to null the velocity vector to point at the target. See comments in header above.

subCommands.name: waypoint_switch_on_ground_turning_radius
subCommands.description: If this input value is set to true, only horizontal offsets are considered when deciding to advance to the next waypoint in a route; vertical miss values are ignored. If set false, then a 3-dimensional slant offset is considered when deciding if a waypoint is sufficiently close to be considered “hit”.

subCommands.name: proportional_navigation_gain
subCommands.description: Defines the factor of proportion between the target line-of-sight-rate (in rad/sec), and the applied lateral or vertical acceleration (in m/sec^2) to null the velocity vector to intercept the target’s future position at time of intercept. See comments in header above.

subCommands.name: use_route
subCommands.description: Supplies the name of the route to follow. The route is assumed to be a predefined absolute route.

subCommands.name: ignore_surveillance
subCommands.description: Specifies if this processor should process J3 series messages as a WsfTrack, populating the track manager.

subCommands.name: output_dis
subCommands.description: Determines if the messages sent using this processor are also sent over DIS.

subCommands.name: output_wsf
subCommands.description: Determines if the messages sent using this processor are sent to other WSF platforms. Setting this to no will reduce overhead of Link-16 if DIS output is the primary objective.

subCommands.name: decimal_track_number
subCommands.description: Specifies the Source Track Number for messages sent using this processor. Must be in the range (0, 32767).

subCommands.name: octal_track_number
subCommands.description: Specifies the Source Track Number for messages sent using this processor using an octal-integer. Must be in the range (00, 077777).

subCommands.name: iff_color_mapping
subCommands.description: Defines the mapping of identity types to colors. The identity type must one of the following: pending, unknown, assumed_friend, friend, neutral, suspect, hostile, undefined.

subCommands.name: message_processor
subCommands.description: Adds a message processor to the Link-16 computer.

subCommands.name: command_chain
subCommands.description: This command specifies which command chain is used to receive and send messages for this message processor. Each message processor must specify a command chain. In turn, each command chain must be linked to a distinct Slot Group Commands on the WSF_JTIDS_TERMINAL. This defines a mapping between the slot group and the messages which are sent and received over the slot group. This command is required for each message processor.

subCommands.name: send_interval
subCommands.description: This command specifies the rate at which to send messages. If a <time-value> is specified, it is the interval between each sent message. rrn <rrn-number> can be used to set the send interval based on a standard recurrence rate number.

subCommands.name: script
subCommands.description: If a script in this format is defined, it will be executed whenever this message processor sends a message. The primary use for this is to customize the message before it is sent by changing field values. This example sets the ‘flight-leader’ field in each sent message:

subCommands.name: network
subCommands.description: The JTIDS network number in the range [0, 127].

subCommands.name: npg
subCommands.description: The network participation in the range [0, 512].

subCommands.name: slot_number
subCommands.description: The slot number packed into the JTIDS header. This value may usually be ignored.

subCommands.name: msec
subCommands.description: The JTIDS MSEC value in the range [0, 127].

subCommands.name: tsec
subCommands.description: The JTIDS TSEC value in the range [0, 127].

subCommands.name: environment
subCommands.description: Used to explicitly specify what type of PPLI to send. If unspecified, the platform’s mover will be used to determine the message type to send.

subCommands.name: land_or_point
subCommands.description: Used to explicitly specify what type of land PPLI to send when the environment command was not set and the platform’s mover is being used to determine the message type to send.

subCommands.name: environment
subCommands.description: Specifies the spatial domain to use when selecting message type to send for a track. This value is only used when the spatial domain of a track is unknown. See Track Information Reporting Commands in sensor for more information on spatial domains.

subCommands.name: ignore_reporting_responsibility
subCommands.description: If true, reporting responsibility rules for tracks are ignored.

subCommands.name: maximum_send_interval
subCommands.description: Specifies the interval to queue unmodified tracks to send. Modified tracks are queued immediately.

subCommands.name: send_non_sensor_reports
subCommands.description: Specifies whether non-sensor (fused) tracks or raw sensor tracks in the master track list should be sent.

subCommands.name: suppress_dead_targets
subCommands.description: If true, suppresses the sending of J3 messages for platforms that are fully damaged or no longer in the simulation.

subCommands.name: suppress_domain
subCommands.description: If specified, tracks from the given domain will not be sent over Link-16.

subCommands.name: suppress_sensor

subCommands.name: track_number_range

subCommands.description: Specify the eccentricity of the orbit. The specified value must be greater than or equal to zero (circular orbit).

subCommands.name: revolutions_per_day
subCommands.description: Specify the number revolutions per day the satellite orbits the Earth.

subCommands.name: periapsis_radius
subCommands.description: Specify the periapsis radius of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the smallest distance between the satellite and the center of the central body.

subCommands.name: apoapsis_radius
subCommands.description: Specify the apoapsis radius of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the largest distance between the satellite and the center of the central body.

subCommands.name: periapsis_altitude
subCommands.description: Specify the periapsis altitude of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the smallest distance between the satellite and the surface of the central body.

subCommands.name: apoapsis_altitude
subCommands.description: Specify the apoapsis altitude of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the largest distance between the satellite and the surface of the central body.

subCommands.description: Specify the right ascension of the ascending node (“raan”). This is the angle, measured counterclockwise along the celestial equator from the vernal equinox (the angle of right ascension) that the satellite crosses the equator from south to north (the ascending node).

subCommands.name: inclination
subCommands.description: Specify the separation angle of the tangent to the orbital plane with the Earth’s axis of rotation.

subCommands.name: mean_anomaly
subCommands.description: Specify the angular location of the satellite in its orbit at the epoch time. This angle is measured from the periapsis and represents the angle the satellite would traverse at a constant angular rate.

subCommands.name: true_anomaly
subCommands.description: Specify the angular location of the satellite in its orbit at the epoch time. This angle is measured from the periapsis and represents the true angular location of the satellite.

subCommands.name: argument_of_periapsis
subCommands.description: Specify the angle of the perigee (periapsis) with respect to the Earth’s surface. This angle is measured from the ascending node.

subCommands.name: conjunction_setup
subCommands.description: Set this spacecraft’s initial conditions such that a conjunction with a given target spacecraft will occur at a specified time. During initialization an attempt will be made to find a solution with the given boundary conditions. If successful, this platform’s state will be set so that the specified conjunction occurs. If there is no solution (for example, the orbit would take the satellite through the Earth), the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to a default value (see below).

subCommands.name: from_lla
subCommands.description: Set the initial position of this spacecraft to the given latitude, longitude and altitude. If there is no solution to the conjunction, the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to that of a circular orbit with a heading of 90 degrees.

subCommands.name: from_eci
subCommands.description: Set the initial position of this spacecraft to the given position in the ECI frame. If there is no solution to the conjunction, the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to that of a circular orbit with a heading of 90 degrees.

subCommands.name: from_initial
subCommands.description: Set the initial position of this spacecraft using other means to specify the initial orbit of the spacecraft. If there is no solution to the conjunction, the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to that provided by the other initialization methods.

subCommands.name: with_target
subCommands.description: Specify the name of the target platform of the conjunction. This spacecraft will move to the position of the target platform at the time specified in the at_time command. The specified target must be the name of a platform that moves in the space spatial domain.

subCommands.name: at_time
subCommands.description: Specify the time at which this spacecraft should suffer a conjunction with the specified target.

subCommands.name: tolerance
subCommands.description: Specify the tolerance for the conjunction solution. The default value of the tolerance is 1.0e-9.

subCommands.name: attitude_controller
subCommands.description: Specify the attitude controller for the platform. All platforms having a WSF_SPACE_MOVER or WSF_NORAD_SPACE_MOVER will have an attitude controller of some kind. If no attitude controller block is specified, the mover will operate as if the instant attitude controller was selected.

subCommands.name: maneuvering
subCommands.description: Specifiy a model for executing orbital maneuvers in space.

subCommands.name: mission_sequence
subCommands.description: Specify a sequence of pre-determined orbital mission events. The first mission event specified is executed first, then the second, etc. An optional constraint can be specified to delay execution of the sequence; otherwise the mission event will begin executing at the creation time of the platform.

subCommands.name: orbital_state
subCommands.description: Specify the orbital state in the form of an epoch or epoch_date_time, and one of the following:

subCommands.name: position
subCommands.description: Sets the initial location of the space mover. This command must be used in conjunction with the velocity command.

subCommands.name: velocity
subCommands.description: Sets the initial velocity of the space mover. This command must be used in conjunction with the position command.

subCommands.name: epoch
subCommands.description: Specify the epoch that corresponds with the reference epoch at which the orbital elements are valid.

subCommands.name: epoch_date_time
subCommands.description: Specify the date and time that corresponds with the reference epoch at which the orbital elements are valid.

subCommands.name: designator
subCommands.description: Specify the designator for the space mover.

subCommands.name: eccentricity
subCommands.description: Specify the eccentricity of the orbit. The specified value must be greater than or equal to zero (circular orbit).

subCommands.name: semi_major_axis
subCommands.description: Specify the semi-major axis of the ellipse defining the orbit.

subCommands.name: revolutions_per_day
subCommands.description: Specify the number revolutions per day the satellite orbits the Earth.

subCommands.name: periapsis_radius
subCommands.description: Specify the periapsis radius of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the smallest distance between the satellite and the center of the central body.

subCommands.name: apoapsis_radius
subCommands.description: Specify the apoapsis radius of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the largest distance between the satellite and the center of the central body.

subCommands.name: periapsis_altitude
subCommands.description: Specify the periapsis altitude of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the smallest distance between the satellite and the surface of the central body.

subCommands.name: apoapsis_altitude
subCommands.description: Specify the apoapsis altitude of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the largest distance between the satellite and the surface of the central body.

subCommands.name: raan
subCommands.description: Specify the right ascension of the ascending node (“raan”). This is the angle, measured counterclockwise along the celestial equator from the vernal equinox (the angle of right ascension) that the satellite crosses the equator from south to north (the ascending node).

subCommands.name: inclination
subCommands.description: Specify the separation angle of the tangent to the orbital plane with the Earth’s axis of rotation.

subCommands.name: mean_anomaly
subCommands.description: Specify the angular location of the satellite in its orbit at the epoch time. This angle is measured from the periapsis and represents the angle the satellite would traverse at a constant angular rate.

subCommands.name: true_anomaly
subCommands.description: Specify the angular location of the satellite in its orbit at the epoch time. This angle is measured from the periapsis and represents the true angular location of the satellite.

subCommands.name: argument_of_periapsis
subCommands.description: Specify the angle of the perigee (periapsis) with respect to the Earth’s surface. This angle is measured from the ascending node.

subCommands.name: descriptor
subCommands.description: Specify an arbitrary descriptor (tag) for the space vehicle.

subCommands.name: orbit_color
subCommands.description: Specify the color of the orbit.

subCommands.name: orbit_color
subCommands.description: Specify the color of the orbit.

subCommands.name: orbit_color
subCommands.description: Specify the color of the orbit.

subCommands.name: orbit
subCommands.description: Specify a Two Line Element (TLE) that defines mean orbital elements and other data used to propagate a satellite. Two Line Elements are usually acquired from an existing source such as the Spacetrak database (http://www.space-track.org) or Celestrak (http://www.celestrak.com/NORAD/elements). Unlike ordinary AFSIM inputs, the column formatting, field length, and character format must be exactly as specified below.:

subCommands.name: central_body
subCommands.description: Specify the central body and related ellipsoid model to be used by simulation platforms. Options for <central body type> are the following:

subCommands.name: polar_offset_angles
subCommands.description: Specify the central_body’s polar offset angles ( and , respectively) of the Celestial Intermediate Pole (CIP) with respect to the WCS (ITRS) coordinate system. Providing these values (of the order of tenths of arc-seconds) enables very highly accurate conversions between ECI and WCS coordinates.

subCommands.name: heliocentric
subCommands.description: Specify use of the wgs_84 gravitational parameter, the egm_96 gravitational parameter, or the heliocentric gravitational parameter for propagation. The heliocentric option is used to simulate bodies orbiting the sun.

subCommands.name: conjunction_setup
subCommands.description: Set this spacecraft’s initial conditions such that a conjunction with a given target spacecraft will occur at a specified time. During initialization an attempt will be made to find a solution with the given boundary conditions. If successful, this platform’s state will be set so that the specified conjunction occurs. If there is no solution (for example, the orbit would take the satellite through the Earth), the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to a default value (see below).

subCommands.name: from_lla
subCommands.description: Set the initial position of this spacecraft to the given latitude, longitude and altitude. If there is no solution to the conjunction, the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to that of a circular orbit with a heading of 90 degrees.

subCommands.name: from_eci
subCommands.description: Set the initial position of this spacecraft to the given position in the ECI frame. If there is no solution to the conjunction, the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to that of a circular orbit with a heading of 90 degrees.

subCommands.name: from_initial
subCommands.description: Set the initial position of this spacecraft using other means to specify the initial orbit of the spacecraft. If there is no solution to the conjunction, the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to that provided by the other initialization methods.

subCommands.name: with_target
subCommands.description: Specify the name of the target platform of the conjunction. This spacecraft will move to the position of the target platform at the time specified in the at_time command. The specified target must be the name of a platform that moves in the space spatial domain.

subCommands.name: at_time
subCommands.description: Specify the time at which this spacecraft should suffer a conjunction with the specified target.

subCommands.name: tolerance
subCommands.description: Specify the tolerance for the conjunction solution. The default value of the tolerance is 1.0e-9.

subCommands.name: attitude_controller
subCommands.description: Specify the attitude controller for the platform. All platforms having a WSF_SPACE_MOVER or WSF_NORAD_SPACE_MOVER will have an attitude controller of some kind. If no attitude controller block is specified, the mover will operate as if the instant attitude controller was selected.

name: WSF_OLD_GUIDANCE_COMPUTER
description: Specifies if the perceived target location (as defined by the current target track) or the truth target location should be used in the guidance computations.

subCommands.name: guide_to_truth
subCommands.description: Specifies if the perceived target location (as defined by the current target track) or the truth target location should be used in the guidance computations.

subCommands.name: proportional_navigation_gain
subCommands.description: Specifies the gain to apply to a perceived inertial line-of-sight rate, to null the rate to zero. The default value may be inadequate, as the appropriate value is usually a matter of experimentation. Reducing the value to 0.0 would result in no guidance to intercept, and increasing the gain by an order of magnitude (10.0) would likely saturate the control system into a “bang-bang” type of oscillation, and wash out any ability to simultaneously accomplish g-biasing.

subCommands.name: velocity_pursuit_gain
subCommands.description: Specifies the gain to apply to a perceived off-boresight target angle, to place the velocity vector back on the target. (The gain comments made for proportional_navigation_gain also apply here.)

subCommands.name: g_bias
subCommands.description: Specifies the degree to which the trajectory should be compensated for vertical acceleration due to gravity. The default value of unity results in a somewhat flat trajectory along the line of sight to the target. Some missiles may be intentionally over-biased to fly an arcing trajectory to the target, descending upon it from above (use > 1.0, but < 10.0). Some inexpensive infrared-guided missiles do not contain an attitude reference gyro, and cannot “know” which way is up. Because they cannot compensate for gravity, they tend to fly a “sagging” trajectory below the line-of-sight to the target (use 0.0). Extreme positive values of g-bias (> 10.0) may possibly vertically saturate the control system, and wash out any ability to accomplish target homing guidance in the lateral direction.

subCommands.name: continuous_g_bias
subCommands.description: This flag requests that g bias be used throughout the whole flight profile. The default behavior is not to turn on g bias compensation until the horizontal target distance is large relative to the vertical drop to the target. If a ballistic falling trajectory to the target has the ability to intercept, then further g-bias is not needed, and would likely even increase the miss distance.

subCommands.name: max_commanded_g
subCommands.description: This sets the maximum commanded lateral turn acceleration that the guidance computer will request of the guided mover. This models a guidance-imposed structural limit constraint to prevent airframe destruction.

subCommands.name: guidance_delay
subCommands.description: This keyword specifies a time interval after launch when guidance request is clamped to null. This models a no-guidance period to clear the launch rail, or perhaps a time before uplink guidance has been established.

subCommands.name: aspect_angle_for_pro_nav_switch
subCommands.description: After the velocity-vector to target line-of-sight angle decreases below this value, the guidance algorithm will switch from velocity pursuit to proportional navigation. This value is not used if either omit_velocity_pursuit or omit_proportional_navigation is specified.

subCommands.name: omit_velocity_pursuit
subCommands.description: This flag forces the trajectory guidance to include only pure proportional navigation, from the very beginning of the flight, with no velocity pursuit segment.

subCommands.name: omit_proportional_navigation
subCommands.description: This flag forces the trajectory guidance to include only velocity pursuit, with no switch to proportional navigation.

subCommands.name: time_between_GPS_fixes
subCommands.description: For the drift model, this duration specifies how often a positional update is received. The value will not be used unless the drift rate (below) is input as non-zero.

subCommands.name: IMU_drift_rate
subCommands.description: For the drift model, this specifies the rate of drift of positional perception.

subCommands.name: pitchover_guidance
subCommands.description: Specifies that the weapon will use a proportional navigation guidance scheme only that is modified for weapons that must perform a pitchover maneuver to point at the target. The proportional_navigation_gain is adjusted throughout the weapon’s flight based upon the weapon’s closure rate. (All indented commands below require that this option be enabled.)

subCommands.name: maximum_loft_time
subCommands.description: Specifies the time the missile will loft using the specified loft angle.

subCommands.name: loft_angle
subCommands.description: Specifies the angle the missile will initially climb at for the specified maximum_loft_time.

subCommands.name: frequency_cutoff
subCommands.description: A method of specifying the doppler frequency that determines the method of computing the pitchover gain. The guidance computer assumes a frequency of 10 GHz to compute the closing doppler frequency (i.e., doppler shift = 10.0e9 / light_speed * doppler_range_rate).

subCommands.name: min_nav_gain
subCommands.description: The minimum pitchover gain that is used when the doppler shift is less than zero.

subCommands.name: max_nav_gain
subCommands.description: The maximum pitchover gain that is used when the doppler shift is equal to or greater than the frequency_cutoff.

subCommands.name: nav_gain_factor
subCommands.description: A factor that is applied to the computed pitchover gain.

subCommands.name: nav_gain_slope_1
subCommands.description: Used to compute the pitchover gain when the doppler shift is less than the specified frequency_cutoff. The pitchover gain is computed as follows: Pitchover_gain = nav_gain_slope_1 * doppler_shift + min_nav_gain.

subCommands.name: nav_gain_slope_2
subCommands.description: Used to compute the pitchover gain when the doppler shift is greater than or equal to the specified frequency_cutoff. The pitchover gain is computed as follows, unless limited by the max_nav_gain: Pitchover_gain = nav_gain_slope_2 * (doppler_shift - frequency_cutoff) + 0.5.

name: WSF_OLD_GUIDED_MOVER
description: Enables a debug printout that indicates when a staging operation takes place. Automatically enabled if debug is also enabled.

subCommands.name: show_status
subCommands.description: Enables a debug printout that indicates when a staging operation takes place. Automatically enabled if debug is also enabled.

subCommands.name: show_trajectory
subCommands.description: Enables debug printouts on mass changes and trajectory data points. (Normal debug information includes [LLA] location and NED Orientation [hdg,pitch,roll]). This option provides downrange distance, speed, Mach number, and applied aerodynamic forces.

subCommands.name: disable_guidance
subCommands.description: Disables generation of any aerodynamic lift (lateral or vertical forces). Turns a guided weapon into a “dumb” ballistic one. This option is the default setting for the WSF_UNGUIDED_MOVER.

subCommands.name: integration_method
subCommands.description: Specify the method used to integrate the equations of motion.

subCommands.name: integration_timestep
subCommands.description: Specifies the global value of timestep to be used for integrating the equations of motion. This value is used for any stage that does not specify a local integration timestep.

subCommands.name: stage
subCommands.description: Defines the attributes of the only stage of a single stage vehicle or one of the stages in a multistage vehicle. <stage number> must be a value that is greater than or equal to 1 and less than or equal to the current number of defined stages plus one. If the value specifies a stage that already exists then the enclosed subcommands override the values in that stage. If the value is equal to the current number of defined stages plus one then a new stage is created and populated with the enclosed subcommands. It is invalid to specify a stage number that is more than one higher than the current highest defined stage number.

subCommands.name: integration_timestep
subCommands.description: Specifies the timestep to be used for integrating the equations of motion. If specified this overrides the global integration timestep.

subCommands.name: aero
subCommands.description: Specifies the aerodynamics type name for this stage. Type must be known at initialization time.

subCommands.name: empty_mass
subCommands.description: Specifies the mass of the stage without fuel.

subCommands.name: fuel_mass
subCommands.description: Specifies the mass of the fuel on the stage.

subCommands.name: total_mass
subCommands.description: Specifies the total mass of the stage, which is the sum of empty_mass and fuel_mass but does not include the mass of any upper stages on top of this one (considered payload). Note: For backward compatibility, this same value may be supplied via the keywords: ‘launch_mass’, ‘mass’, ‘initial_mass’, or ‘weight’, but future support of these keywords is not guaranteed.

subCommands.name: pre_ignition_coast_time
subCommands.description: Specifies the amount of time that will elapse between the start of the stage and when the engine will ignite.

subCommands.name: pre_separation_coast_time
subCommands.description: Specifies the amount of time that will elapse between the burnout of this stage and its separation from the vehicle. This command has no effect for single-stage vehicles or the last stage of a multistage vehicle.

subCommands.name: thrust
subCommands.description: Specifies the thrust of the propulsion system.

subCommands.name: thrust_duration
subCommands.description: Specifies the amount of time the engine will produce the specified thrust.

subCommands.name: burn_rate
subCommands.description: Specifies the propellant burn rate while thrusting.

subCommands.name: specific_impulse
subCommands.description: Specific impulse of the propulsion system.

subCommands.name: thrust_vectoring_angle_limit
subCommands.description: Specifies the angle off the longitudinal axis that the thrust is vectored during thrust_vectoring_time_limits in order to introduce a pitch-over maneuver.

subCommands.name: thrust_vectoring_time_limits
subCommands.description: Specifies the time window after stage ignition in which thrust vectoring may be employed. This is applicable only if thrust_vectoring_angle_limit is greater than zero.

name: WSF_P6DOF_FUEL
description: Defines the initial quantity of fuel to be loaded on the vehicle. WSF_P6DOF_FUEL will interact with WSF_P6DOF_MOVER to set the initial fuel. Fuel will be added to internal tanks first, keeping the percentage filled for each tank in sync. For example, if the initial_quantity was 75% of the total internal fuel capacity, each internal fuel tank would be filled to 75% and no external tanks would be filled.

For example, if the initial_quantity was 75% of the total internal fuel capacity, each internal fuel tank would be filled to 75% and no external tanks would be filled.

subCommands.name: reserve_quantity

subCommands.description: The fuel capacity is determined by fuel tank definitions in a WSF_P6DOF_MOVER. If maximum_quantity is specified, it will be ignored and WSF_P6DOF_FUEL will output a warning.
