subCommands.name: show_commands
subCommands.description: Specifies that calls from script commands should be written to standard output.

subCommands.name: show_evaluations
subCommands.description: Specifies that phase change rule evaluations should be written to standard output.

subCommands.name: guide_to_truth
subCommands.description: Specifies if the guidance target should be the location specified in the current target track (false), or should be the true location of the platform specified in the current target track (true).

subCommands.name: phase
subCommands.description: The ‘phase’ block is used to define the guidance for the various phases of flight and the rules to transition between phases.

subCommands.name: edit
subCommands.description: This command is typically used when creating a new guidance computer type by deriving from another guidance computer type.

subCommands.name: guidance_delay
subCommands.description: Specifies the elapsed time since the start of the phase when guidance commands should start being computed. This is useful during lift-off and other phases where pursuit of the target is not desirable.

subCommands.name: on_entry
subCommands.description: These commands define scripts to be executed when entering and exiting the phase.

subCommands.name: on_update
subCommands.description: Define a script to be executed on every phase update.

subCommands.name: maximum_commanded_g
subCommands.description: Specifies the magnitude of the maximum acceleration that can be commanded.

subCommands.name: proportional_navigation_gain
subCommands.description: Specifies the gain for proportional navigation. A value of zero indicates proportional navigation will not be performed.

subCommands.name: proportional_navigation_limit_angle
subCommands.description: Specifies the 3D aspect angle of the target with respect to the weapon at which the navigation method will switch between proportional and velocity pursuit. Proportional navigation will be used if the target aspect angle is less than or equal to this value, otherwise velocity pursuit will be used.

subCommands.name: proportional_navigation_method
subCommands.description: Specifies whether additional acceleration should be commanded because of current target acceleration.

subCommands.name: velocity_pursuit_gain
subCommands.description: Specifies the gain for velocity pursuit navigation. A value of zero indicates velocity pursuit navigation will not be performed.

subCommands.name: g_bias
subCommands.description: Specifies the bias factor used to overcome gravity. This is typically used during midcourse to prevent the trajectory from sagging. If zero is specified then gravity bias will not be applied.

subCommands.name: lateral_g_bias
subCommands.description: Specifies the bias factor used skew the horizontal component of the trajectory in a particular direction. If zero is specified then gravity bias will not be applied.

subCommands.name: commanded_azimuth_offset
subCommands.description: Specifies the azimuth angle to the target that should be maintained. The angle is defined to be the angle in the local horizontal plane between the weapon velocity vector and the line-of-sight vector from the weapon to the target. (This is consistent with the ‘target_azimuth’ conditional tests in the next_phase command.)

subCommands.name: guidance_target
subCommands.description: Overrides the top-level guide_to_truth command for the current phase. This is expanded to include the options:

subCommands.name: aimpoint_altitude_offset
subCommands.description: Modify the aimpoint to be above or below the perceived target location. This is typically used to create an air burst.

subCommands.name: aimpoint_azimuth_offset
subCommands.description: These commands provide a method to produce an aimpoint that is laterally offset from the perceived target location. This is typically used to meet some tactical requirement.

subCommands.name: aimpoint_evaluation_interval
subCommands.description: Controls how often a new aimpoint is computed when using aimpoint_azimuth_offset and aimpoint_range_offset. This is a fairly time-consuming operation that does not need to be performed on every call to the guidance computer.

subCommands.name: next_phase
subCommands.description: The next_phase command defines a condition under which a phase transition occurs. A phase block may have multiple next_phase commands to define a number of conditions that might trigger a phase change. The next_phase commands are evaluated on each guidance update and are evaluated in the order specified.

subCommands.name: commanded_altitude
subCommands.description: Specifies a commanded altitude. Typically used to climb or dive to a cruise altitude and hold the altitude. The altitude reference tag (’msl’, or ‘above mean sea level’; ‘agl’, or ‘above ground level’) may be omitted, in which case ‘msl’ is assumed.

subCommands.name: commanded_flight_path_angle
subCommands.description: Specifies a commanded flight path angle. If from_launch_computer is specified then the value produced by the launch computer will be used (if present).

subCommands.name: commanded_mach
subCommands.description: Specifies the commanded speed/mach to be used during this phase. Typically used for cruise.

subCommands.name: commanded_throttle
subCommands.description: Specifies a throttle factor in the range [0..1] that overrides and throttle specification in the mover.

subCommands.name: allow_route_following
subCommands.description: If true, the computer will follow a route if it has been provided to the associated mover. If the mover does not have a route then this command has no effect. Conventional target point selection will resume at the end of the route.

name: WSF_P6DOF_MOVER
description: This defines the type of p6dof object used by the mover. The p6dof_object_type is defined in a p6dof_object_types block and must be defined before being referenced.

subCommands.name: p6dof_object_type
subCommands.description: This defines the type of p6dof object used by the mover. The p6dof_object_type is defined in a p6dof_object_types block and must be defined before being referenced.

subCommands.name: autopilot_no_control
subCommands.description: This will command the autopilot to “zero” all controls, which will center the stick and rudder and pull back throttle(s) to zero (idle). It is similar to enable_controls but is commanding the autopilot, rather than the controls themselves.

subCommands.name: enable_controls
subCommands.description: This enables/disables control inputs from any source (autopilot, external manual pilot, P6Net interface, etc.). Controls are enabled by default, so this command is typically used to disable controls at the start. This is often used to allow a weapon to drop ballistically and without control inputs as it is released from the carrying aircraft and then calling the script method WsfP6DOF_Mover.EnableControls with true to establish control input after the weapon is safely clear of the aircraft.

subCommands.name: enable_thrust_vectoring
subCommands.description: Indicates whether thrust vectoring is enabled or not.

subCommands.name: engines_on
subCommands.description: Indicates whether the engines should be on or off when the scenario begins.

subCommands.name: follow_vertical_track
subCommands.description: Normally, the autopilot will climb/dive as quickly as possible (within the current limits – see WsfP6DOF_Mover.SetVerticalSpeedMax and WsfP6DOF_Mover.SetVerticalSpeedMin) when changing altitude, but when “follow_vertical_track” is set, the autopilot will instead use a vertical speed that will allow the object to smoothly/slowly change altitude along a straight line vertical track between waypoints.

subCommands.name: ignore_all_crashes
subCommands.description: Indicates whether the mover ignore all forms of crashes. This is often used in testing.

subCommands.name: landing_gear_down
subCommands.description: Indicates whether the landing gear should be down or not when the scenario begins.

subCommands.name: nws_enabled
subCommands.description: Indicates whether nose-wheel steering should be enabled or not. Nose-wheel steering is commonly used when taxiing but should be removed prior to the takeoff roll.

subCommands.name: p6dof_alt
subCommands.description: This command sets the initial altitude of the mover.

subCommands.name: p6dof_initsetup
subCommands.description: This is deprecated – use wash_in_conditions instead.

subCommands.name: p6dof_ned_heading
subCommands.description: This command sets the initial heading of the mover.

subCommands.name: p6dof_ned_pitch
subCommands.description: This command sets the initial pitch angle of the mover.

subCommands.name: p6dof_ned_roll
subCommands.description: This command sets the initial roll angle of the mover.

subCommands.name: p6dof_position
subCommands.description: This command sets the initial position (using decimal latitude longitude) of the mover.

subCommands.name: p6dof_set_velocity_ned_fps
subCommands.description: This command sets the initial velocity of the mover in NED coordinates using ft/sec.

subCommands.name: parking_brake_on
subCommands.description: This command sets whether the parking brake should be on or off when the scenario begins.

subCommands.name: produces_launch_smoke
subCommands.description: This command sets how long the vehicle will produce a launch smoke/flash effect (appearance only) when launched. If no launch effect is desired, this should not be defined at all.

subCommands.name: taxi_mode_enabled
subCommands.description: This command set whether the autopilot should be in taxi mode when the scenario begins. This should be used only be used when the platform is on ground.

subCommands.name: throttle_afterburner
subCommands.description: This command sets the throttle to afterburner when the scenario begins.

subCommands.name: throttle_full
subCommands.description: This command sets the throttle to mil power when the scenario begins.

subCommands.name: throttle_idle
subCommands.description: This command sets the throttle to idle when the scenario begins.

subCommands.name: wash_in_conditions
subCommands.description: Including this flag indicates that this mover should “wash-in” conditions on initialization. This means that the object will run in a special mode to help “ramp-in” and “stabilize” the object on initialization by allowing it to have some time to settle in the needed angle of attack (alpha) as well as the proper throttle setting. This is useful to ensure vehicles are stable when they start the simulation – they may otherwise lack the correct alpha, for example, when they start in the simulation.

subCommands.name: route
subCommands.description: Specifies the latitude and longitude of the waypoint.

subCommands.name: position
subCommands.description: Specifies the latitude and longitude of the waypoint.

subCommands.name: altitude
subCommands.description: Specifies the altitude (MSL) at the waypoint.

subCommands.name: speed
subCommands.description: Specifies the speed at the waypoint.

subCommands.name: label
subCommands.description: Associates a label with the immediately following waypoint definition. This can be used as the target of a goto command.

subCommands.name: goto
subCommands.description: Go to the waypoint with the specified label in the current route.

subCommands.name: bank_angle_limit
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum bank angle to be used for turns when making heading changes on the route segment that starts with this waypoint. This effectively sets the radial_acceleration to .

subCommands.name: radial_acceleration
subCommands.description: Specifies the radial acceleration to be used for turns when making heading changes on the route segment that starts with this waypoint.

subCommands.name: turn_g_limit
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum turn g-load to be used for turns when making heading changes on the route segment that starts with this waypoint. This effectively sets the radial_acceleration to .

subCommands.name: switch_on_approach
subCommands.description: Defines the condition when the mover should declare that it has reached this waypoint and should start moving towards the next waypoint. switch_on_passing is sometimes known as ‘turn long’ and causes the switch to occur when the platform passes over or along side of the waypoint. switch_on_approach is sometimes known as ‘turn short’ and causes the switch to occur before the waypoint.

subCommands.name: use_route
subCommands.description: Supplies the name of the route to follow. The route is assumed to be a predefined absolute route.

subCommands.name: p6dof_object_type

name: WSF_PARABOLIC_MOVER
description: If non-zero, specifies a periodic time interval at which the simulation will call the mover. If zero then the mover will be called only when it is necessary to determine the position of the containing platform.

subCommands.name: update_interval
subCommands.description: If non-zero, specifies a periodic time interval at which the simulation will call the mover. If zero then the mover will be called only when it is necessary to determine the position of the containing platform.

subCommands.name: update_time_tolerance
subCommands.description: When a position update is requested by the simulation, if the time since the previous update is less than or equal to this value then the mover will ignore the update.

subCommands.name: tof_and_impact_lat_lon_alt
subCommands.description: The desired final conditions: time of flight and impact latitude, longitude, and altitude.

subCommands.name: tof_and_impact_lat_lon
subCommands.description: The desired final conditions: time of flight and impact latitude, longitude. Altitude is determined by finding the terrain elevation at the given latitude and longitude.

subCommands.name: update_interval
subCommands.description: If non-zero, specifies a periodic time interval at which the simulation will call the mover. If zero then the mover will be called only when it is necessary to determine the position of the containing platform.

subCommands.name: update_time_tolerance
subCommands.description: When a position update is requested by the simulation, if the time since the previous update is less than or equal to this value then the mover will ignore the update.

subCommands.name: tof_and_impact_lat_lon_alt

subCommands.name: tof_and_impact_lat_lon

name: WSF_PASSIVE_SENSOR
description: Defines how the passive sensor reports target type information in tracks.

subCommands.name: reported_target_type
subCommands.description: Defines how the passive sensor reports target type information in tracks.

subCommands.name: default_time_to_declare
subCommands.description: Defines the duration of time after the initial detection that is required to make a determination of the target type.

subCommands.name: default_time_to_reevaluate
subCommands.description: Defines the time interval used for reevaluating the identification of the target. A value of 0 seconds indicates no reevaluation will take place.

subCommands.name: type
subCommands.description: Specifies the truth type to which the following subcommands apply.

subCommands.name: default_type
subCommands.description: Specifies that the following type subcommands apply for any type not defined with the type command.

subCommands.name: time_to_declare
subCommands.description: Defines the duration of time after the initial detection that is required to make a determination of the target type.

subCommands.name: time_to_reevaluate
subCommands.description: Defines the time interval used for reevaluating the identification of the target.

subCommands.name: report_type
subCommands.description: Defines the reporting type-name as the target type based on the listed emitter-type(s) being reported in the emitter list. Currently exact matches between the emitter’s defined for the report_type and a track’s emitter list must happen for the given report_type to be reported. If there are differences another report_type or the default_type will be reported.

subCommands.name: report_type
subCommands.description: Defines the probability of reporting type-name as the target type. The probability parameter is a value between 0.0 and 1.0. Any number of report_type commands may be specified as long as the probability parameters add up to 1.0. For greater ease of use, the value remainder may be used as the probability parameter to specify whatever value is required to add up to 1.0.

subCommands.name: unframed_detection_optimization
subCommands.description: This command indicates if unframed detection optimization will be used. If enabled, once the sensor successfully detects a given transmitter within a frame, subsequent attempts to detect the same transmitter in the same frame will be suppressed. For instance, if multiple messages are sent from a single transmitter during the passive frame, the passive sensor will only report on the first message that it can detect (if any). If the first message cannot be detected because of transmitter antenna pointing, it will report the second message if it can be detected, an so on.

subCommands.name: unframed_detection_coast_time
subCommands.description: If the passive sensor is running at a faster frame time than the sensors it is trying to detect, it may detect the transmitter one frame and not the next. This can cause a lot of track creation and deletion. This value indicates how long a successful detection from a transmitter will be reported.

subCommands.name: revisit_time
subCommands.description: These two commands pertain to the immediately preceding frequency_band and define how long the sensor dwells in the band and the interval between dwells. These commands are effectively only when the scan_on_scan_model is enabled and are used to determine the temporal probability that the sensor would be looking at the frequency of the target emitter when a detection chance occurs.

subCommands.name: threat_importance_function
subCommands.description: Specify a script function name used to measure threat importance. If specified, it completely over-rides the use of any script functions that try to set threat importance or unimportance (see WsfPerceptionProcessor). Only useful when max_threat_load is defined, otherwise no limit is imposed and importance is not necessary. Script function must match the signature of “double FunctionName(WsfLocalTrack)”. Values returned by the script will be interpreted as lower being more important (golf scoring).

If this input is specified within the system_type_data input block then it is specific to a system-type, otherwise this input is defined as the ‘default’ data to use for undefined system-types in the system_type_data.

subCommands.description: Specifies a mitigating adjustment to the effective receiver noise power level created by this technique. If this input is specified within the system_type_data input block then it is specific to a system-type, otherwise this input is defined as the ‘default’ data to use for undefined system-types in the system_type_data.

subCommands.name: system_type_data
subCommands.description: Input block to provide the system type (e.g., SENSOR-TYPE, JAMMER-TYPE) specific data necessary to implement this technique for a given system type. Default data can be set up for system types not defined using the “default” string as the system type.

name: WSF_PULSE_EFFECT
description: Specifies the pulse density of the jamming signal in range [0,1] to use for this radar type. This input is used only for Electronic Attack based effects.

subCommands.name: jamming_pulse_density
subCommands.description: Specifies the pulse density of the jamming signal in range [0,1] to use for this radar type. This input is used only for Electronic Attack based effects.

subCommands.name: jamming_pulse_density

subCommands.name: allow
subCommands.description: Specifies the rejected or allowed suppression-type and required input variables that are dependent upon the suppression-type specified.

subCommands.name: allow

name: WSF_QUANTUM_TASKER_PROCESSOR
description: Indicates that the Quantum Tasker should not pass tracks of allies to the task generator, and subsequently should not have any tasks related to ally tracks.

subCommands.name: ignore_ally_tracks
subCommands.description: Indicates that the Quantum Tasker should not pass tracks of allies to the task generator, and subsequently should not have any tasks related to ally tracks.

subCommands.name: asset_representation
subCommands.description: Indicates how the Quantum Tasker should represent asset perception objects. If ‘systems’ is defined then each platform subsystem is considered as an individual asset that can receive task assignments separate from other subsystems. If ‘resources’ is defined then each resource of a subsystem is considered as a taskable individual asset (missiles, sensor/jammer beams). However, the task assignments are still sent to the owning platform for processing as required.

subCommands.name: generator
subCommands.syntax: generator [ simple_weapon | simple_jammer | simple_sensor | custom <script method name> ]
subCommands.description: Indicates which task generator the Quantum Tasker is to use.

subCommands.name: evaluator
subCommands.syntax: evaluator [ simple | distance | intercept_time | custom <script method name> ]
subCommands.description: Indicates which task evaluator the Quantum Tasker is to use.

subCommands.name: allocator
subCommands.syntax: allocator [ simple | greedy_isolated | greedy_priority | greedy_value | greedy_profit | optimal_profit | custom <script method name> ] [type <task_type>]
subCommands.description: Indicates which allocation algorithm the Quantum Tasker is to use to assign tasks to assets given the current evaluation values.

subCommands.name: allocator_extra_tasks
subCommands.syntax: allocator_extra_tasks [ simple | greedy_isolated | greedy_priority | greedy_value | greedy_profit | optimal_profit | custom <script method name> ]
subCommands.description: Indicates which allocator will be used on any extra tasks that were not allocated by the primary allocator. If used, this means assets might have more than one task to perform. This allocator will be called repeatedly as long there are tasks that are still remaining and as long as it keeps finding at least one new allocation each pass. If no assets evaluated a task positively, then that task will not be allocated.

subCommands.name: allocator_extra_assets
subCommands.syntax: allocator_extra_assets [ simple | greedy_isolated | greedy_priority | greedy_value | greedy_profit | optimal_profit | custom <script method name> ]
subCommands.description: Indicates which allocator will be used on any extra assets that were not allocated by the primary allocator. If used, this means tasks might have more than one asset performing them. This allocator will be called repeatedly as long there are assets that are still remaining and as long as it keeps finding at least one new allocation each pass. If an asset did not evaluate any task positively, then that asset will not be allocated to a task.

subCommands.name: reallocation_strategy
subCommands.description: Indicates how the Quantum Tasker handles previously assigned tasks and changes in task assignments.

subCommands.name: update_assignments
subCommands.description: If declared, a task assign message is sent to all assigned assets every update. This is only useful when task data (like aux data) is updated regularly on the tasks.

subCommands.name: comm_retry_attempts
subCommands.description: Indicates the number of attempts to retry failed communications.

subCommands.name: comm_retry_interval
subCommands.description: Indicates the amount of time between attempts to retry failed communications.

subCommands.name: operating_level
subCommands.description: Indicates the operating condition or state and the associated level.

subCommands.name: track_processor
subCommands.description: Specifies the name of a WSF_TRACK_PROCESSOR (typically operating as a non_master_track_processor) whose track list will provide the tracks used in the evaluation process.

subCommands.name: time_to_recognize_messages
subCommands.description: Indicates the amount of time it takes to recognize a message.

subCommands.name: track_update_interval
subCommands.description: Indicates the time interval for sending track updates to assignees.

subCommands.name: track_update_strategy
subCommands.description: Indicates how track updates are sent. With default behavior, if a task has been accepted then periodic track updates are sent to the assignee. With the Suppressor behavior, track updates are sent to assignees only when the track manager indicates a track has been updated.

subCommands.name: show_task_messages
subCommands.description: Indicates that information related task assignment, cancellation and completion are to be written to standard output.

subCommands.name: show_uncompleted_tasks
subCommands.description: This is a debugging tool that indicates information about uncompleted tasks is to be written to standard output during the destruction of the task processor.

subCommands.name: queuing_method
subCommands.description: Only used if time_to_recognize_messages is defined and greater than zero. Specifies how incoming messages are to be queued if all of the servers are busy. A value of none indicates the message will be discarded.

subCommands.name: number_of_servers
subCommands.description: Only used if time_to_recognize_messages is defined and greater than zero. Specifies the maximum number of messages that can be ‘in process’ at any given instant of time. If a new message is received and all the servers are busy, the message will be queued according to the queuing_method

name: WSF_RADAR_SENSOR
description: Write information about the characteristics of the radar to standard output. This will include the one square meter detection range as well as any other values that may need to be derived.

subCommands.name: show_calibration_data
subCommands.description: Write information about the characteristics of the radar to standard output. This will include the one square meter detection range as well as any other values that may need to be derived.

subCommands.name: receive_only
subCommands.description: Indicate that only the transmitter or receiver will be used.

subCommands.name: compute_measurement_errors
subCommands.description: If true, measurement errors will be computed using standard radar error model equations. If false, measurement errors will be computed using the common sensor error model.

subCommands.name: override_measurement_with_truth
subCommands.description: This command will compute the measurement errors and report the errors in the track, but will report the truth location in the track instead of using the location with the measurement errors applied. This is typically used for testing trackers.

subCommands.name: frequency_select_delay
subCommands.description: Specifies the delay when selecting between different frequencies as defined on the transmitter.

subCommands.name: maintain_track_measurement_history
subCommands.description: If true, the mode will maintain a track’s history of measurements produced from successful detections.

subCommands.name: doppler_resolution
subCommands.description: Defines the target Doppler speed resolution (i.e., opening or closing speed) capability of the radar.

subCommands.name: adjustment_factor
subCommands.description: A method of adjusting a beam’s detection capability. Positive value increase the sensor’s detection capability.

subCommands.name: operating_loss
subCommands.description: Defines the beam’s operating loss.

subCommands.name: integration_gain
subCommands.description: Defines the integration gain when using the binary detector (detection_threshold). This is not applicable when using the Swerling detector (swerling_case) or detection_probability.

subCommands.name: detection_threshold
subCommands.description: An alternative method of defining the receiver’s detection threshold. The value can be entered here for readability of the input file.

subCommands.name: swerling_case
subCommands.description: Indicates that the Marcum-Swerling detector model is to be used and specifies the ‘case’ to be used.

subCommands.name: number_of_pulses_integrated
subCommands.description: Specifies the number of pulses the Marcum-Swerling detector integrates.

subCommands.name: probability_of_false_alarm
subCommands.description: Specifies the false alarm probability.

subCommands.name: detector_law
subCommands.description: Specifies the type of Marcum-Swerling detector.

subCommands.name: no_swerling_case
subCommands.description: Specifies not to use a Marcum-Swerling detector. Detections will be based on the detection_threshold. This is the default configuration.

subCommands.name: detection_probability
subCommands.description: Defines a function of probability of detection (Pd) versus received signal-to-noise ratio (more specifically, it is really the signal-to-interference ratio, which includes the effects of receiver noise, interference and unsuppressed clutter). This is an alternative to using the Swerling detector (swerling_case) or the binary detector (detection_threshold). The table is defined as follows:

subCommands.name: post_lockon_detection_threshold_adjustment
subCommands.description: Defines a value by which the detection threshold will be adjusted once a ‘locked-on’ state has been achieved for the current mode of the sensor. This is typically used with tracking sensors to indicate that the detection threshold is less once a locked-on state has been achieved. The value is typically a negative ‘dB’ value, although it can be 0 dB or greater if that is what is desired.

subCommands.name: post_lockon_adjustment_delay_time
subCommands.description: Defines the time that must elapse from when a sensor declares that a ‘locked-on’ state has been achieved before applying the post_lockon_detection_threshold_adjustment.

subCommands.name: loop_gain
subCommands.description: Alternative methods to specify a radar beam’s detection capability. If specified, the receiver’s noise value will be calibrated to yield the specified detection range.

subCommands.name: look_down_factor
subCommands.description: Defines a beam’s look-down loss. The ratio will adjust the received signal power for targets that are located below the beam’s antenna.

subCommands.name: prf_factor
subCommands.description: Defines a factor that represents the detection difference for a beam that uses interleaved HPRF and MPRF waveforms. The prf_factor is applied to the received signal power if the absolute value of the target closing speed is less than the ownship velocity.

subCommands.name: clutter_attenuation_factor
subCommands.description: Specifies a constant value in the range [ 0 .. 1 ] by which the clutter returned will be multiplied to create an ‘attenuated clutter return.’ If the signal_processor type mti_processor is supplied and this value is not provided, a clutter attenuation value will be computed.

subCommands.name: signal_processor
subCommands.description: Specifies the signal processor identified by <type-name> form the following list:

subCommands.name: error_model_parameters
subCommands.description: radar_sensor_error

subCommands.name: azimuth_beamwidth
subCommands.description: Specifies the azimuth beamwidth to be used by the error_model.

subCommands.name: elevation_beamwidth
subCommands.description: Specifies the elevation beamwidth to be used by the error_model.

subCommands.name: pulse_width
subCommands.description: Specifies the pulse width to be used by the error_model.

subCommands.name: receiver_bandwidth
subCommands.description: Specifies the receiver bandwidth to be used by the error_model.

subCommands.name: doppler_resolution
subCommands.description: Specifies the doppler resolution to be used by the error_model.

subCommands.name: jam_strobe_detector
subCommands.description: The jam_strobe_detector allows a WSF_RADAR_SENSOR mode to detect and report the azimuth and/or elevation of jamming power it receives via indicator or strobe tracks. These recorded strobes can be combined with angle-only measurements from other radars using a jam strobe estimator (JSE) algorithm to produce pseudo-measurements passed to a tracking algorithm. Reporting information as well as errors are specified outside the general sensor error models due to differences in the error calculations.

subCommands.name: uniform_elevation_error_bound
subCommands.description: Specifies the standard deviation for a Gaussian or Uniform distribution of errors to be applied to the azimuth and elevation of the track. The standard deviation may be specified directly as an angle value or as a fraction of the beamwidth of the receiver. In the case of a Uniform distribution, the error bound may be specified instead of the standard deviation. The standard deviation of a symmetric Uniform distribution on the interval is defined to be .

subCommands.name: reports_bearing
subCommands.description: The bearing from the sensor to the target is reported. This angle is measured in radians from the sensor’s north orientation, and it is in the range .

subCommands.name: reports_elevation
subCommands.description: The elevation angle from the sensor to the target is reported.

subCommands.name: reports_nothing
subCommands.description: Has the effect of canceling any previous ‘reports’ commands. This is useful if one wants to reuse an existing sensor definition with embedded ‘reports’ commands but needs to change what is reported.

subCommands.name: track_quality
subCommands.description: Specify the ‘quality’ of the track when produced from this jam strobe detector.

subCommands.name: jamming_perception_timeout
subCommands.description: Specifies the time after which jamming that was perceived is no longer perceived, so that the perception of jamming will be returned to a ‘false’ state. If jamming is perceived again before this time has elapsed then the perception of jamming will remain or become ‘true’.

subCommands.name: coherent_jamming_perception_threshold
subCommands.description: Specifies the minimum threshold value that jamming will be perceived by the operator. Often used in conjunction with jamming_perception_timeout, JammingPerceived script method and electronic_protect techniques.

subCommands.name: close_target_detection
subCommands.description: The Close Target Detection (CTD) model allows for closely spaced targets and other platform types to be detected and their results used for location measurement and track creation.

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: If specified debug messages to standard output are available.

subCommands.name: acquire_deltas
subCommands.description: Defines the deltas for azimuth, elevation and range, with-respect-to the current target cue or request, for which targets will be acquired.

subCommands.name: azimuth_delta
subCommands.description: Specifies the azimuth delta wrt to the current target cue or request for which other targets will be considered. Value must be >= 0.0.

subCommands.name: elevation_delta
subCommands.description: Specifies the elevation delta wrt to the current target cue or request for which other targets will be considered. Value must be >= 0.0.

subCommands.name: range_delta
subCommands.description: Specifies the range delta wrt to the current target cue or request for which other targets will be considered. Value must be >= 0.0.

subCommands.name: reacquire_deltas
subCommands.description: Defines the deltas for azimuth, elevation and range, with-respect-to the current target cue or request, for which the target can no longer be reacquired.

subCommands.name: azimuth_delta
subCommands.description: Specifies the azimuth delta wrt to the current target cue or request for which the target may be reacquired. Value must be >= 0.0.

name: WSF_RIPR_PROCESSOR
description: Specifies that the indicated channel on this RIPR agent processor will be allowed to bid on and win jobs of the indicated type. If no types are specified for a channel than all types are allowed on that channel. The channel-index is an integer value and the job-type is a string that equals the job name (also called the job type). Users can specify many job types for particular channels, or one, or none. If a particular channel bids on a job of type that is not allowed, that bid is ignored. A job of the wrong type will never be awarded to a channel.

subCommands.name: channel_job_type
subCommands.description: Specifies that the indicated channel on this RIPR agent processor will be allowed to bid on and win jobs of the indicated type. If no types are specified for a channel than all types are allowed on that channel. The channel-index is an integer value and the job-type is a string that equals the job name (also called the job type). Users can specify many job types for particular channels, or one, or none. If a particular channel bids on a job of type that is not allowed, that bid is ignored. A job of the wrong type will never be awarded to a channel.

subCommands.name: job_board_comm
subCommands.description: Specifies the name of a comm device that all job interactions will take place over. This includes bidding, status update, and winning jobs.

subCommands.name: job_pass_through
subCommands.description: If specified, this RIPR processor will simply act as a pass-through for jobs and bids. If asked for its jobs or job board, it will reply with its commander’s jobs or job board. It will not hold any jobs on its own board. Subsequently, all bids from its subordinates go up to its commander and its subordinates will win jobs from its commander’s job board.

subCommands.name: job_stickiness
subCommands.description: A RIPR processor’s job stickiness is the value used to provide a little extra stability to the current job allocation. When a RIPR processor has won a job and is performing that job, then all of it bids on that job are multiplied by the job_stickiness value. In this way, it’s harder to dislodge somebody from their job once they have won it.

subCommands.name: num_job_channels
subCommands.description: The number of channels a RIPR processor has represents its capability to perform jobs at the same time. If the RIPR processor is bidding on tracking jobs and its radar can track four targets at once, then it might have four job channels. This way, each channel can bid on jobs, win jobs separately, and allow the agent to perform them concurrently. The responsibility lies with the scenario developer to use the channels. The extended forms of these methods must be used to specify the channel index as parameter aChannelIndex, referenced here:

subCommands.name: auto_exclusive_mode
subCommands.description: If set to true, the RIPR processor job board will use the time values given with “job_window_open_length” and “bid_window_open_length” to automatically alternate the windows for job bidding and job awarding of the job board according to the proper durations. While the bidding window is closed, all bids given to the job board are ignored. While the job window is closed, all jobs maintain a constant allocation (nobody changes jobs).

subCommands.name: bid_window_open_length
subCommands.description: Specifies the amount of time the bidding window will be open each cycle. While the bidding window is closed, all bids given to the job board are ignored.

subCommands.name: job_window_open_length
subCommands.description: Specifies the amount of time the job window will be open each cycle. While the job window is closed, all jobs maintain a constant allocation (nobody changes jobs).

subCommands.name: max_weapon_uplinks
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum number of active uplinks the RIPR agent is capable of.

subCommands.name: use_remote_tracks_for_uplink
subCommands.description: If set to true, the RIPR processor will send tracks from any sensor and any source to weapons it is supporting with an uplink.

subCommands.name: weapon_uplink_path
subCommands.description: If a weapon uplink path is specified for a RIPR processor, then the processor will support uplinks for all fired weapons. It will send track updates over the designated comm to the fired weapon platform using tracks from the designated sensor. Uplinks can be stopped and started from script, see WSF_RIPR_PROCESSOR.

This way, each channel can bid on jobs, win jobs separately, and allow the agent to perform them concurrently. The responsibility lies with the scenario developer to use the channels. The extended forms of these methods must be used to specify the channel index as parameter aChannelIndex, referenced here:

subCommands.name: auto_exclusive_mode
subCommands.description: If set to true, the RIPR processor job board will use the time values given with “job_window_open_length” and “bid_window_open_length” to automatically alternate the windows for job bidding and job awarding of the job board according to the proper durations. While the bidding window is closed, all bids given to the job board are ignored. While the job window is closed, all jobs maintain a constant allocation (nobody changes jobs).

subCommands.name: bid_window_open_length
subCommands.description: Specifies the amount of time the bidding window will be open each cycle. While the bidding window is closed, all bids given to the job board are ignored.

subCommands.name: job_window_open_length
subCommands.description: Specifies the amount of time the job window will be open each cycle. While the job window is closed, all jobs maintain a constant allocation (nobody changes jobs).

subCommands.name: max_weapon_uplinks
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum number of active uplinks the RIPR agent is capable of.

subCommands.name: use_remote_tracks_for_uplink
subCommands.description: If set to true, the RIPR processor will send tracks from any sensor and any source to weapons it is supporting with an uplink.

subCommands.name: weapon_uplink_path
subCommands.description: If a weapon uplink path is specified for a RIPR processor, then the processor will support uplinks for all fired weapons. It will send track updates over the designated comm to the fired weapon platform using tracks from the designated sensor. Uplinks can be stopped and started from script, see WSF_RIPR_PROCESSOR.

subCommands.name: query_bid_type
subCommands.description: Determines and returns an agent’s bid on a given job of the indicated type. No other query_bid_type block for the same job type is allowed to be defined on this agent. The script method WsfRIPRProcessor.QueryBid will execute this block on the given job. You can access the job object by using the “JOB” keyword within the query_bid_type script block. This input is the preferred and explicit method for providing bid values from agents.

subCommands.name: query_bid
subCommands.description: This input block is obsolete and now deprecated. See the “query_bid_type” script block definition above.

name: WSF_ROAD_MOVER
description: The name of the route_network to follow.

subCommands.name: road_network
subCommands.description: The name of the route_network to follow.

subCommands.name: end_position
subCommands.description: Defines the starting location and ending locations. The resulting path will be the points from the road network that define the shortest path between the specified locations.

subCommands.name: speed
subCommands.description: Defines the platform speed while traveling on the road network.

subCommands.name: off_road_speed
subCommands.description: Defines the platform speed while traveling off the road network.

subCommands.name: linear_acceleration
subCommands.description: The linear acceleration to be used to accelerate the platform.

subCommands.name: pause_time
subCommands.description: The time the mover is paused at the user-specified start position.

subCommands.name: use_closest_waypoint
subCommands.description: The mover will use the closest waypoints to the user-specified start and end positions when calculating the shortest path along the road network. No off-road segments at the start or the end will be generated.

subCommands.name: consider_off_road_shortcut
subCommands.description: If this command has a value of true, a second path will be considered as a possible route, that being an off-road ‘shortcut’ path between the start position and the end position. If the shortcut path takes less time to traverse using the off_road_speed than the normal path, it will be used as the route.

subCommands.name: update_interval
subCommands.description: If non-zero, specifies a periodic time interval at which the simulation will call the mover. If zero then the mover will be called only when it is necessary to determine the position of the containing platform.

subCommands.name: update_time_tolerance
subCommands.description: When a position update is requested by the simulation, if the time since the previous update is less than or equal to this value then the mover will ignore the update.

name: WSF_ROTORCRAFT_MOVER
description: Sets the desired heading for the mover, which will take effect at speeds below the “weathercocking speed.”

subCommands.name: desired_heading
subCommands.description: Sets the desired heading for the mover, which will take effect at speeds below the “weathercocking speed.”

subCommands.name: position_hold_capture_radius
subCommands.description: The rotorcraft mover uses a rate guidance mechanism when transiting from one location to another. When approaching a target point, guidance fundamentally changes to capture a position value, and so must decelerate in anticipation of capturing and holding the target position. This value determines the transition point from one guidance type to the other. The default value is set to 200 meters, which should suffice for the vast majority of Rotorcraft models.

subCommands.name: start_mode
subCommands.description: Specifies the initial mover mode of the platform. The mover mode may be changed externally via script settings or at waypoint transitions. Mover modes are discussed separately.

subCommands.name: ned_filter_time_constant
subCommands.description: Specifies a filter time constant to apply to commanded acceleration values to smooth transient responses. A larger value will apply a greater amount of smoothing to the commands. Value must be greater than zero. The default is 1 second and is adequate for most purposes.

subCommands.name: altitude_error_to_rate_of_climb_gain
subCommands.description: Specifies a gain to apply to an altitude error to arrive at a vertical acceleration value. The default is 1 and is adequate for most purposes.

subCommands.name: lateral_acceleration_value_pid
subCommands.description: Each of the above four input blocks may contain tuning parameters to apply to the Proportional Integral Derivative (PID) controllers, which determine acceleration values which drive the motion state of the platform. It is not necessary for the end-user to modify the default gains, unless a particular dynamic response is required. Tuning PID controllers is outside the scope of this document, but many separate resources are available to assist. PID controller response should be adequate for most purposes.

subCommands.name: mode
subCommands.description: Ground speed above which the platform will assume a heading that matches the course angle. Below this speed, the platform will assume a desired heading angle, as set by script commands.

subCommands.name: weathercock_speed
subCommands.description: Ground speed above which the platform will assume a heading that matches the course angle. Below this speed, the platform will assume a desired heading angle, as set by script commands.

subCommands.name: maximum_attitude_rate
subCommands.description: Maximum angular rate for body attitude changes. This is primarily used in concert with weathercock_speed to determine how quickly the platform will transition in and out of weathercocking mode.

subCommands.name: maximum_total_acceleration
subCommands.description: Maximum magnitude of linear acceleration. Sets the upper limit during hard lateral accelerations.

subCommands.name: minimum_upward_acceleration
subCommands.description: Minimum upward acceleration value. When aircraft is rising, and then a command is given to descend quickly, this value sets the minimum vertical acceleration constraint. Note that many rotorcraft with teetering rotor heads are not permitted to pull negative g, by design.

subCommands.name: body_rates_gain
subCommands.description: Gain to apply to an angular heading error to obtain the rate at which the heading error is removed. Used primarily in removing a heading error when transitioning to fast forward flight, above weathercock speed.

subCommands.name: maximum_ground_speed
subCommands.description: Maximum permitted ground speed in this motion mode. Typical use would be for <mode> speed constraint.

subCommands.name: maximum_rate_of_climb
subCommands.description: Maximum permitted rate of climb in this motion mode. Typical use would be to set a realistic climb rate for <mode>.

subCommands.name: maximum_rate_of_descent
subCommands.description: Magnitude of maximum permitted rate of descent in this motion mode. Value must be greater than zero but will be negated when applied. Typical use would be to set a realistic descent rate for <mode>.

subCommands.name: proportional_gain
subCommands.description: Gain to apply to current error to attempt to null the error to zero. Larger values will more forcibly attempt to null the error but are prone to induce oscillation in the output.

subCommands.name: derivative_gain
subCommands.description: Gain to apply to current rate-of-change of error to attempt to prevent the error from overshooting the desired target value. Larger values will oppose any change in the output, causing drift.

subCommands.name: integral_gain
subCommands.description: Gain to oppose a steady-state bias, which attempts to drive the bias to zero.

subCommands.name: input_threshold
subCommands.description: Comparison value to determine whether to apply integral summing of the input error sample. While the input value differs more than <input_threshold> from the target value no input integration is performed. Once the input threshold is near the target value, a continuous integration is performed to discern and react to an input bias. If so, integral_gain is applied to the bias to remove it over time.
