name: WSF_SIX_DOF_MOVER
description: This defines the type of object used by the mover. See vehicle_type and vehicle_type.

subCommands.name: vehicle_type
subCommands.description: This defines the type of object used by the mover. See vehicle_type and vehicle_type.

subCommands.name: autopilot_no_control
subCommands.description: This will command the autopilot to “zero” all controls, which will center the stick and rudder and pull back throttle(s) to zero (idle). It is similar to enable_controls but is commanding the autopilot, rather than the controls themselves.

subCommands.name: enable_controls
subCommands.description: This enables/disables control inputs from any source (autopilot, external manual pilot, etc.). Controls are enabled by default, so this command is typically used to disable controls at the start. This is often used to allow a weapon to drop ballistically and without control inputs as it is released from the carrying aircraft and then calling the script method WsfSixDOF_Mover.EnableControls with true to establish control input after the weapon is safely clear of the aircraft.

subCommands.name: enable_thrust_vectoring
subCommands.description: Indicates whether thrust vectoring is enabled or not.

subCommands.name: engines_on
subCommands.description: Indicates whether the engines should be on or off when the scenario begins.

subCommands.name: follow_vertical_track
subCommands.description: Normally, the autopilot will climb/dive as quickly as possible (within the current limits – see WsfSixDOF_Mover.SetVerticalSpeedMax and WsfSixDOF_Mover.SetVerticalSpeedMin) when changing altitude, but when “follow_vertical_track” is set, the autopilot will instead use a vertical speed that will allow the object to smoothly/slowly change altitude along a straight line vertical track between waypoints.

subCommands.name: ignore_all_crashes
subCommands.description: Indicates whether the mover ignore all forms of crashes. This is often used in testing.

subCommands.name: six_dof_alt
subCommands.description: This command sets the initial altitude of the mover.

subCommands.name: six_dof_ned_heading
subCommands.description: This command sets the initial heading of the mover.

subCommands.name: six_dof_ned_pitch
subCommands.description: This command sets the initial pitch angle of the mover.

subCommands.name: six_dof_ned_roll
subCommands.description: This command sets the initial roll angle of the mover.

subCommands.name: six_dof_position
subCommands.description: This command sets the initial position (using decimal latitude longitude) of the mover.

subCommands.name: six_dof_set_velocity_ned_fps
subCommands.description: This command sets the initial velocity of the mover in NED coordinates using ft/sec.

subCommands.name: produces_launch_smoke
subCommands.description: This command sets how long the vehicle will produce a launch smoke/flash effect (appearance only) when launched. If no launch effect is desired, this should not be defined at all.

subCommands.name: throttle_afterburner
subCommands.description: This command sets the throttle to afterburner when the scenario begins.

subCommands.name: throttle_full
subCommands.description: This command sets the throttle to mil power when the scenario begins.

subCommands.name: throttle_idle
subCommands.description: This command sets the throttle to idle when the scenario begins.

subCommands.name: wash_in_conditions
subCommands.description: Including this flag indicates that this mover should “wash-in” conditions on initialization. This means that the object will run in a special mode to help “ramp-in” and “stabilize” the object on initialization by allowing it to have some time to settle in the needed angle of attack (alpha) as well as the proper throttle setting. This is useful to ensure vehicles are stable when they start the simulation – they may otherwise lack the correct alpha, for example, when they start in the simulation.

subCommands.name: position
subCommands.description: Specifies the latitude and longitude of the waypoint.

subCommands.name: altitude
subCommands.description: Specifies the altitude (MSL) at the waypoint.

subCommands.name: speed
subCommands.description: Specifies the speed at the waypoint.

subCommands.name: label
subCommands.description: Associates a label with the immediately following waypoint definition. This can be used as the target of a goto command.

subCommands.name: goto
subCommands.description: Go to the waypoint with the specified label in the current route.

subCommands.name: bank_angle_limit

subCommands.name: radial_acceleration

subCommands.name: turn_g_limit

name: WSF_SPACE_MOVER
description: Specify the orbital state in the form of an epoch or epoch_date_time, and one of the following:

subCommands.name: orbital_state
subCommands.description: Specify the orbital state in the form of an epoch or epoch_date_time, and one of the following:

subCommands.name: position
subCommands.description: Sets the initial location of the space mover. This command must be used in conjunction with the velocity command.

subCommands.name: velocity
subCommands.description: Sets the initial velocity of the space mover. This command must be used in conjunction with the position command.

subCommands.name: epoch
subCommands.description: Specify the epoch that corresponds with the reference epoch at which the orbital elements are valid.

subCommands.name: epoch_date_time
subCommands.description: Specify the date and time that corresponds with the reference epoch at which the orbital elements are valid.

subCommands.name: designator
subCommands.description: Specify the designator for the space mover.

subCommands.name: eccentricity
subCommands.description: Specify the eccentricity of the orbit. The specified value must be greater than or equal to zero (circular orbit).

subCommands.name: semi_major_axis
subCommands.description: Specify the semi-major axis of the ellipse defining the orbit.

subCommands.name: revolutions_per_day
subCommands.description: Specify the number revolutions per day the satellite orbits the Earth.

subCommands.name: periapsis_radius
subCommands.description: Specify the periapsis radius of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the smallest distance between the satellite and the center of the central body.

subCommands.name: apoapsis_radius
subCommands.description: Specify the apoapsis radius of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the largest distance between the satellite and the center of the central body.

subCommands.name: periapsis_altitude
subCommands.description: Specify the periapsis altitude of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the smallest distance between the satellite and the surface of the central body.

subCommands.name: apoapsis_altitude
subCommands.description: Specify the apoapsis altitude of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the largest distance between the satellite and the surface of the central body.

subCommands.name: raan
subCommands.description: Specify the right ascension of the ascending node (“raan”). This is the angle, measured counterclockwise along the celestial equator from the vernal equinox (the angle of right ascension) that the satellite crosses the equator from south to north (the ascending node).

subCommands.name: inclination
subCommands.description: Specify the separation angle of the tangent to the orbital plane with the Earth’s axis of rotation.

subCommands.name: mean_anomaly
subCommands.description: Specify the angular location of the satellite in its orbit at the epoch time. This angle is measured from the periapsis and represents the angle the satellite would traverse at a constant angular rate.

subCommands.name: true_anomaly
subCommands.description: Specify the angular location of the satellite in its orbit at the epoch time. This angle is measured from the periapsis and represents the true angular location of the satellite.

subCommands.name: argument_of_periapsis
subCommands.description: Specify the angle of the perigee (periapsis) with respect to the Earth’s surface. This angle is measured from the ascending node.

subCommands.name: descriptor
subCommands.description: Specify an arbitrary descriptor (tag) for the space vehicle.

subCommands.name: position
subCommands.description: Specify a waypoint as an alternate method to define the orbital path (i.e., instead of the orbit … end_orbit block). The platform will be placed in a circular orbit if no speed is specified; otherwise the speed specified in the waypoint will be used to produce the orbit.

subCommands.name: initial_state_lla
subCommands.description: Specify the initial state of the platform in terms of a location and velocity. The location is in lat, lon, alt format; the velocity is in a local North, East, Down frame. This input is similar to the position input above, but in this case it completely specifies the physical state of the object.

subCommands.name: initial_state_eci
subCommands.description: Specify the initial state of the platform in terms of a location and velocity. The location and velocity are in the ECI frame. This input is similar to the position input above, but in this case it completely specifies the physical state of the object.

subCommands.name: oblate_earth

subCommands.name: conjunction_setup
subCommands.description: Set this spacecraft’s initial conditions such that a conjunction with a given target spacecraft will occur at a specified time. During initialization an attempt will be made to find a solution with the given boundary conditions. If successful, this platform’s state will be set so that the specified conjunction occurs. If there is no solution (for example, the orbit would take the satellite through the Earth), the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to a default value (see below).

subCommands.name: from_lla
subCommands.description: Set the initial position of this spacecraft to the given latitude, longitude and altitude. If there is no solution to the conjunction, the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to that of a circular orbit with a heading of 90 degrees.

subCommands.name: from_eci
subCommands.description: Set the initial position of this spacecraft to the given position in the ECI frame. If there is no solution to the conjunction, the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to that of a circular orbit with a heading of 90 degrees.

subCommands.name: from_initial
subCommands.description: Set the initial position of this spacecraft using other means to specify the initial orbit of the spacecraft. If there is no solution to the conjunction, the velocity of the spacecraft will be set to that provided by the other initialization methods.

subCommands.name: with_target
subCommands.description: Specify the name of the target platform of the conjunction. This spacecraft will move to the position of the target platform at the time specified in the at_time command. The specified target must be the name of a platform that moves in the space spatial domain.

subCommands.name: at_time
subCommands.description: Specify the time at which this spacecraft should suffer a conjunction with the specified target.

subCommands.name: tolerance
subCommands.description: Specify the tolerance for the conjunction solution. The default value of the tolerance is 1.0e-9.

subCommands.name: attitude_controller

subCommands.name: position
subCommands.description: Sets the initial location of the space mover. This command must be used in conjunction with the velocity command.

subCommands.name: velocity
subCommands.description: Sets the initial velocity of the space mover. This command must be used in conjunction with the position command.

subCommands.name: epoch
subCommands.description: Specify the epoch that corresponds with the reference epoch at which the orbital elements are valid.

subCommands.name: epoch_date_time
subCommands.description: Specify the date and time that corresponds with the reference epoch at which the orbital elements are valid.

subCommands.name: designator
subCommands.description: Specify the designator for the space mover.

subCommands.name: eccentricity
subCommands.description: Specify the eccentricity of the orbit. The specified value must be greater than or equal to zero (circular orbit).

subCommands.name: semi_major_axis
subCommands.description: Specify the semi-major axis of the ellipse defining the orbit.

subCommands.name: revolutions_per_day
subCommands.description: Specify the number revolutions per day the satellite orbits the Earth.

subCommands.name: periapsis_radius
subCommands.description: Specify the periapsis radius of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the smallest distance between the satellite and the center of the central body.

subCommands.name: apoapsis_radius
subCommands.description: Specify the apoapsis radius of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the largest distance between the satellite and the center of the central body.

subCommands.name: periapsis_altitude
subCommands.description: Specify the periapsis altitude of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the smallest distance between the satellite and the surface of the central body.

subCommands.name: apoapsis_altitude
subCommands.description: Specify the apoapsis altitude of the ellipse defining the orbit. This is the largest distance between the satellite and the surface of the central body.

subCommands.name: raan
subCommands.description: Specify the right ascension of the ascending node (“raan”). This is the angle, measured counterclockwise along the celestial equator from the vernal equinox (the angle of right ascension) that the satellite crosses the equator from south to north (the ascending node).

subCommands.name: inclination
subCommands.description: Specify the separation angle of the tangent to the orbital plane with the Earth’s axis of rotation.

subCommands.name: mean_anomaly
subCommands.description: Specify the angular location of the satellite in its orbit at the epoch time. This angle is measured from the periapsis and represents the angle the satellite would traverse at a constant angular rate.

subCommands.name: true_anomaly
subCommands.description: Specify the angular location of the satellite in its orbit at the epoch time. This angle is measured from the periapsis and represents the true angular location of the satellite.

subCommands.name: argument_of_periapsis
subCommands.description: Specify the angle of the perigee (periapsis) with respect to the Earth’s surface. This angle is measured from the ascending node.

subCommands.name: use_pk_table
subCommands.description: Sets the name of a Pk table to evaluate upon weapon fusing, in order to compute the threshold value for intercept_pk. At platform initialization, this table name must be known by the PkTable Manager to supply to the weapon. Table will override any value supplied for intercept_pk.

subCommands.name: pk_table
subCommands.description: Following is an example input to specify a PkTable while using the use_pk_table option. The pk_table…end_pk_table block must occur either in global context (as all tables are read in by the PkTableManager, and supplied by reference to the weapon), or nested inside of a weapon_effects block. The weapon must request use of the table by employing the use_pk_table option. Each of the one or more tables listed within the pk_table block is tied to a target_type. The independent variables for the table lookup, if not a constant Pk value, will include: target azimuth, target elevation, weapon speed, and target speed. The first target_type listed must be DEFAULT, which is used if there is no more specific match provided below the DEFAULT option. PkTables may be specified as inline_tables, and the “inline_table” keyword is always followed by two integers, the (n) number of azimuths (beginning with zero, as the pk is assumed to be symmetric about the weapon’s XZ plane), and the (m) number of elevations (not assumed symmetric) in increasing order. Then the inline table will contain n X m values of Pk for the weapon to interpolate as the Pk threshold. The kill determination will be 1.0 (total kill) if the uniform random draw is less than the threshold value.

subCommands.name: update_time_tolerance
subCommands.description: When a position update is requested by the simulation, if the time since the previous update is less than or equal to this value then the mover will ignore the update.

subCommands.description: Specifies the weapon’s average speed that will be used for the duration of flight.

subCommands.name: tof_and_speed

subCommands.name: maximum_lateral_acceleration
subCommands.description: Specifies the weapon’s maximum lateral acceleration that will be used for weapon maneuvers.

subCommands.name: guidance_mode
subCommands.description: Specifies the weapon’s guidance mode. Using lead_pursuit, the velocity vector will always be aimed toward the current target track if stationary, and if the track is moving, will be extrapolated as necessary for a predicted time to intercept, mimicking proportional navigation guidance. Using pure_pursuit, the velocity vector will always be aimed toward the current target track.

subCommands.name: update_interval

subCommands.name: update_time_tolerance
subCommands.description: When a position update is requested by the simulation, if the time since the previous update is less than or equal to this value then the mover will ignore the update.

subCommands.name: average_speed
subCommands.description: Specifies the weapon’s average speed that will be used for the duration of flight.

subCommands.name: tof_and_speed
subCommands.description: Specifies the weapon’s speed versus time profile that will be used. The time values must be in increasing numerical order.

subCommands.name: maximum_lateral_acceleration
subCommands.description: Specifies the weapon’s maximum lateral acceleration that will be used for weapon maneuvers.

subCommands.name: guidance_mode

subCommands.name: switch_on_approach
subCommands.description: Switches to the next waypoint when approaching within one turn radius of the current target waypoint.

subCommands.name: switch_on_passing
subCommands.description: Switches to the next waypoint only when abreast of the current target waypoint.

subCommands.name: turn_failure_threshold
subCommands.description: Defines the threshold for which the on_turn_failure behavior is triggered, given as a ratio of the turn radius. subCommands.name: body_g_limit

subCommands.name: heading_pursuit_gain
subCommands.description: The heading pursuit gain.

subCommands.name: maximum_climb_rate
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum climb rate and dive rate used when changing altitude. Other climb rates specified by waypoints or scripts are bounded by this value.

subCommands.name: maximum_flight_path_angle
subCommands.description: Specifies maximum flight path angle (angle of climb/dive). Value must be greater than or equal to 0.

subCommands.name: maximum_linear_acceleration

subCommands.name: maximum_radial_acceleration

subCommands.description: Maximum altitude constraint.

subCommands.description: Minimum altitude constraint.

subCommands.name: minimum_speed

subCommands.name: path_variance_radius
subCommands.description: This value will randomly vary the location of the waypoint within the radius given. A random bearing and distance are chosen and applied to the next waypoint when calculating the path.

subCommands.name: roll_rate_limit
subCommands.description: The roll rate limit. Value must be greater than 0. Note: When applied to a WSF_AIR_MOVER or other waypoint mover types, the roll rate will not affect the platform’s movement along a route. To affect route following behavior use maximum_radial_acceleration.

subCommands.name: speed_variance_percent

subCommands.name: turn_rate_limit

name: WSF_SUBSURFACE_RADIO_TRANSCEIVER
description: Prevents unrealistically long underwater ranges by specifying a range constraint for the underwater portion of the transmission path. This keyword also has an additional effect of permitting communication over the short range without regard to horizon or terrain.

subCommands.name: max_underwater_range_filter
subCommands.description: Prevents unrealistically long underwater ranges by specifying a range constraint for the underwater portion of the transmission path. This keyword also has an additional effect of permitting communication over the short range without regard to horizon or terrain.

subCommands.name: max_communication_depth
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum depth at which a submerged platform is permitted to exchange communication events. In order to reduce user input issues, the absolute value of the numeric input is used, and the value is converted to be a negative altitude to represent the depth below the surface for the submerged platform.

subCommands.name: minimum_horizon_angle
subCommands.description: Specifies the minimum angle acceptable for transmissions through the water’s surface. This angle is measured from the horizon upward. Communications with angles less than this limit are stopped. The effect is to require platforms to reduce their slant range to be able to communicate.

subCommands.name: unset_VLF_comm
subCommands.description: When the command is set_VLF_comm, then all horizon checks are ignored and the message is delivered.

subCommands.name: water_attenuation_factor
subCommands.description: Specifies a factor by which signals are attenuated as they pass through the water part of the transmission path. The format for data is a number followed by a dB ratio value, followed by a backslash, and then followed by a <length-value>.

subCommands.name: adjustment_factor
subCommands.description: Specifies a multiplier to be applied to returned values. This would typically be used to account for the fact that values integrated over a wide band (i.e.: visual) represent an average that may include many ‘dead-zones’ that the sensor may exclude. Thus, the effective transmittance may be higher.

subCommands.description: Specifies end-points (source and target points) for a given interaction can be logically interchanged so the path goes from the highest object to the lowest object. subCommands.name: target_to_background_radiance
subCommands.description: Specifies the name of the file which contains the raw spectral target-to-background radiance as a function of observer altitude and elevation angle and slant range to the target. Using the current processes, this file name will be of the form <filename>_tbr.plt.

subCommands.name: spectral_response_curve

subCommands.name: output

name: WSF_TANKED_FUEL
description: Specifies the lower value on a band of desired operating fuel quantity. This value, along with maximum_refuel_quantity specifies the hysteresis band to stay within while operating in proximity to a refueling tanker, such as during a group ferry flight. In other words, when fuel quantity transitions from above this quantity to below, it is desired to begin a fuel receive operation from a nearby tanker if possible. Script operations may key upon this transition, in order to take a desired action. Conversely, when the fuel quantity transitions from below maximum_refuel_quantity to above, a separate scripted action may be taken, such as to terminate the receive-in-process action.

subCommands.name: desired_top_off_quantity
subCommands.description: Specifies the lower value on a band of desired operating fuel quantity. This value, along with maximum_refuel_quantity specifies the hysteresis band to stay within while operating in proximity to a refueling tanker, such as during a group ferry flight. In other words, when fuel quantity transitions from above this quantity to below, it is desired to begin a fuel receive operation from a nearby tanker if possible. Script operations may key upon this transition, in order to take a desired action. Conversely, when the fuel quantity transitions from below maximum_refuel_quantity to above, a separate scripted action may be taken, such as to terminate the receive-in-process action.

subCommands.name: maximum_receive_rate
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum rate at which the platform can be refueled.

subCommands.name: maximum_refuel_quantity
subCommands.description: Specifies the upper value on a band of desired operating fuel quantity. See desired_top_off_quantity for more detail.

subCommands.name: receive_method
subCommands.description: Sets the method that this tanked fuel may use to receive fuel. At the time a fuel supply operation between two tanks is initiated, the Tanker must have an available fuel supply point that matches the Receiver’s configuration, or the transfer cannot begin. See supply_method_preference.

subCommands.name: supply_location_preference
subCommands.description: Sets the preferred location that this tanked fuel may use to supply fuel. Often a tanker may have multiple stations to supply fuel, leading to some ambiguity about which transfer point should be used, so this setting is consulted to resolve the ambiguity, if necessary. Run-time software is permitted to change this setting to reconfigure to an anticipated receiver arrival.

subCommands.name: supply_method_preference
subCommands.description: Sets the preferred method that this tanked fuel may use to supply fuel. Often a tanker may have multiple methods to supply fuel, leading to some ambiguity about which type of transfer should be attempted, so this setting is consulted to resolve the ambiguity, if necessary. At the time a fuel supply operation between two tanks is initiated, the Tanker must have an available fuel supply point type that matches the Receiver’s configuration, or the transfer cannot begin. name: WSF_TASK_PROCESSOR
description: Indicates if ‘candidate tracks’ are to be evaluated. A candidate track is one that has been received but has not yet been determined to be ‘stable’ as defined by the filter.

subCommands.name: evaluate_candidate_tracks
subCommands.description: Indicates if ‘candidate tracks’ are to be evaluated. A candidate track is one that has been received but has not yet been determined to be ‘stable’ as defined by the filter.

subCommands.name: evaluation_interval
subCommands.description: Specifies how often a track in the indicated state should be (re)evaluated.

subCommands.name: number_of_servers
subCommands.description: Indicates the maximum number of track evaluations that can occur simultaneously. The time to perform the evaluation is set using the time_to_evaluate command.

subCommands.name: show_state_evaluations
subCommands.description: Indicates that information about state evaluations should be written to standard output. This essentially shows the true or false status of the evaluation of each next_state block.

subCommands.name: show_state_transitions
subCommands.description: Indicates that information about state transitions should be written to standard output.

subCommands.name: state
subCommands.description: Defines a state in a state machine with the name <state-name>.

subCommands.name: on_entry
subCommands.description: When entering this state, performs these script commands. This is an optional subcommand.

subCommands.name: on_exit
subCommands.description: When leaving this state, performs these script commands. This is an optional subcommand.

subCommands.name: next_state
subCommands.description: This optional subcommand is a script block that must return a true/false value. When evaluated, the return value determines whether to transition to the named state defined by the <next-state-name>. If next_state is not defined, it will “dead end” in this state.

subCommands.name: time_to_evaluate
subCommands.description: Specifies how long it takes to perform an evaluation of track in the indicated state. This simulates how long it takes to “think’ or perform an evaluation in a logical sense.

subCommands.name: track_processor
subCommands.description: Specifies the name of a WSF_TRACK_PROCESSOR (typically operating as a non_master_track_processor) whose track list will provide the tracks used in the evaluation process.

subCommands.name: comm_retry_attempts
subCommands.description: Indicates the number of attempts to retry failed communications.

subCommands.name: comm_retry_interval
subCommands.description: Indicates the amount of time between attempts to retry failed communications.

subCommands.name: operating_level
subCommands.description: Indicates the operating condition or state and the associated level.

subCommands.name: time_to_recognize_messages
subCommands.description: Indicates the amount of time it takes to recognize a message.

subCommands.name: track_update_interval
subCommands.description: Indicates the time interval for sending track updates to assignees.

subCommands.name: track_update_strategy
subCommands.description: Indicates how track updates are sent. With default behavior, if a task has been accepted then periodic track updates are sent to the assignee. With the Suppressor behavior, track updates are sent to assignees only when the track manager indicates a track has been updated.

subCommands.name: weapon_uplink_path
subCommands.description: Indicates the sensor and communication device to use when supporting a weapon uplink. If a tracking task is assigned to the sensor and a weapon is fired, the weapon is supported with an uplinked track.

subCommands.name: uplink_source
subCommands.description: Indicates the source of the track when uplinking. If this command is not used, the uplink will be sent any time the track is updated in the track manager. If this command is used, only sensor tracks originating from the uplink source will be used. The sensor must report tracks to the track manager.

subCommands.name: uplink_comm
subCommands.description: Indicates the comm system used to transmit an uplink. If this command is not used, the first compatible comm system will be chosen.

subCommands.name: uplink_delay
subCommands.description: Indicates the delay before an uplink is initiated after an uplink task is received.

subCommands.name: auto_weapon_uplink

subCommands.name: auto_weapon_uplink_platform

name: WSF_TBM_MOVER
description: Specify the type of trajectory to be used to reach the target. This is not used if a target was not specified.

subCommands.name: trajectory_type
subCommands.description: Specify the type of trajectory to be used to reach the target. This is not used if a target was not specified.

subCommands.description: Specify the position of the target. Not used if ignore_target is used. May miss the target if cep or cep_table is used.

subCommands.name: ignore_target
subCommands.description: Indicate that any target position (defined either by target_position or the ‘current target track’) is to be ignored. The orientation of the platform to which the mover is attached defines the initial state.

subCommands.name: show_status
subCommands.description: Display status information at launch time.

subCommands.name: stage
subCommands.description: Define the attributes of the only state of a single stage vehicle or one of the stages in a multistage vehicle. <stage number> must be a value that is greater than or equal to 1 and less than or equal to the current number of defined stages plus one. If the value specifies a stage that already exists then the enclosed subcommands override the values in that stage. If the value is equal to the current number of defined stages plus one then a new stage is created and populated with the enclosed subcommands. It is invalid to specify a stage number that is more than one higher than the current highest defined stage number.:

subCommands.name: ballistic_coefficient
subCommands.description: The ballistic coefficient. This is a required value and there is no default.

subCommands.name: empty_mass
subCommands.description: Specify the mass of the stage without fuel.

subCommands.name: fuel_mass
subCommands.description: Specify the mass of the fuel on the stage. This, or fuel_mass_fraction, must be specified if a non-zero thrust_duration is specified.

subCommands.name: fuel_mass_fraction
subCommands.description: Specify the fraction (0.0 to 1.0) of the total_mass of the stage that is fuel. This, or fuel_mass, must be specified if a non-zero thrust_duration is specified.

subCommands.name: pre_ignition_coast_time
subCommands.description: Specify the amount of time that will elapse between the start of the stage and when the engine will ignite.

subCommands.name: pre_separation_coast_time

name: WSF_TOWED_MOVER
description: If non-zero, specifies a periodic time interval at which the simulation will call the mover. If zero then the mover will be called only when it is necessary to determine the position of the containing platform.

subCommands.name: update_interval

subCommands.name: tow_length
subCommands.description: Specifies the desired distance between the lead platform and the towed asset.

subCommands.name: reel_out_speed
subCommands.description: Specifies the speed or rate at which the towed asset is reeled out from the lead platform. While being reeled out, the state is set to REELING_OUT. When the desired tow length has been reached, the state is set to DEPLOYED and the distance is maintained.

subCommands.name: reel_in_speed
subCommands.description: Specifies the speed or rate at which the towed asset is to be reeled back onto the lead platform. If not set, the towed asset will be deployed and remain in the simulation until killed or until the lead platform is removed from the simulation.

subCommands.name: reel_in_at_absolute_time
subCommands.description: Defines the absolute simulation time to start reeling the towed asset back onto the lead platform. A reel in rate must be set. Use ‘reel_in_speed’ or a script command to set the reel in rate for the towed asset.

subCommands.name: reel_in_time_after_deployed
subCommands.description: Specifies the speed or rate at which the towed asset is to be reeled back onto the lead platform after the towed asset has been fully deployed.

subCommands.name: restore_quantity
subCommands.description: If set to ‘true’, the quantity remaining for the towed asset is reset to the initial loadout after the towed asset was reeled out, deployed and then reeled back onto the lead platform. This allows for an unlimited number of towed launches.

subCommands.name: follow_lead_trajectory
subCommands.description: If set to ‘true’, the towed asset will follow the lead platform’s trajectory. The towed asset’s state is taken from the lead platform’s state history, with the time offset calculated by dividing the tether length by the lead platform’s speed. If set to ‘false’, the towed asset will follow as though it were rigidly attached, fixed in the lead platform’s entity coordinate system for a given deployed tether length and desired relative geometry (specified with the azimuth_relative_to_lead and elevation_relative_to_lead commands.

subCommands.name: elevation_relative_to_lead
subCommands.description: Towed asset elevation with respect to the lead platform. Value must be in range [-90 deg, 90 deg], with positive elevation corresponding to -Z direction of the lead platform’s entity coordinate system.

subCommands.description: Specifies that track histories should be kept for the given time interval. This option is valid only if retain_track_history is set in the associated track manager.

subCommands.description: Report tracks (raw or fused depending on the following inputs) at the given interval. Each track in the respective track lists will be sent to externally connected entities once per report interval.

subCommands.description: All tracks are reported to externally connected entities at the beginning of the reporting interval. New tracks will be reported immediately.

subCommands.name: relocate_and_rotate
subCommands.description: The relocate_and_rotate … end_relocate_and_rotate block is a means to move a trajectory from one locale to another, including a change in orientation. Two keywords will move a TSPI trajectory from one (latitude, longitude) to another (latitude, longitude), either: A) initial_endpoint_anchor <lat> <lon>, or B) terminal_endpoint_anchor <lat> <lon>. After the path is relocated, it can them be re-oriented. To do so, use either A) great_circle_heading_at_anchor_point <angle-value>, or B) align_to_great_circle_through <lat> <lon>. In the later case, the <lat> <lon> value must be different than the anchor point. Note that due to the spherical geometry calculations used, and the ellipsoidal earth, the path translation process will be approximate. Also note that the initial or terminal heading value to be specified is along a great circle arc between initial and final trajectory points, not necessarily the true heading being flown at the beginning or end of trajectory.

subCommands.name: gross_update_interval
subCommands.description: Update interval for the fuse processor, when not in proximity to any platforms of interest. (The update interval may be temporarily reduced internally when close to target platforms of interest.)

subCommands.name: fine_update_interval
subCommands.description: Update interval for the fuse processor, when considered to be in proximity to a platform of interest. This value must be smaller than update_interval, and is used to increase the resolution and accuracy of a proximity pass to a target of interest. Appropriate values for this parameter will depend upon closing speed of the weapon. As a rough guide, allow that one fine_update_interval should elapse during the time the weapon traverses the lethal radius of the weapon.

subCommands.name: time_of_flight_to_arm
subCommands.description: Do not consider detonating before the specified time of flight elapses. This value is relative to when the weapon first leaves the “rail” or “pad”. This will allow a safe launch separation before arming the weapon for detonation. If a detonation is commanded (by various means) before the weapon is armed, the weapon will be removed from the simulation with no damaging effect upon any platform.

subCommands.name: max_time_of_flight_to_detonate
subCommands.description: Automatically detonate when the specified time of flight elapses. This value is relative to when the weapon first leaves the “rail” or “pad.” This will prevent a weapon that misses a proximity hit from flying forever.

subCommands.name: detonate_below_height_msl
subCommands.description: As the weapon is descending, detonate upon crossing below the specified AGL or MSL altitude.

subCommands.name: detonate_above_height_msl
subCommands.description: As the weapon is ascending, detonate upon crossing above the specified AGL or MSL altitude.

subCommands.name: detonate_below_mach
subCommands.description: As the weapon is descending and the speed is decreasing, detonate if the speed or Mach number falls below the specified value.

subCommands.name: detonate_on_mach_decreasing_to
subCommands.description: As the weapon accelerates, the peak Mach number is stored. After burnout, when decelerating, detonate if the Mach number falls below the specified value. Detonation is triggered _only_ after a peak Mach greater than the specified value is attained.

subCommands.name: gross_proximity_range
subCommands.description: This value must be specified for weapon-target proximity checks to occur. This input specifies the minimum separation distance in which the weapon is considered close to the target. During the time when a weapon is with this range of a target of interest, finer resolution time steps (see fine_update_interval) will be used to improve the accuracy of intercept determination for the weapon.

subCommands.name: hit_proximity_range
subCommands.description: If proximity checks are enabled (gross_proximity_range non-zero) and do_not_use_current_target is specified, this indicates the maximum range between the weapon and target’s point of closest approach in which a detonation will be triggered. If the weapon and target do not pass within this distance at their point of closest approach then the platforms will continue on without a detonation.

subCommands.name: fuse_function_range
subCommands.description: If non-zero, point-of-closest-approach (PCA) calculations are prematurely terminated (the fuse actions) when just inside this specified standoff range. Default is zero, which causes fusing to occur at PCA. Some small standoff is recommended when a PkTable is used, because the un-modified PCA fusing will almost always result in Azimuth and Elevation values at PCA greater than 90 degrees.

subCommands.name: do_not_use_current_target

subCommands.name: proximity_all_on_loss_of_target
subCommands.description: The inputs each specify what to do if use_current_target or exclusive_target_name is enabled, and then an existing target is lost. The options (respectively) are to:

subCommands.name: excluded_category
subCommands.description: For use only when proximity to all platforms is being considered. This input will exclude consideration of all platforms belonging to <category-name>. This command can be specified multiple times to exclude multiple categories from consideration.

subCommands.name: air_to_ground_mode
subCommands.description: This flag will raise the intercept value for an AGL limit by the height of a specified target type (either the current target or the specified exclusive_target_name). This is done to permit the weapon to detonate as close as possible to the center of gravity of the intended target, without artificially increasing miss distance by the vertical height of a ground target.

subCommands.name: on_intercept
subCommands.description: This setting allows a weapon platform to freeze and remain in the simulation after the fuse has computed an intercept condition. Normally the platform will be detonated and deleted upon intercept. If set to “halt”, then motion will freeze at the intercept location, and the fuse-controlled engagement object will be interrupted. It will be up to scripting, or some other mechanism, to Terminate() the engagement, which will then remove the weapon platform from the simulation.

subCommands.description: As the weapon is descending and the speed is decreasing, detonate if the speed or Mach number falls below the specified value.

subCommands.name: detonate_on_mach_decreasing_to
subCommands.description: As the weapon accelerates, the peak Mach number is stored. After burnout, when decelerating, detonate if the Mach number falls below the specified value. Detonation is triggered _only_ after a peak Mach greater than the specified value is attained.

subCommands.name: gross_proximity_range
subCommands.description: This value must be specified for weapon-target proximity checks to occur. This input specifies the minimum separation distance in which the weapon is considered close to the target. During the time when a weapon is with this range of a target of interest, finer resolution time steps (see fine_update_interval) will be used to improve the accuracy of intercept determination for the weapon.

subCommands.name: hit_proximity_range
subCommands.description: If proximity checks are enabled (gross_proximity_range non-zero) and do_not_use_current_target is specified, this indicates the maximum range between the weapon and target’s point of closest approach in which a detonation will be triggered. If the weapon and target do not pass within this distance at their point of closest approach then the platforms will continue on without a detonation.

subCommands.name: fuse_function_range
subCommands.description: If non-zero, point-of-closest-approach (PCA) calculations are prematurely terminated (the fuse actions) when just inside this specified standoff range. Default is zero, which causes fusing to occur at PCA. Some small standoff is recommended when a PkTable is used, because the un-modified PCA fusing will almost always result in Azimuth and Elevation values at PCA greater than 90 degrees.

subCommands.name: do_not_use_current_target
subCommands.description: If proximity checks are enabled (gross_proximity_range non-zero), this specifies against which platforms proximity checks will occur. The options are, respectively:

subCommands.name: proximity_all_on_loss_of_target
subCommands.description: The inputs each specify what to do if use_current_target or exclusive_target_name is enabled, and then an existing target is lost. The options (respectively) are to:

subCommands.name: excluded_category
subCommands.description: For use only when proximity to all platforms is being considered. This input will exclude consideration of all platforms belonging to <category-name>. This command can be specified multiple times to exclude multiple categories from consideration.

subCommands.name: air_to_ground_mode
subCommands.description: This flag will raise the intercept value for an AGL limit by the height of a specified target type (either the current target or the specified exclusive_target_name). This is done to permit the weapon to detonate as close as possible to the center of gravity of the intended target, without artificially increasing miss distance by the vertical height of a ground target.

subCommands.name: on_intercept
subCommands.description: This setting allows a weapon platform to freeze and remain in the simulation after the fuse has computed an intercept condition. Normally the platform will be detonated and deleted upon intercept. If set to “halt”, then motion will freeze at the intercept location, and the fuse-controlled engagement object will be interrupted. It will be up to scripting, or some other mechanism, to Terminate() the engagement, which will then remove the weapon platform from the simulation.

subCommands.name: script
subCommands.description: This script is executed when the fuse is just about to detonate but prior to the assessment of weapon lethality. The weapon engagement object (available through PLATFORM.WeaponEngagement()) has been populated with the detonation reason and location.

subCommands.name: port
subCommands.description: This is the only command required to set up the weapon server as a host that listens for “RELEASE_STORE” commands, fires, and manages weapon fly-outs. The weapon server will listen for connections on the given port, and a theoretically infinite number of clients can connect and request weapon fires. It is important to note that the weapon server will only be able to handle requests for weapon types that it knows about, so any weapon types referenced in the received RELEASE_STORE commands should already be defined in the WSF input files that mission loads.

subCommands.name: outgoing_weapon_server
subCommands.description: If this command is used then mission will act as regular, but will send off “RELEASE_STORE” commands to an external weapon server specified by the given host and port. It will only send off such fire requests for weapon types that are specified with the “outgoing_weapon_type” command. See below.

subCommands.name: outgoing_weapon_type

This approach allows the user to map a track number (decimal value) to a DisEntityId of an external platform using the keyword ‘tn_to_disid’.

subCommands.name: coast_time
subCommands.description: The amount of time the weapon will remain active without receiving a track update. When the coast time is reached, the weapon engagement is terminated. See also uplink_required.

subCommands.name: switch_time
subCommands.description: Specifies a time to intercept when the processor switches to terminal guidance.

subCommands.name: switch_range
subCommands.description: Specifies a range to intercept that, when reached, switches the processor to terminal guidance.

subCommands.name: ignore_uplink_target_change
subCommands.description: Forces the processor to ignore track messages that do not pertain to the current target.

subCommands.name: uplink_required
subCommands.description: Specifies if uplinked (external) track updates are required. This is used in conjunction with coast_time to decide which track sources are to be used for deciding if the coast time has been exceeded. If ‘true’, then only the time of the last received uplink is used. If ‘false’ then the maximum time of the last uplink received and the last local sensor track received is used. A value of ‘true’ would be appropriate for a command-guided weapon, with or without a terminal seeker. A value of ‘false’ would be appropriate for a track-via-missile system.

subCommands.description: When true, the weapons manager will conduct engagements against target tracks derived from an EW radar.

subCommands.name: ttr_targets

subCommands.name: engage_local_ttr_targets_only
subCommands.description: When true, the weapons manager will conduct engagements only against targets derived from a local TTR.

subCommands.name: track_quality
subCommands.description: The weapons manager will conduct engagements only against tracks with a quality meeting or exceeding the value specified.

subCommands.name: time_between_engagements
subCommands.description: The delay between assignment engagements. For example, if the weapons manager has two different assignments and both need to be engaged at the current time, when one will be engaged, this delay will take place, then the next will be engaged. Meant to serve as a way to prevent simultaneous assignment engagements.

subCommands.name: expected_sensor_acquisition
subCommands.description: The delay associated with expected sensor acquisition time. This delay allows battle managers to adjust assignment time sufficiently to optimize engagement shot timelines. Assignments will be assessed and created early by an amount of time equal to this delay, which allows the IADS to acquire tracks of sufficient quality to engage targets according to an optimized timeline.

subCommands.name: assess_engage_via
subCommands.description: Collision-Intercept-PT-Inside-Zone assesses engagements by evaluating if the AI can intercept the target within a FEZ, if any. Munition-Intercept-PT assesses engagements by evaluating if an AI’s weapon can currently intercept the target; Inside-Zone requires the target be inside a FEZ, if any, whereas Ignore-Zone does not use zones.

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: When set, logs debugging information.

subCommands.name: home_base_position
subCommands.description: Establishes the latitude and longitude of the AI’s home base, which may be used if the AI egresses.

subCommands.name: intercept_speed
subCommands.description: Intercept speed is the speed at which the AI will move as it attempts to intercept a track.

subCommands.name: my_place_in_formation
subCommands.description: When taking action, an AI’s place in formation determines which action to perform and for which duration. For details, see the documentation for take_action above.

subCommands.name: pursuit_range
subCommands.description: If an AI is beginning to engage a track, and the track is within the AI’s pursuit range, the AI will pursue the track rather than intercepting it. If the AI is currently intercepting a track and comes close enough that the track falls within the pursuit range, the AI will stop intercepting and begin pursuing.

subCommands.name: disable
subCommands.description: When enabled, the Weapons Manager AI will assess whether to “take action” in the form of presentation versus the target while intercepting or pursuing a track.

subCommands.name: action_distance
subCommands.description: When evaluating whether to take action, the Weapons Manager AI will only perform an action behavior if it is within action_distance of the threat.

subCommands.name: ai_action_1
subCommands.description: Default: Break-Left

subCommands.name: duration_1
subCommands.description: Default: 3 seconds

subCommands.name: ai_action_2
subCommands.description: Default: Break-Right

subCommands.name: duration_2
subCommands.description: Default: 3 seconds

subCommands.name: ai_action_3
subCommands.description: Default: Straight

subCommands.name: duration_3
subCommands.description: Default: 0 seconds

subCommands.name: ai_action_4
subCommands.description: Default: Straight

subCommands.name: duration_4
subCommands.description: Default: 10 seconds

subCommands.name: disable
subCommands.description: When enabled, the Weapons Manager AI will attempt to detect and evade threats.

subCommands.name: beam_duration
subCommands.description: The Weapons Manager AI begins to evade a threat with a “beam response” (moving along a vector that’s 90 degrees left or right of the threat’s velocity on a horizontal plane). If the Weapons Manager AI determines that the threat has not been evaded once the beam time has elapsed, it may decide to continue evading using a “drag response” (flying away from the threat at the highest possible speed). The beam_duration determines how long the Weapons Manager AI will execute a beam response before considering a drag response.

subCommands.name: sam_response_range
subCommands.description: If a threat has a spatial domain of land or surface, the Weapons Manager AI will consider evasion responses relative to the threat only if the threat is within the SAM response range. If a threat has a spatial domain of subsurface, the Weapons Manager AI will also default to using the SAM response range, and an error message will be logged stating that evasion behaviors have not been properly implemented for the domain.

subCommands.name: ai_response_range
subCommands.description: If a threat has a spatial domain of air, the Weapons Manager AI will consider evasion responses relative to the threat only if the threat is within the AI response range. For threats with a spatial domain of space or with an unknown spatial domain, the Weapons Manager AI will also default to using the AI response range, and an error message will be logged stating that evasion behaviors have not been properly implemented for the domain.

subCommands.name: restore_after_break_lock
subCommands.description: The Weapons Manager AI will conclude that the platform has succesfully broken a lock by a threat that it is evading if the RWR has not received any updates corresponding to the threat for a certain amount of time. The value set by restore_after_break_lock establishes the time that must elapse after the most recent update before a lock will be considered broken.

subCommands.name: priority
subCommands.description: Even if the RWR senses that multiple threats are within range, the Weapons Manager AI will only evalulate whether to perform evasion behaviors relative to one threat per time step. The “priority” command allows the user to select the criteria for choosing which threat to prioritize when deciding whether to evade. “Default” simply chooses the threat that appears first in the RWR’s active track list; this method is most similar to HELIOS, but it can lead to surprising results, such as attempting to evade a threat that is barely within the response range while ignoring a much closer threat. “Choose-Closest-Threat” evaluates evasion behaviors relative to the threat that is closest to the platform.

subCommands.name: alert_time
subCommands.description: For a parked AI, alert time represents the amount of time it takes before the AI is ready to scramble.

subCommands.name: assess_engage_via
subCommands.description: Collision-Intercept-PT-Inside-Zone assesses engagements by evaluating if the AI can intercept the target within a FEZ, if any. Munition-Intercept-PT assesses engagements by evaluating if an AI’s weapon can currently intercept the target; Inside-Zone requires the target be inside a FEZ, if any, whereas Ignore-Zone does not use zones.

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: When set, logs debugging information.

subCommands.name: home_base_position
subCommands.description: Establishes the latitude and longitude of the AI’s home base, which may be used if the AI egresses.

subCommands.name: intercept_speed
subCommands.description: Intercept speed is the speed at which the AI will move as it attempts to intercept a track.

subCommands.name: my_place_in_formation
subCommands.description: When taking action, an AI’s place in formation determines which action to perform and for which duration. For details, see the documentation for take_action above.

subCommands.name: pursuit_range
subCommands.description: If an AI is beginning to engage a track, and the track is within the AI’s pursuit range, the AI will pursue the track rather than intercepting it. If the AI is currently intercepting a track and comes close enough that the track falls within the pursuit range, the AI will stop intercepting and begin pursuing.

subCommands.name: disable
subCommands.description: When enabled, the Weapons Manager AI will assess whether to “take action” in the form of presentation versus the target while intercepting or pursuing a track.

subCommands.name: action_distance
subCommands.description: When evaluating whether to take action, the Weapons Manager AI will only perform an action behavior if it is within action_distance of the threat.

subCommands.name: ai_action_1
subCommands.description: Default: Break-Left

subCommands.name: duration_1
subCommands.description: Default: 3 seconds

subCommands.name: ai_action_2
subCommands.description: Default: Break-Right

subCommands.name: duration_2
subCommands.description: Default: 3 seconds

subCommands.name: ai_action_3
subCommands.description: Default: Straight

subCommands.name: duration_3
subCommands.description: Default: 0 seconds

subCommands.name: ai_action_4
subCommands.description: Default: Straight

subCommands.name: duration_4
subCommands.description: Default: 10 seconds

subCommands.name: disable
subCommands.description: When enabled, the Weapons Manager AI will attempt to detect and evade threats.

subCommands.name: beam_duration
subCommands.description: The Weapons Manager AI begins to evade a threat with a “beam response” (moving along a vector that’s 90 degrees left or right of the threat’s velocity on a horizontal plane). If the Weapons Manager AI determines that the threat has not been evaded once the beam time has elapsed, it may decide to continue evading using a “drag response” (flying away from the threat at the highest possible speed). The beam_duration determines how long the Weapons Manager AI will execute a beam response before considering a drag response.

subCommands.name: sam_response_range
subCommands.description: If a threat has a spatial domain of land or surface, the Weapons Manager AI will consider evasion responses relative to the threat only if the threat is within the SAM response range. If a threat has a spatial domain of subsurface, the Weapons Manager AI will also default to using the SAM response range, and an error message will be logged stating that evasion behaviors have not been properly implemented for the domain.

For threats with a spatial domain of space or with an unknown spatial domain, the Weapons Manager AI will also default to using the AI response range, and an error message will be logged stating that evasion behaviors have not been properly implemented for the domain.

subCommands.name: broadcast
subCommands.description: Specifies a broadcast IP address and port that will be used to communicate with other WSF applications.

subCommands.name: multicast
subCommands.description: Specifies a multicast IP address, interface, and port that will be used to communicate with other WSF applications.

subCommands.name: unicast
subCommands.description: Specifies an address to communicate with other WSF applications. A port specification is required directly after the unicast command.

subCommands.name: port
subCommands.description: Specifies the port used for a connection command. Must be used directly after multicast, broadcast, or unicast command.

subCommands.name: receive_port
subCommands.description: Specifies the send and receive ports used for a connection command. Must be used directly after multicast, broadcast, or unicast command. This is an alternative to the port command, and allows different ports for sending and receiving.

subCommands.name: mover_update_timer
subCommands.description: If greater than 0, the interface will generate events to force platforms to update their position at the specified interval. This is useful for event-driven simulations where position updates may occur infrequently due to the lack of interaction between objects.

subCommands.name: entity_position_threshold
subCommands.description: Specify the entity position threshold used for some interfaces.

subCommands.name: entity_orientation_threshold
subCommands.description: Specify the entity orientation threshold used for some interfaces.

subCommands.name: connect_to_simulations
subCommands.description: Specifies that the WSF application should try to connect to other WSF simulations. By default, most simulation applications, like SAGE, will not connect to each other. This command is not required when connecting only to WSF display applications such as trackview.

subCommands.name: application
subCommands.description: Specifies the application’s name as text. The application name communicated between applications primarily for user identification. This value is optional.

subCommands.name: debug
subCommands.description: Enables or suppresses XIO status information printed to the screen.

subCommands.name: auto_dis_mapping
subCommands.description: Enables or disables automatic mapping of DIS entities. Currently this option will only work for pure WSF exercises, and does not support DIS exercises with non-WSF applications. In this mode, platform types of DIS objects are communicated over XIO. The entity_type command is not required in this case.

subCommands.name: no_auto_map_application
subCommands.description: <site>: Site number to which this command applies. Must either be an integer in the range 1-65534, or an asterisk (*).

subCommands.name: maximum_modelled_sensors
subCommands.description: Specifies the maximum number of external sensor modelling request the application is able to handle simultaneously.

subCommands.name: debug_modelled_sensors
subCommands.description: Specifies that external sensors modeled locally will be put in debug mode.

subCommands.name: falling_behind_threshold
subCommands.description: Specifies how far a simulation must fall behind real time before notifying connected simulations.

subCommands.name: send_aux_data_updates
subCommands.description: Enables or suppresses aux_data updates for local platforms.

subCommands.name: minimum_altitude
subCommands.description: Minimum altitude constraint (mean sea level).

subCommands.name: maximum_altitude
subCommands.description: Maximum altitude constraint (mean sea level).

subCommands.name: position
subCommands.description: Statically defines the origin of a relative zone.

subCommands.name: heading
subCommands.description: Used with position to statically specify the orientation of the zone.

subCommands.name: reference_platform
subCommands.description: Defines the pose of a relative global zone using the pose of the specified platform and moves using the ECS reference frame of the platform. Whenever a zone containment check is performed, the pose of the indicated platform is used as that of the zone.

subCommands.name: references
subCommands.description: A reference to another zone. Zones which specify the references command are Reference Zones. The geometry of the referenced zone is copied and properties may be overridden through the use of other valid geometry commands. .. note:: Commands which are unrelated to the inherited geometry should not be used and if used may result in unexpected behavior.

subCommands.name: negative
subCommands.description: Specifies whether the zone is negative or positive. A negative zone has the exact opposite area as would be defined by the zone commands. For example, if a circular zone is specified, negating it would represent the area outside the circle.

subCommands.name: aux_data
subCommands.description: Defines auxiliary data for a zone. See aux_data.

subCommands.name: fill_color
subCommands.description: Defines the fill color for a zone.

subCommands.name: line_color
subCommands.description: Defines the line color for a zone.

subCommands.name: minimum_radius
subCommands.description: Minimum radius constraint.

subCommands.name: maximum_radius
subCommands.description: Maximum radius constraint.

subCommands.name: start_angle
subCommands.description: Defines the angular constraint. The angular region starts at start_angle and proceeds clockwise to stop_angle. An angle of zero degrees points in the direction of the reference heading (North in WCS, entity heading in ECS).

subCommands.name: lateral_axis
subCommands.description: Lateral axis constraint for an elliptically-shaped zone.

subCommands.name: longitudinal_axis
subCommands.description: Longitudinal axis constraint for an elliptically-shaped zone.

subCommands.name: polygonal
subCommands.description: A polygonal zone is defined by a sequence of node points. The following conditions must be observed:

subCommands.name: point
subCommands.description: A single point in the polygonal-shaped zone, specified using the relative x/y input format. The positive X axis points in the direction of the reference heading and the positive Y axis is 90 degrees clockwise.

subCommands.name: polar
subCommands.description: Indicates the point data are provided using bearing-range format (by default the data are assumed to be in relative x/y format).

subCommands.name: point
subCommands.description: A single point in a in the polygonal-shaped zone using the polar input format.

subCommands.name: lat_lon
subCommands.description: Indicates the point data are provided using latitude, longitude format (by default the data are assumed to be in relative x,y format). Zones which specify lat_lon are absolute.

subCommands.name: point
subCommands.description: A single point in the polygonal-shaped zone, specified using the absolute lat_lon input format.

subCommands.name: mgrs
subCommands.description: Indicates the point data are provided in the form of an MGRS location format (by default the data are assumed to be in relative x,y format). Zones which specify mgrs are absolute.

subCommands.name: point
subCommands.description: A single point in the polygonal-shaped zone, specified using the absolute mgrs input format.

subCommands.name: modifier
subCommands.description: Specify attenuation to be applied to comm and sensor device detections. Computed attenuation is proportional to the penetration distance through the zone along detection lines of sight. <category-name> is the name used as a corresponding modifier_category (comm modifier_category and sensor modifier_category). <real-value> is a number between 0.0 and 1.0, representing the attenuation value as a percentage loss per meter within the zone. For example, a modifier value of 0.1 means that 10 meters of penetration will cause 100% attenuation.

subCommands.name: zone
subCommands.description: Create an embedded zone that will act as an inclusion zone for this zone_set.

subCommands.name: exclude_zone
subCommands.description: Create an embedded zone that will act as an exclusion zone for this zone_set.

subCommands.name: use_zone
subCommands.description: Declare that the specified shared zone is to be an inclusion zone for this zone set.

subCommands.name: use_exclude_zone
subCommands.description: Declare that the specified shared zone is to be an exclusion zone for this zone set.

subCommands.name: line_color
subCommands.description: Defines the line color for a zone.

subCommands.name: attenuation_parameters
subCommands.description: Defines the variables necessary to define attenuation to the given zone_set. Zone-based attenuation provides a mechanism to attenuate an RF or optical signal from a communications or sensor device without resorting to complex propagation algorithms. In order to use this capability, the user must first create comm and sensor definitions which include the modifier_category command. Then the user must create one or more zone_sets which define the attenuation to be applied for signals that pass through the zone.

subCommands.name: file
subCommands.description: Declare shape file (.shp) to be imported to represent this zone_set. <file-name> is the name of the ESRI shapefile. Leave the extension off.

subCommands.name: use_dted
subCommands.description: If included, the vertical offsets defined in the currently loaded DTED file will be used.

subCommands.name: height_parameter
subCommands.description: A parameter in the .dbf file used to define the height of the individual shapes. “” is acceptable input.

subCommands.name: constant_height
subCommands.description: A constant height to use for all shapes. height_parameter overrides this value.

subCommands.name: base_altitude_parameter
subCommands.description: A parameter in the .dbf file used to define the base altitude of the individual shapes. “” is acceptable input.

subCommands.name: constant_base_altitude
subCommands.description: A constant base altitude to use for all shapes. base_altitude_parameter overrides this value.

subCommands.name: projection
subCommands.description: Define the projection type to be used. Currently geocentric and geodetic are acceptable.

subCommands.name: sensor_modifier
subCommands.description: Declare that this zone_set modifies all sensors with modifier_category <modifier-name> with the attenuation value defined in <modifier-value>

subCommands.name: comm_modifier
subCommands.description: Declare that this zone_set modifies all comm devices with comm <modifier-name> with the attenuation value defined in <modifier-value>
